# Adw – 1: Adaptive Layouts

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-layouts.html

#### Adaptive Layouts

# Adaptive Layouts [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-layouts.html\#adaptive-layouts "Permanent link")

Libadwaita provides a number of widgets that change their layout based on the
available space. This can be used to make applications adapt their UI between
desktop and mobile devices.

# Clamp [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-layouts.html\#clamp "Permanent link")

[`AdwClamp`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Clamp.html) has one child and constrains its maximum size while still
allowing it to shrink. In other words, it allows the child to have padding when
there’s enough space, and to remove them otherwise.

This is commonly used for patterns such as [boxed lists](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/boxed-lists.html):

![adaptive-boxed-lists-wide](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-boxed-lists-wide.png)![adaptive-boxed-lists-narrow](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-boxed-lists-narrow.png)

```
<object class="AdwClamp">
  <property name="child">
    <object class="GtkBox">
      <property name="orientation">vertical</property>
      <property name="margin-top">24</property>
      <property name="margin-bottom">24</property>
      <property name="margin-start">12</property>
      <property name="margin-end">12</property>
      <property name="spacing">24</property>
      <child>
        <object class="GtkListBox">
          <property name="selection-mode">none</property>
          <style>
            <class name="boxed-list"/>
          </style>
          <!-- rows -->
        </object>
      </child>
      <!-- more lists -->
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

See also: [`AdwClampLayout`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ClampLayout.html), [`AdwClampScrollable`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ClampScrollable.html).

# Wrap Box [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-layouts.html\#wrap-box "Permanent link")

[`AdwWrapBox`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.WrapBox.html) is similar to [`GtkBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Box.html), but can wrap lines when the
widgets cannot fit otherwise. Unlike [`GtkFlowBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.FlowBox.html), the children aren’t
arranged into a grid and behave like words in a wrapping label.

![adaptive-tags-wide](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-tags-wide.png)![adaptive-tags-narrow](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-tags-narrow.png)

```
<object class="AdwWrapBox">
  <property name="line-spacing">6</property>
  <property name="child-spacing">6</property>
  <!-- children -->
</object>
```

Copy

See also: [`AdwWrapLayout`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.WrapLayout.html).

# Dialogs [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-layouts.html\#dialogs "Permanent link")

[`AdwDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Dialog.html) is an adaptive dialog container. It can be presented as a
centered floating window or a bottom sheet, depending on the size of its parent window.

![dialog-floating](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/dialog-floating.png)![dialog-bottom](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/dialog-bottom.png)

To use `AdwDialog`, your window must be [`AdwWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Window.html) or
[`AdwApplicationWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ApplicationWindow.html).

# Breakpoints [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-layouts.html\#breakpoints "Permanent link")

[`AdwBreakpoint`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Breakpoint.html) allows applications to restructure UI in arbitrary ways
depending on available size. Breakpoints can be used with [`AdwWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Window.html),
[`AdwApplicationWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ApplicationWindow.html), [`AdwDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Dialog.html) or [`AdwBreakpointBin`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.BreakpointBin.html).

When using breakpoints, the widget containing them will have no minimum size,
and the application must manually set the [`GtkWidget:width-request`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Widget.width-request.html)
and [`GtkWidget:height-request`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Widget.height-request.html) properties, indicating the smallest
supported size.

All of the examples below use breakpoints.

# View Switcher [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-layouts.html\#view-switcher "Permanent link")

The [`AdwViewSwitcher`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcher.html) and [`AdwViewSwitcherBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherBar.html) widgets implement an
adaptive [view switcher](https://developer.gnome.org/hig/patterns/nav/view-switchers.html).

They are typically used together, providing desktop and mobile UI for the same
navigation: a view switcher in the header bar when there’s enough space, or a
view switcher in a bottom bar otherwise. An [`AdwBreakpoint`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Breakpoint.html) is used to
switch between them depending on available width.

![adaptive-view-switcher-wide](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-view-switcher-wide.png)![adaptive-view-switcher-narrow](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-view-switcher-narrow.png)

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <child>
    <object class="AdwBreakpoint">
      <condition>max-width: 550sp</condition>
      <setter object="switcher_bar" property="reveal">True</setter>
      <setter object="header_bar" property="title-widget"/>
    </object>
  </child>
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwToolbarView">
      <child type="top">
        <object class="AdwHeaderBar" id="header_bar">
          <property name="title-widget">
            <object class="AdwViewSwitcher">
              <property name="stack">stack</property>
              <property name="policy">wide</property>
            </object>
          </property>
        </object>
      </child>
      <property name="content">
        <object class="AdwViewStack" id="stack"/>
      </property>
      <child type="bottom">
        <object class="AdwViewSwitcherBar" id="switcher_bar">
          <property name="stack">stack</property>
        </object>
      </child>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

You may need to adjust the breakpoint threshold depending on the number of
pages in your application, as well as their titles.

# Split Views [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-layouts.html\#split-views "Permanent link")

Libadwaita provides two containers for creating multi-pane layouts that can
collapse on small widths: [`AdwNavigationSplitView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationSplitView.html) and
[`AdwOverlaySplitView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.OverlaySplitView.html).

Both widgets have two children: sidebar and content. They are typically used
together with a [`AdwBreakpoint`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Breakpoint.html) toggling their `collapsed` property for
narrow widths.

They look identical at large widths, only differing when collapsed.

They are commonly used for implement [sidebar](https://developer.gnome.org/hig/patterns/nav/sidebars.html)
and [utility pane](https://developer.gnome.org/hig/patterns/containers/utility-panes.html) patterns.

Split views are commonly used with [`AdwSidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Sidebar.html) or
[`AdwViewSwitcherSidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherSidebar.html).

## Navigation Sidebars [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-layouts.html\#navigation-sidebars "Permanent link")

`AdwNavigationSplitView` turns into an [`AdwNavigationView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationView.html) when collapsed,
containing the sidebar as the root page and content as its subpage. Only
[`AdwNavigationPage`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationPage.html) can be used for both the sidebar and content.

[`AdwSidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Sidebar.html) and [`AdwViewSwitcherSidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherSidebar.html) can turn into boxed list pages.
This should be done at the same time as collapsing the split view.

![adaptive-navigation-sidebar-wide](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-navigation-sidebar-wide.png)![adaptive-navigation-sidebar-narrow-1](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-navigation-sidebar-narrow-1.png)![adaptive-navigation-sidebar-narrow-2](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-navigation-sidebar-narrow-2.png)

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <child>
    <object class="AdwBreakpoint">
      <condition>max-width: 400sp</condition>
      <setter object="split_view" property="collapsed">True</setter>
      <setter object="sidebar" property="mode">page</setter>
    </object>
  </child>
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwNavigationSplitView" id="split_view">
      <property name="sidebar">
        <object class="AdwNavigationPage">
          <property name="title" translatable="yes">Sidebar</property>
          <property name="tag">sidebar</property>
          <property name="child">
            <object class="AdwToolbarView">
              <child type="top">
                <object class="AdwHeaderBar">
                  <child type="end">
                    <object class="GtkMenuButton">
                      <property name="icon-name">open-menu-symbolic</property>
                      <property name="primary">True</property>
                      <!-- specify the menu model -->
                    </object>
                  </child>
                </object>
              </child>
              <property name="content">
                <object class="AdwSidebar" id="sidebar">
                  <signal name="activated" handler="sidebar_activated_cb" swapped="yes"/>
                  <!-- sidebar contents -->
                </object>
              </property>
            </object>
          </property>
        </object>
      </property>
      <property name="content">
        <object class="AdwNavigationPage">
          <property name="title" translatable="yes">Content</property>
          <property name="tag">content</property>
          <property name="child">
            <object class="AdwToolbarView">
              <child type="top">
                <object class="AdwHeaderBar"/>
              </child>
              <property name="content">
                <!-- content -->
              </property>
            </object>
          </property>
        </object>
      </property>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

Switch to the content pane when the sidebar is activated:

```
static void
sidebar_activated_cb (MyObject *self)
{
  adw_navigation_split_view_set_show_content (self->split_view, TRUE);
}
```

Copy

`AdwHeaderBar` will automatically provide a back button, manage window controls
and display the title from its `AdwNavigationPage`.

## Overlay Sidebars [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-layouts.html\#overlay-sidebars "Permanent link")

`AdwOverlaySplitView` shows the sidebar as an overlay above the content when collapsed.

[`AdwSidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Sidebar.html) and [`AdwViewSwitcherSidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherSidebar.html) should be kept in sidebar mode
in this case.

To move the menu button from the sidebar to content when the split view is
collapsed, add a menu button to each pane, hide one of them and toggle their
visibility from your breakpoint.

![adaptive-overlay-sidebar-wide](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-overlay-sidebar-wide.png)![adaptive-overlay-sidebar-narrow-1](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-overlay-sidebar-narrow-1.png)![adaptive-overlay-sidebar-narrow-2](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-overlay-sidebar-narrow-2.png)

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <child>
    <object class="AdwBreakpoint">
      <condition>max-width: 400sp</condition>
      <setter object="split_view" property="collapsed">True</setter>
      <setter object="show_sidebar_button" property="visible">True</setter>
      <setter object="sidebar_menu_button" property="visible">False</setter>
      <setter object="content_menu_button" property="visible">True</setter>
    </object>
  </child>
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwOverlaySplitView" id="split_view">
      <property name="sidebar">
        <object class="AdwToolbarView">
          <child type="top">
            <object class="AdwHeaderBar">
              <property name="title-widget">
                <object class="AdwWindowTitle">
                  <property name="title">Sidebar</property>
                  <child type="end">
                    <object class="GtkMenuButton" id="sidebar_menu_button">
                      <property name="icon-name">open-menu-symbolic</property>
                      <property name="primary">True</property>
                      <!-- specify the menu model -->
                    </object>
                  </child>
                </object>
              </property>
            </object>
          </child>
          <property name="content">
            <object class="AdwSidebar" id="sidebar">
              <signal name="activated" handler="sidebar_activated_cb" swapped="yes"/>
              <!-- sidebar contents -->
            </object>
          </property>
        </object>
      </property>
      <property name="content">
        <object class="AdwToolbarView" id="content">
          <child type="top">
            <object class="AdwHeaderBar">
              <property name="title-widget">
                <object class="AdwWindowTitle">
                  <property name="title">Content</property>
                </object>
              </property>
              <child type="start">
                <object class="GtkToggleButton" id="show_sidebar_button">
                  <property name="visible">False</property>
                  <property name="icon-name">adw-sidebar-symbolic</property>
                  <property name="active"
                            bind-source="split_view"
                            bind-property="show-sidebar"
                            bind-flags="sync-create|bidirectional"/>
                </object>
              </child>
              <child type="end">
                <object class="GtkMenuButton" id="content_menu_button">
                  <property name="visible">False</property>
                  <property name="icon-name">open-menu-symbolic</property>
                  <property name="primary">True</property>
                  <!-- specify the menu model -->
                </object>
              </child>
            </object>
          </child>
          <property name="content">
            <!-- content -->
          </property>
        </object>
      </property>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

If the split view is collapsed, hide the sidebar pane when the sidebar is activated:

```
static void
sidebar_activated_cb (MyObject *self)
{
  if (adw_overlay_split_view_get_collapsed (self->split_view)
    adw_overlay_split_view_set_show_sidebar (self->split_view, FALSE);
}
```

Copy

## Utility Panes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-layouts.html\#utility-panes "Permanent link")

Utility panes are constructed similarly to overlay sidebars, but they share a
single header bar and a single [`AdwToolbarView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToolbarView.html), while the split view goes
into the content child of the `AdwToolbarView`.

![adaptive-utility-pane-wide](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-utility-pane-wide.png)![adaptive-utility-pane-narrow-1](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-utility-pane-narrow-1.png)![adaptive-utility-pane-narrow-2](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-utility-pane-narrow-2.png)

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <child>
    <object class="AdwBreakpoint">
      <condition>max-width: 400sp</condition>
      <setter object="split_view" property="collapsed">True</setter>
    </object>
  </child>
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwToolbarView">
      <property name="top-bar-style">raised</property>
      <child type="top">
        <object class="AdwHeaderBar">
          <child type="start">
            <object class="GtkToggleButton" id="show_sidebar_button">
              <property name="icon-name">sidebar-show-symbolic</property>
              <property name="active">True</property>
            </object>
          </child>
        </object>
      </child>
      <property name="content">
        <object class="AdwOverlaySplitView" id="split_view">
          <property name="show-sidebar"
                    bind-source="show_sidebar_button"
                    bind-property="active"
                    bind-flags="sync-create|bidirectional"/>
          <property name="sidebar">
            <!-- utility pane -->
          </property>
          <property name="content">
            <!-- main view -->
          </property>
        </object>
      </property>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

## Triple Pane Layouts [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-layouts.html\#triple-pane-layouts "Permanent link")

Both split views can be used for creating triple pane layouts, via nesting two
of the views within one another. The inner view can be placed as the sidebar or
content widget in the outer view, depending on how you want to handle collapsing.

An example of a triple-pane layout with the an `AdwNavigationSplitView` nested
within another `AdwNavigationSplitView`‘s sidebar:

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <child>
    <object class="AdwBreakpoint">
      <condition>max-width: 860sp</condition>
      <setter object="outer_view" property="collapsed">True</setter>
      <setter object="inner_view" property="sidebar-width-fraction">0.33</setter>
    </object>
  </child>
  <child>
    <object class="AdwBreakpoint">
      <condition>max-width: 500sp</condition>
      <setter object="outer_view" property="collapsed">True</setter>
      <setter object="inner_view" property="sidebar-width-fraction">0.33</setter>
      <setter object="inner_view" property="collapsed">True</setter>
    </object>
  </child>
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwNavigationSplitView" id="outer_view">
      <property name="min-sidebar-width">470</property>
      <property name="max-sidebar-width">780</property>
      <property name="sidebar-width-fraction">0.47</property>
      <property name="sidebar">
        <object class="AdwNavigationPage">
          <property name="child">
            <object class="AdwNavigationSplitView" id="inner_view">
              <property name="max-sidebar-width">260</property>
              <property name="sidebar-width-fraction">0.38</property>
              <property name="sidebar">
                <!-- sidebar -->
              </property>
              <property name="content">
                <!-- middle pane -->
              </property>
            </object>
          </property>
        </object>
      </property>
      <property name="content">
        <!-- content -->
      </property>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

![adaptive-triple-pane-wide](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-triple-pane-wide.png)![adaptive-triple-pane-medium](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-triple-pane-medium.png)![adaptive-triple-pane-narrow-3](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-triple-pane-narrow-3.png)![adaptive-triple-pane-narrow-1](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-triple-pane-narrow-1.png)![adaptive-triple-pane-narrow-2](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-triple-pane-narrow-2.png)

When only the outer split view is collapsed, either the content is visible or
the sidebar and middle pane are visible. When both split views are collapsed,
only one pane is visible at a time.

An example of a triple-pane layout with the an `AdwNavigationSplitView` nested
within an `AdwOverlaySplitView`‘s content:

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <child>
    <object class="AdwBreakpoint">
      <condition>max-width: 860sp</condition>
      <setter object="outer_view" property="collapsed">True</setter>
    </object>
  </child>
  <child>
    <object class="AdwBreakpoint">
      <condition>max-width: 500sp</condition>
      <setter object="outer_view" property="collapsed">True</setter>
      <setter object="inner_view" property="collapsed">True</setter>
    </object>
  </child>
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwOverlaySplitView" id="outer_view">
      <property name="max-sidebar-width">260</property>
      <property name="sidebar-width-fraction">0.179</property>
      <property name="sidebar">
        <!-- sidebar -->
      </property>
      <property name="content">
        <object class="AdwNavigationSplitView" id="inner_view">
          <property name="min-sidebar-width">290</property>
          <property name="max-sidebar-width">520</property>
          <property name="sidebar-width-fraction">0.355</property>
          <property name="sidebar">
            <!-- middle pane -->
          </property>
          <property name="content">
            <!-- content -->
          </property>
        </object>
      </property>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

When only the outer split view is collapsed the middle pane and content are
visible, and the sidebar can be overlaid above them.

# Tabs [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-layouts.html\#tabs "Permanent link")

[`AdwTabView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabView.html) is a dynamic tab container. It doesn’t have a visible tab
switcher on its own, leaving that to [`AdwTabBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabBar.html), [`AdwTabButton`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabButton.html) and
[`AdwTabOverview`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabOverview.html). When used together with breakpoints, these widgets can
provide an adaptive tabbed interface.

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <child>
    <object class="AdwBreakpoint">
      <condition>max-width: 500px</condition>
      <setter object="overview_btn" property="visible">True</setter>
      <setter object="new_tab_btn" property="visible">False</setter>
      <setter object="tab_bar" property="visible">False</setter>
    </object>
  </child>
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwTabOverview">
      <property name="view">view</property>
      <property name="enable-new-tab">True</property>
      <property name="child">
        <object class="AdwToolbarView">
          <property name="top-bar-style">raised</property>
          <child type="top">
            <object class="AdwHeaderBar">
              <child type="end">
                <object class="AdwTabButton" id="overview_btn">
                  <property name="visible">False</property>
                  <property name="view">view</property>
                  <property name="action-name">overview.open</property>
                </object>
              </child>
              <child type="end">
                <object class="GtkButton" id="new_tab_btn">
                  <property name="icon-name">tab-new-symbolic</property>
                </object>
              </child>
            </object>
          </child>
          <child type="top">
            <object class="AdwTabBar" id="tab_bar">
              <property name="view">view</property>
            </object>
          </child>
          <property name="content">
            <object class="AdwTabView" id="view"/>
          </property>
        </object>
      </property>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

![adaptive-tabs-wide](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-tabs-wide.png)![adaptive-tabs-narrow-1](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-tabs-narrow-1.png)![adaptive-tabs-narrow-2](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-tabs-narrow-2.png)

# Multi-Layout View [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-layouts.html\#multi-layout-view "Permanent link")

[`AdwMultiLayoutView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.MultiLayoutView.html) defines multiple layouts and allows switching between
them. Each layout has slots inside it, and when switching layouts, children are
inserted into slots with matching IDs. Breakpoints can be used for switching the
layout depending on available size.

For example, it can be used to have a sidebar that transforms into a bottom
sheet on narrow sizes, as follows:

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <child>
    <object class="AdwBreakpoint">
      <condition>max-width: 400sp</condition>
      <setter object="multi_layout_view" property="layout-name">bottom-sheet</setter>
    </object>
  </child>
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwMultiLayoutView" id="multi_layout_view">
      <child>
        <object class="AdwLayout">
          <property name="name">sidebar</property>
          <property name="content">
            <object class="AdwOverlaySplitView">
              <property name="sidebar-position">end</property>
              <property name="sidebar">
                <object class="AdwLayoutSlot">
                  <property name="id">secondary</property>
                </object>
              </property>
              <property name="content">
                <object class="AdwLayoutSlot">
                  <property name="id">primary</property>
                </object>
              </property>
            </object>
          </property>
        </object>
      </child>
      <child>
        <object class="AdwLayout">
          <property name="name">bottom-sheet</property>
          <property name="content">
            <object class="AdwBottomSheet">
              <property name="open">True</property>
              <property name="content">
                <object class="AdwLayoutSlot">
                  <property name="id">primary</property>
                </object>
              </property>
              <property name="sheet">
                <object class="AdwLayoutSlot">
                  <property name="id">secondary</property>
                </object>
              </property>
            </object>
          </property>
        </object>
      </child>
      <child type="primary">
        <!-- primary child -->
      </child>
      <child type="secondary">
        <!-- secondary child -->
      </child>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

![adaptive-multi-layout-wide](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-multi-layout-wide.png)![adaptive-multi-layout-narrow](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-multi-layout-narrow.png)

# Adw – 1: Boxed Lists

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/boxed-lists.html

#### Boxed Lists

# Boxed Lists [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/boxed-lists.html\#boxed-lists "Permanent link")

Libadwaita provides API to implement the [boxed lists](https://developer.gnome.org/hig/patterns/containers/boxed-lists.html) pattern.

Boxed lists are composed of a [`GtkListBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListBox.html) with the
[`GtkListBox:selection-mode`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.ListBox.selection-mode.html) set to [`GTK_SELECTION_NONE`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.SelectionMode.html#none) and
with the [`.boxed-list` or `.boxed-list-separate`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#boxed-lists-cards)
style classes.

[`GtkListView`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListView.html) cannot be used as a boxed list at the moment.

An example boxed list:

```
<object class="GtkListBox">
  <property name="selection-mode">none</property>
  <style>
    <class name="boxed-list"/>
  </style>
  <child>
    <object class="AdwActionRow">
      <property name="title">Item 1</property>
    </object>
  </child>
  <child>
    <object class="AdwActionRow">
      <property name="title">Item 2</property>
    </object>
  </child>
  <child>
    <object class="AdwActionRow">
      <property name="title">Item 3</property>
    </object>
  </child>
</object>
```

Copy

![boxed-lists](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/boxed-lists.png)

# Rows [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/boxed-lists.html\#rows "Permanent link")

A number of predefined list row classes are available and intended to be used
inside boxed lists:

## Action Rows [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/boxed-lists.html\#action-rows "Permanent link")

[`AdwActionRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ActionRow.html) is a basic row. It has a title, a subtitle, an icon, and can
have prefix and suffix children.

![action-row](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/action-row.png)

## Switch Rows [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/boxed-lists.html\#switch-rows "Permanent link")

[`AdwSwitchRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SwitchRow.html) is an [`AdwActionRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ActionRow.html) with an embedded [`GtkSwitch`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Switch.html).
It’s used to represent two states: “on” and “off”.

![switch-row](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/switch-row.png)

## Expander Rows [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/boxed-lists.html\#expander-rows "Permanent link")

[`AdwExpanderRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ExpanderRow.html) is similar to [`AdwActionRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ActionRow.html), but can expand to show
other rows.

![expander-row](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/expander-row.png)

## Combo Rows [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/boxed-lists.html\#combo-rows "Permanent link")

[`AdwComboRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ComboRow.html) is a row with an embedded drop down menu, similar to
[`GtkDropDown`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.DropDown.html).

![combo-row](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/combo-row.png)

## Entry Rows [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/boxed-lists.html\#entry-rows "Permanent link")

[`AdwEntryRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.EntryRow.html) is a row with an embedded entry. It can have prefix and suffix
widgets, and an apply button.

![entry-row](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/entry-row.png)

## Password Entry Rows [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/boxed-lists.html\#password-entry-rows "Permanent link")

[`AdwPasswordEntryRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PasswordEntryRow.html) is a variant of [`AdwEntryRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.EntryRow.html) tailored for entering
secrets. It conceals the text and provides a button to show it, along with a
`Caps Lock` indicator.

![password-entry-row](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/password-entry-row.png)

## Spin Rows [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/boxed-lists.html\#spin-rows "Permanent link")

[`AdwSpinRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SpinRow.html) is a [`AdwActionRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ActionRow.html) with an embedded
[`GtkSpinButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.SpinButton.html).

![spin-row](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/spin-row.png)

## Property Rows [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/boxed-lists.html\#property-rows "Permanent link")

When used together with the [`.property`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#property-rows)
style class, [`AdwActionRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ActionRow.html) and [`AdwExpanderRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ExpanderRow.html) deemphasize their title
and emphasize their subtitle instead, which is useful for displaying read-only properties:

```
<object class="AdwActionRow">
  <property name="title" translatable="yes">Property Name</property>
  <property name="subtitle">Value</property>
  <property name="subtitle-selectable">True</property>
  <style>
    <class name="property"/>
  </style>
</object>
```

Copy

![property-row](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property-row.png)

## Button Rows [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/boxed-lists.html\#button-rows "Permanent link")

[`AdwButtonRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ButtonRow.html) is a list row that acts as a button. It can be useful for
presenting actions at the end of a boxed list.

![button-rows](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/button-rows.png)

## Preferences Group [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/boxed-lists.html\#preferences-group "Permanent link")

[`AdwPreferencesGroup`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesGroup.html) provides a boxed list along with a title and a
description. It’s mainly meant to be used as a child of [`AdwPreferencesPage`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesPage.html),
but can also be used separately.

The [`AdwPreferencesGroup:separate-rows`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.PreferencesGroup.separate-rows.html) property can be used to separate
rows in its boxed list.

![preferences-group](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/preferences-group.png)

# Adw – 1: Compiling with Libadwaita

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/build-howto.html

#### Compiling with Libadwaita

# Compiling with Libadwaita [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/build-howto.html\#compiling-with-libadwaita "Permanent link")

If you need to build Libadwaita, get the source from
[here](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/) and see the `README.md` file.

## Using `pkg-config` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/build-howto.html\#using-pkg-config "Permanent link")

Like other GNOME libraries, Libadwaita uses `pkg-config` to provide compiler
options. The package name is `libadwaita-1`.

When using the Meson build system you can declare a dependency like:

```
dependency('libadwaita-1')
```

Copy

The `1` in the package name is the “API version” (indicating “the version of the
Libadwaita API that first appeared in version 1”) and is essentially just part
of the package name.

## Bundling the Library [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/build-howto.html\#bundling-the-library "Permanent link")

### Using Flatpak [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/build-howto.html\#using-flatpak "Permanent link")

If you’re using the GNOMESDK of the version 42 or later, Libadwaita is already
included and there’s no need to do anything.

If you’re using an older version or a different SDK, add the following modules
to your manifest:

```
{
    "name" : "libadwaita",
    "buildsystem" : "meson",
    "config-opts" : [\
        "-Dexamples=false",\
        "-Dtests=false"\
    ],
    "sources" : [\
        {\
            "type" : "git",\
            "url" : "https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita.git",\
            "branch" : "main"\
        }\
    ],
    "modules" : [\
        {\
            "name" : "libsass",\
            "buildsystem" : "meson",\
            "cleanup" : [\
                "*"\
            ],\
            "sources" : [\
                {\
                    "type" : "git",\
                    "url" : "https://github.com/lazka/libsass.git",\
                    "branch" : "meson"\
                }\
            ]\
        },\
        {\
            "name" : "sassc",\
            "buildsystem" : "meson",\
            "cleanup" : [\
                "*"\
            ],\
            "sources" : [\
                {\
                    "type" : "git",\
                    "url" : "https://github.com/lazka/sassc.git",\
                    "branch" : "meson"\
                }\
            ]\
        }\
    ]
}
```

Copy

### Using a Subproject [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/build-howto.html\#using-a-subproject "Permanent link")

If you’re not using Flatpak, Libadwaita can be used as a Meson subproject.
Create a `subprojects/libadwaita.wrap` file with the following contents:

```
[wrap-git]
directory=libadwaita
url=https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita.git
revision=main
depth=1
```

Copy

Add this to your `meson.build`:

```
libadwaita = dependency(
  'libadwaita-1',
  version: '>= 1.0.0',
  fallback: ['libadwaita', 'libadwaita_dep'],
  default_options: [\
    'examples=false',\
    'introspection=disabled',\
    'tests=false',\
    'vapi=false',\
  ]
)
```

Copy

Then the `libadwaita` variable can be used as a dependency.

## Building on macOS [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/build-howto.html\#building-on-macos "Permanent link")

To build on macOS you need to install the build-dependencies first. This can
e.g. be done via [`brew`](https://brew.sh/):

```
brew install pkg-config gtk4 meson gobject-introspection vala
```

Copy

After running the command above, one may now build the library:

```
git clone https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita.git
cd libadwaita
meson setup _build
ninja -C _build
ninja -C _build install
```

Copy

Working with the library on macOS is pretty much the same as on Linux. To link
it, use `pkg-config`:

```
gcc $(pkg-config --cflags --libs gtk4) $(pkg-config --cflags --libs libadwaita-1) main.c -o main
```

Copy

# Next Steps [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/build-howto.html\#next-steps "Permanent link")

Once libadwaita has been compiled and included into your project, it needs to be
initialized. See [Initialization](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/initialization.html).

# Adw.SidebarSectionCreateItemFunc

since: 1.9

```
AdwSidebarItem*

  GObject* item,
  gpointer user_data
)
```

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-sidebar-section.h\#L27 "go to source location")

Called for sidebars that are bound to a [`GListModel`](https://docs.gtk.org/gio/iface.ListModel.html) with
[`adw_sidebar_section_bind_model()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.SidebarSection.bind_model.html) for each
item that gets added to the model.

Available since: 1.9

\[−\]

#### Parameters

`item`

_Type:_ [`GObject`](https://docs.gtk.org/gobject/class.Object.html)

The item from the model for which to create an item for.

|     |
| --- |
| The data is owned by the caller of the function. |

`user_data`

_Type:_`gpointer`

User data.

|     |
| --- |
| The argument can be `NULL`. |
| The data is owned by the caller of the function. |

\[−\]

#### Return value

_Type:_ [`AdwSidebarItem`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SidebarItem.html)

An `AdwSidebarItem` that represents `item`.

|     |
| --- |
| The caller of the function takes ownership of the data, and is responsible for freeing it. |

# Adw.AboutDialog

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AboutDialog.html

since: 1.5

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-about-dialog.c\#L24 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.AboutDialog : Adw.Dialog
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget, Gtk.ShortcutManager {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.5

A dialog showing information about the application.

![about-dialog](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/about-dialog.png)

an about dialog is typically opened when the user activates the `About …`
item in the application’s primary menu. All parts of the dialog are optional.

## Main page [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AboutDialog.html\#main-page "Permanent link")

`AdwAboutDialog` prominently displays the application’s icon, name, developer
name and version. They can be set with the [`AdwAboutDialog:application-icon`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutDialog.application-icon.html),
[`AdwAboutDialog:application-name`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutDialog.application-name.html),
[`AdwAboutDialog:developer-name`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutDialog.developer-name.html) and [`AdwAboutDialog:version`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutDialog.version.html) respectively.

## What's New [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AboutDialog.html\#whats-new "Permanent link")

`AdwAboutDialog` provides a way for applications to display their release
notes, set with the [`AdwAboutDialog:release-notes`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutDialog.release-notes.html) property.

Release notes are formatted the same way as
[AppStream descriptions](https://freedesktop.org/software/appstream/docs/chap-Metadata.html#tag-description).

The supported formatting options are:

- Paragraph (`<p>`)
- Ordered list (`<ol>`), with list items (`<li>`)
- Unordered list (`<ul>`), with list items (`<li>`)

Within paragraphs and list items, emphasis (`<em>`) and inline code
(`<code>`) text styles are supported. The emphasis is rendered in italic,
while inline code is shown in a monospaced font.

Any text outside paragraphs or list items is ignored.

Nested lists are not supported.

Only one version can be shown at a time. By default, the displayed version
number matches [`AdwAboutDialog:version`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutDialog.version.html). Use
[`AdwAboutDialog:release-notes-version`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutDialog.release-notes-version.html) to override it.

## Details [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AboutDialog.html\#details "Permanent link")

The Details page displays the application comments and links.

The comments can be set with the [`AdwAboutDialog:comments`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutDialog.comments.html) property.
Unlike [`GtkAboutDialog:comments`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.AboutDialog.comments.html), this string can be long and
detailed. It can also contain links and Pango markup.

To set the application website, use [`AdwAboutDialog:website`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutDialog.website.html).
To add extra links below the website, use [`adw_about_dialog_add_link()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.AboutDialog.add_link.html).

If the Details page doesn’t have any other content besides website, the
website will be displayed on the main page instead.

## Troubleshooting [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AboutDialog.html\#troubleshooting "Permanent link")

`AdwAboutDialog` displays the following two links on the main page:

- Support Questions, set with the [`AdwAboutDialog:support-url`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutDialog.support-url.html) property,
- Report an Issue, set with the [`AdwAboutDialog:issue-url`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutDialog.issue-url.html) property.

Additionally, applications can provide debugging information. It will be
shown separately on the Troubleshooting page. Use the
[`AdwAboutDialog:debug-info`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutDialog.debug-info.html) property to specify it.

It’s intended to be attached to issue reports when reporting issues against
the application. As such, it cannot contain markup or links.

`AdwAboutDialog` provides a quick way to save debug information to a file.
When saving, [`AdwAboutDialog:debug-info-filename`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutDialog.debug-info-filename.html) would be used as
the suggested filename.

## Credits and Acknowledgements [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AboutDialog.html\#credits-and-acknowledgements "Permanent link")

The Credits page has the following default sections:

- Developers, set with the [`AdwAboutDialog:developers`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutDialog.developers.html) property,
- Designers, set with the [`AdwAboutDialog:designers`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutDialog.designers.html) property,
- Artists, set with the [`AdwAboutDialog:artists`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutDialog.artists.html) property,
- Documenters, set with the [`AdwAboutDialog:documenters`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutDialog.documenters.html) property,
- Translators, set with the [`AdwAboutDialog:translator-credits`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutDialog.translator-credits.html) property.

When setting translator credits, use the strings `"translator-credits"` or
`"translator_credits"` and mark them as translatable.

The default sections that don’t contain any names won’t be displayed.

The Credits page can also contain an arbitrary number of extra sections below
the default ones. Use [`adw_about_dialog_add_credit_section()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.AboutDialog.add_credit_section.html) to add them.

The Acknowledgements page can be used to acknowledge additional people and
organizations for their non-development contributions. Use
[`adw_about_dialog_add_acknowledgement_section()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.AboutDialog.add_acknowledgement_section.html) to add sections to it. For
example, it can be used to list backers in a crowdfunded project or to give
special thanks.

Each of the people or organizations can have an email address or a website
specified. To add a email address, use a string like
`Edgar Allan Poe <edgar@poe.com>`. To specify a website with a title, use a
string like `The GNOME Project https://www.gnome.org`:

![about-dialog-credits](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/about-dialog-credits.png)

## Legal [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AboutDialog.html\#legal "Permanent link")

The Legal page displays the copyright and licensing information for the
application and other modules.

The copyright string is set with the [`AdwAboutDialog:copyright`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutDialog.copyright.html)
property and should be a short string of one or two lines, for example:
`© 2022 Example`.

Licensing information can be quickly set from a list of known licenses with
the [`AdwAboutDialog:license-type`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutDialog.license-type.html) property. If the application’s
license is not in the list, [`AdwAboutDialog:license`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutDialog.license.html) can be used instead.

To add information about other modules, such as application dependencies or
data, use [`adw_about_dialog_add_legal_section()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.AboutDialog.add_legal_section.html).

## Other applications [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AboutDialog.html\#other-applications "Permanent link")

`AdwAboutDialog` can show links to your other apps at the end of the main
page. To add them, use [`adw_about_dialog_add_other_app()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.AboutDialog.add_other_app.html).

By default the other apps section will have “Other Apps by
[`AdwAboutDialog:developer-name`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutDialog.developer-name.html)” as its title. Use
[`AdwAboutDialog:other-apps-title`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutDialog.other-apps-title.html) to override it.

## Constructing [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AboutDialog.html\#constructing "Permanent link")

To make constructing an `AdwAboutDialog` as convenient as possible, you can
use the function [`adw_show_about_dialog()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/func.show_about_dialog.html) which constructs and shows a dialog.

```
static void
show_about (GtkApplication *app)
{
  const char *developers[] = {
    "Angela Avery",
    NULL
  };

  const char *designers[] = {
    "GNOME Design Team",
    NULL
  };

  adw_show_about_dialog (GTK_WIDGET (gtk_application_get_active_window (app)),
                         "application-name", _("Example"),
                         "application-icon", "org.example.App",
                         "version", "1.2.3",
                         "copyright", "© 2022 Angela Avery",
                         "issue-url", "https://gitlab.gnome.org/example/example/-/issues/",
                         "license-type", GTK_LICENSE_GPL_3_0,
                         "developers", developers,
                         "designers", designers,
                         "translator-credits", _("translator-credits"),
                         NULL);
}
```

###### [adw\_dialog\_add\_breakpoint](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Dialog.add_breakpoint.html)

A window showing information about the application.

![about-window](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/about-window.png)

An about window is typically opened when the user activates the `About …`
item in the application’s primary menu. All parts of the window are optional.

## Main page [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AboutWindow.html\#main-page "Permanent link")

`AdwAboutWindow` prominently displays the application’s icon, name, developer
name and version. They can be set with the [`AdwAboutWindow:application-icon`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutWindow.application-icon.html),
[`AdwAboutWindow:application-name`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutWindow.application-name.html),
[`AdwAboutWindow:developer-name`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutWindow.developer-name.html) and [`AdwAboutWindow:version`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutWindow.version.html) respectively.

## What's New [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AboutWindow.html\#whats-new "Permanent link")

`AdwAboutWindow` provides a way for applications to display their release
notes, set with the [`AdwAboutWindow:release-notes`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutWindow.release-notes.html) property.

Release notes are formatted the same way as
[AppStream descriptions](https://freedesktop.org/software/appstream/docs/chap-Metadata.html#tag-description).

The supported formatting options are:

- Paragraph (`<p>`)
- Ordered list (`<ol>`), with list items (`<li>`)
- Unordered list (`<ul>`), with list items (`<li>`)

Within paragraphs and list items, emphasis (`<em>`) and inline code
(`<code>`) text styles are supported. The emphasis is rendered in italic,
while inline code is shown in a monospaced font.

Any text outside paragraphs or list items is ignored.

Nested lists are not supported.

Only one version can be shown at a time. By default, the displayed version
number matches [`AdwAboutWindow:version`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutWindow.version.html). Use
[`AdwAboutWindow:release-notes-version`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutWindow.release-notes-version.html) to override it.

## Details [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AboutWindow.html\#details "Permanent link")

The Details page displays the application comments and links.

The comments can be set with the [`AdwAboutWindow:comments`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutWindow.comments.html) property.
Unlike [`GtkAboutDialog:comments`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.AboutDialog.comments.html), this string can be long and
detailed. It can also contain links and Pango markup.

To set the application website, use [`AdwAboutWindow:website`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutWindow.website.html).
To add extra links below the website, use [`adw_about_window_add_link()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.AboutWindow.add_link.html).

If the Details page doesn’t have any other content besides website, the
website will be displayed on the main page instead.

## Troubleshooting [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AboutWindow.html\#troubleshooting "Permanent link")

`AdwAboutWindow` displays the following two links on the main page:

- Support Questions, set with the [`AdwAboutWindow:support-url`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutWindow.support-url.html) property,
- Report an Issue, set with the [`AdwAboutWindow:issue-url`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutWindow.issue-url.html) property.

Additionally, applications can provide debugging information. It will be
shown separately on the Troubleshooting page. Use the
[`AdwAboutWindow:debug-info`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutWindow.debug-info.html) property to specify it.

It’s intended to be attached to issue reports when reporting issues against
the application. As such, it cannot contain markup or links.

`AdwAboutWindow` provides a quick way to save debug information to a file.
When saving, [`AdwAboutWindow:debug-info-filename`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutWindow.debug-info-filename.html) would be used as
the suggested filename.

## Credits and Acknowledgements [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AboutWindow.html\#credits-and-acknowledgements "Permanent link")

The Credits page has the following default sections:

- Developers, set with the [`AdwAboutWindow:developers`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutWindow.developers.html) property,
- Designers, set with the [`AdwAboutWindow:designers`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutWindow.designers.html) property,
- Artists, set with the [`AdwAboutWindow:artists`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutWindow.artists.html) property,
- Documenters, set with the [`AdwAboutWindow:documenters`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutWindow.documenters.html) property,
- Translators, set with the [`AdwAboutWindow:translator-credits`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutWindow.translator-credits.html) property.

When setting translator credits, use the strings `"translator-credits"` or
`"translator_credits"` and mark them as translatable.

The default sections that don’t contain any names won’t be displayed.

The Credits page can also contain an arbitrary number of extra sections below
the default ones. Use [`adw_about_window_add_credit_section()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.AboutWindow.add_credit_section.html) to add them.

The Acknowledgements page can be used to acknowledge additional people and
organizations for their non-development contributions. Use
[`adw_about_window_add_acknowledgement_section()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.AboutWindow.add_acknowledgement_section.html) to add sections to it. For
example, it can be used to list backers in a crowdfunded project or to give
special thanks.

Each of the people or organizations can have an email address or a website
specified. To add a email address, use a string like
`Edgar Allan Poe <edgar@poe.com>`. To specify a website with a title, use a
string like `The GNOME Project https://www.gnome.org`:

![about-window-credits](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/about-window-credits.png)

## Legal [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AboutWindow.html\#legal "Permanent link")

The Legal page displays the copyright and licensing information for the
application and other modules.

The copyright string is set with the [`AdwAboutWindow:copyright`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutWindow.copyright.html)
property and should be a short string of one or two lines, for example:
`© 2022 Example`.

Licensing information can be quickly set from a list of known licenses with
the [`AdwAboutWindow:license-type`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutWindow.license-type.html) property. If the application’s
license is not in the list, [`AdwAboutWindow:license`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AboutWindow.license.html) can be used instead.

To add information about other modules, such as application dependencies or
data, use [`adw_about_window_add_legal_section()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.AboutWindow.add_legal_section.html).

## Constructing [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AboutWindow.html\#constructing "Permanent link")

To make constructing an `AdwAboutWindow` as convenient as possible, you can
use the function [`adw_show_about_window()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/func.show_about_window.html) which constructs and shows a window.

```
static void
show_about (GtkApplication *app)
{
  const char *developers[] = {
    "Angela Avery",
    NULL
  };

  const char *designers[] = {
    "GNOME Design Team",
    NULL
  };

  adw_show_about_window (gtk_application_get_active_window (app),
                         "application-name", _("Example"),
                         "application-icon", "org.example.App",
                         "version", "1.2.3",
                         "copyright", "© 2022 Angela Avery",
                         "issue-url", "https://gitlab.gnome.org/example/example/-/issues/",
                         "license-type", GTK_LICENSE_GPL_3_0,
                         "developers", developers,
                         "designers", designers,
                         "translator-credits", _("translator-credits"),
                         NULL);
}
```

# Adw.ActionRow

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ActionRow.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-action-row.c\#L13 "go to source location")

```
class Adw.ActionRow : Adw.PreferencesRow
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Actionable, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A [`GtkListBoxRow`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListBoxRow.html) used to present actions.

![action-row](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/action-row.png)

The `AdwActionRow` widget can have a title, a subtitle and an icon. The row
can receive additional widgets at its end, or prefix widgets at its start.

It is convenient to present a preference and its related actions.

`AdwActionRow` is unactivatable by default, giving it an activatable widget
will automatically make it activatable, but unsetting it won’t change the
row’s activatability.

## AdwActionRow as GtkBuildable [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ActionRow.html\#adwactionrow-as-gtkbuildable "Permanent link")

The `AdwActionRow` implementation of the [`GtkBuildable`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/iface.Buildable.html) interface
supports adding a child at its end by specifying “suffix” or omitting the
“type” attribute of a  element.

It also supports adding a child as a prefix widget by specifying “prefix” as
the “type” attribute of a  element.

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ActionRow.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwActionRow` has a main CSS node with name `row`.

It contains the subnode `box.header` for its main horizontal box, and
`box.title` for the vertical box containing the title and subtitle labels.

It contains subnodes `label.title` and `label.subtitle` representing
respectively the title label and subtitle label.

## Style classes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ActionRow.html\#style-classes "Permanent link")

`AdwActionRow` can use the [`.property`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#property-rows)
style class to emphasize the row subtitle instead of the row title, which is
useful for displaying read-only properties.

![property-row](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property-row.png)

When used together with the `.monospace` style class, only the subtitle
becomes monospace, not the title or any extra widgets.

# Adw.AlertDialog

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AlertDialog.html

since: 1.5

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-alert-dialog.c\#L22 "go to source location")

```
class Adw.AlertDialog : Adw.Dialog
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget, Gtk.ShortcutManager {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.5

A dialog presenting a message or a question.

![alert-dialog](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/alert-dialog.png)

Alert dialogs have a heading, a body, an optional child widget, and one or
multiple responses, each presented as a button.

Each response has a unique string ID, and a button label. Additionally, each
response can be enabled or disabled, and can have a suggested or destructive appearance.

When one of the responses is activated, or the dialog is closed, the
[`AdwAlertDialog::response`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.AlertDialog.response.html) signal will be emitted. This signal is
detailed, and the detail, as well as the `response` parameter will be set to
the ID of the activated response, or to the value of the
[`AdwAlertDialog:close-response`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.AlertDialog.close-response.html) property if the dialog had been closed
without activating any of the responses.

Response buttons can be presented horizontally or vertically depending on
available space.

When a response is activated, `AdwAlertDialog` is closed automatically.

An example of using an alert dialog:

```
AdwDialog *dialog;

dialog = adw_alert_dialog_new (_("Replace File?"), NULL);

adw_alert_dialog_format_body (ADW_ALERT_DIALOG (dialog),
                              _("A file named “%s” already exists. Do you want to replace it?"),
                              filename);

adw_alert_dialog_add_responses (ADW_ALERT_DIALOG (dialog),
                                "cancel",  _("_Cancel"),
                                "replace", _("_Replace"),
                                NULL);

adw_alert_dialog_set_response_appearance (ADW_ALERT_DIALOG (dialog),
                                          "replace",
                                          ADW_RESPONSE_DESTRUCTIVE);

adw_alert_dialog_set_default_response (ADW_ALERT_DIALOG (dialog), "cancel");
adw_alert_dialog_set_close_response (ADW_ALERT_DIALOG (dialog), "cancel");

g_signal_connect (dialog, "response", G_CALLBACK (response_cb), self);

adw_dialog_present (dialog, parent);
```

Copy

## Async API [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AlertDialog.html\#async-api "Permanent link")

`AdwAlertDialog` can also be used via the [`adw_alert_dialog_choose()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.AlertDialog.choose.html) method.
This API follows the GIO async pattern, for example:

```
static void
dialog_cb (AdwAlertDialog *dialog,
           GAsyncResult   *result,
           MyWindow       *self)
{
  const char *response = adw_alert_dialog_choose_finish (dialog, result);

  // ...
}

static void
show_dialog (MyWindow *self)
{
  AdwDialog *dialog;

  dialog = adw_alert_dialog_new (_("Replace File?"), NULL);

  adw_alert_dialog_format_body (ADW_ALERT_DIALOG (dialog),
                                _("A file named “%s” already exists. Do you want to replace it?"),
                                filename);

  adw_alert_dialog_add_responses (ADW_ALERT_DIALOG (dialog),
                                  "cancel",  _("_Cancel"),
                                  "replace", _("_Replace"),
                                  NULL);

  adw_alert_dialog_set_response_appearance (ADW_ALERT_DIALOG (dialog),
                                            "replace",
                                            ADW_RESPONSE_DESTRUCTIVE);

  adw_alert_dialog_set_default_response (ADW_ALERT_DIALOG (dialog), "cancel");
  adw_alert_dialog_set_close_response (ADW_ALERT_DIALOG (dialog), "cancel");

  adw_alert_dialog_choose (ADW_ALERT_DIALOG (dialog), GTK_WIDGET (self),
                           NULL, (GAsyncReadyCallback) dialog_cb, self);
}
```

Copy

## AdwAlertDialog as GtkBuildable [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AlertDialog.html\#adwalertdialog-as-gtkbuildable "Permanent link")

`AdwAlertDialog` supports adding responses in UI definitions by via the
`<responses>` element that may contain multiple `<response>` elements, each
representing a response.

Each of the `<response>` elements must have the `id` attribute specifying the
response ID. The contents of the element are used as the response label.

Response labels can be translated with the usual `translatable`, `context`
and `comments` attributes.

The `<response>` elements can also have `enabled` and/or `appearance`
attributes. See [`adw_alert_dialog_set_response_enabled()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.AlertDialog.set_response_enabled.html) and
[`adw_alert_dialog_set_response_appearance()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.AlertDialog.set_response_appearance.html) for details.

Example of an `AdwAlertDialog`UI definition:

```
<object class="AdwAlertDialog" id="dialog">
  <property name="heading" translatable="yes">Save Changes?</property>
  <property name="body" translatable="yes">Open documents contain unsaved changes. Changes which are not saved will be permanently lost.</property>
  <property name="default-response">save</property>
  <property name="close-response">cancel</property>
  <signal name="response" handler="response_cb"/>
  <responses>
    <response id="cancel" translatable="yes">_Cancel</response>
    <response id="discard" translatable="yes" appearance="destructive">_Discard</response>
    <response id="save" translatable="yes" appearance="suggested" enabled="false">_Save</response>
  </responses>
</object>
```

# Adw.Animation

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Animation.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-animation.c\#L16 "go to source location")

```
abstract class Adw.Animation : GObject.Object
{
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A base class for animations.

`AdwAnimation` represents an animation on a widget. It has a target that
provides a value to animate, and a state indicating whether the
animation hasn’t been started yet, is playing, paused or finished.

Currently there are two concrete animation types:
[`AdwTimedAnimation`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TimedAnimation.html) and [`AdwSpringAnimation`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SpringAnimation.html).

`AdwAnimation` will automatically skip the animation if
[`AdwAnimation:widget`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Animation.widget.html) is unmapped, or if
[`GtkSettings:gtk-enable-animations`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Settings.gtk-enable-animations.html) is `FALSE`.

The [`AdwAnimation::done`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.Animation.done.html) signal can be used to perform an action after
the animation ends, for example hiding a widget after animating its
[`GtkWidget:opacity`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Widget.opacity.html) to 0.

`AdwAnimation` will be kept alive while the animation is playing. As such,
it’s safe to create an animation, start it and immediately unref it:
A fire-and-forget animation:

```
static void
animation_cb (double    value,
              MyObject *self)
{
  // Do something with @value
}

static void
my_object_animate (MyObject *self)
{
  AdwAnimationTarget *target =
    adw_callback_animation_target_new ((AdwAnimationTargetFunc) animation_cb,
                                       self, NULL);
  g_autoptr (AdwAnimation) animation =
    adw_timed_animation_new (widget, 0, 1, 250, target);

  adw_animation_play (animation);
}
```

Copy

If there’s a chance the previous animation for the same target hasn’t yet
finished, the previous animation should be stopped first, or the existing
`AdwAnimation` object can be reused.

# Adw.Application

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Application.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-application.c\#L12 "go to source location")

```
class Adw.Application : Gtk.Application
  implements Gio.ActionGroup, Gio.ActionMap {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A base class for Adwaita applications.

`AdwApplication` handles library initialization by calling [`adw_init()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/func.init.html) in the
default [`GApplication::startup`](https://docs.gtk.org/gio/signal.Application.startup.html) signal handler, in turn chaining up
as required by [`GtkApplication`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Application.html). Therefore, any subclass of
`AdwApplication` should always chain up its `startup` handler before using
any Adwaita or GTKAPI.

## Automatic Resources [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Application.html\#automatic-resources "Permanent link")

`AdwApplication` will automatically load certain resources located in the
application’s resource base path (see
[`g_application_set_resource_base_path()`](https://docs.gtk.org/gio/method.Application.set_resource_base_path.html), if they’re present.

### Shortcuts Dialog [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Application.html\#shortcuts-dialog "Permanent link")

If there’s a resource located at `shortcuts-dialog.ui` which defines an
[`AdwShortcutsDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ShortcutsDialog.html) with the ID`shortcuts_dialog`, `AdwApplication`
will set up an `app.shortcuts` action that creates and presents this dialog,
as well as a `Ctrl` `?` accelerator for it.

### Stylesheet [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Application.html\#stylesheet "Permanent link")

If there’s a resource located at `style.css`, `AdwApplication` will load
styles from it. This can be used to add custom styles to the application.

#### Additional styles (deprecated) [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Application.html\#additional-styles-deprecated "Permanent link")

`AdwApplication` will also load the following stylesheets conditionally:

- `style-dark.css` when [`AdwStyleManager:dark`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.StyleManager.dark.html) is `TRUE`.

- `style-hc.css` when the system high contrast preference is enabled.

- `style-hc-dark.css` when the system high contrast preference is enabled and
[`AdwStyleManager:dark`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.StyleManager.dark.html) is `TRUE`.


Warning

These resources are deprecated since 1.9.

Use `style.css` with the following media queries instead:

- `prefers-color-scheme: dark` for styles used only for dark appearance.
- `prefers-contrast: more` for styles used only when the system high
contrast preference is enabled.

# Adw.ApplicationWindow

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ApplicationWindow.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-application-window.c\#L21 "go to source location")

```
class Adw.ApplicationWindow : Gtk.ApplicationWindow
  implements Gio.ActionGroup, Gio.ActionMap, Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget, Gtk.Native, Gtk.Root, Gtk.ShortcutManager {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A freeform application window.

![application-window](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/application-window.png)

`AdwApplicationWindow` is a [`GtkApplicationWindow`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ApplicationWindow.html) subclass providing
the same features as [`AdwWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Window.html).

See [`AdwWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Window.html) for details.

Example of an `AdwApplicationWindow`UI definition:

```
<object class="AdwApplicationWindow">
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwToolbarView">
      <child type="top">
        <object class="AdwHeaderBar"/>
      </child>
      <property name="content">
        <!-- put your content here -->
      </property>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

Using [`GtkApplication:menubar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Application.menubar.html) is not supported and may result in
visual glitches.
