# Adw.Avatar

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Avatar.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-avatar.c\#L22 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.Avatar : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A widget displaying an image, with a generated fallback.

![avatar](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/avatar.png)

`AdwAvatar` is a widget that shows a round avatar.

`AdwAvatar` generates an avatar with the initials of the
[`AdwAvatar:text`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Avatar.text.html) on top of a colored background.

The color is picked based on the hash of the [`AdwAvatar:text`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Avatar.text.html).

If [`AdwAvatar:show-initials`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Avatar.show-initials.html) is set to `FALSE`,
[`AdwAvatar:icon-name`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Avatar.icon-name.html) or `adw-avatar-default-symbolic` is shown instead
of the initials.

Use [`AdwAvatar:custom-image`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Avatar.custom-image.html) to set a custom image.

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Avatar.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwAvatar` has a single CSS node with name `avatar`.

## Accessibility [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Avatar.html\#accessibility "Permanent link")

`AdwAvatar` uses the [`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_IMG`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#img) role.

# Adw.Banner

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Banner.html

since: 1.3

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-banner.c\#L37 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.Banner : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Actionable, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.3

A bar with contextual information.

![banner](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/banner.png)

Banners are hidden by default, use [`AdwBanner:revealed`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Banner.revealed.html) to show them.

Banners have a title, set with [`AdwBanner:title`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Banner.title.html). Titles can be marked
up with Pango markup, use [`AdwBanner:use-markup`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Banner.use-markup.html) to enable it.

The title will be shown centered or left-aligned depending on available space.

Banners can optionally have a button with text on it, set through
[`AdwBanner:button-label`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Banner.button-label.html). The button can be used with a `GAction`,
or with the [`AdwBanner::button-clicked`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.Banner.button-clicked.html) signal. The button can have
different styles, a gray style and a suggested style.

![banner with suggested button style](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/banner-suggested.png)

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Banner.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwBanner` has a main CSS node with the name `banner`.

# Adw.Bin

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Bin.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-bin.c\#L15 "go to source location")

```
class Adw.Bin : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A widget with one child.

![bin](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/bin.png)

The `AdwBin` widget has only one child, set with the [`AdwBin:child`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Bin.child.html) property.

It is useful for deriving subclasses, since it provides common code needed
for handling a single child widget.

\[−\]

# Adw.BottomSheet

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.BottomSheet.html

since: 1.6

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-bottom-sheet.c\#L36 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.BottomSheet : Gtk.Widget
  implements Adw.Swipeable, Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.6

A bottom sheet with an optional bottom bar.

![bottom-sheet](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/bottom-sheet.png)

`AdwBottomSheet` has three child widgets. [`AdwBottomSheet:content`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.BottomSheet.content.html) is
shown persistently. [`AdwBottomSheet:sheet`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.BottomSheet.sheet.html) is displayed above it when
it’s open, and [`AdwBottomSheet:bottom-bar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.BottomSheet.bottom-bar.html) is displayed when it’s not.

Bottom sheet and bottom bar are attached to the bottom edge of the widget.
They take the full width by default, but can only take a portion of it if
[`AdwBottomSheet:full-width`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.BottomSheet.full-width.html) is set to `FALSE`. In this case,
[`AdwBottomSheet:align`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.BottomSheet.align.html) determines where along the bottom edge they are placed.

Bottom bar can be hidden using the [`AdwBottomSheet:reveal-bottom-bar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.BottomSheet.reveal-bottom-bar.html) property.

`AdwBottomSheet` can be useful for applications such as music players, that
want to have a persistent bottom bar that expands into a bottom sheet when
clicked. It’s meant for cases where a bottom sheet is tightly integrated into
the UI. For more transient bottom sheets, see [`AdwDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Dialog.html).

To open or close the bottom sheet, use the [`AdwBottomSheet:open`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.BottomSheet.open.html) property.

By default, the bottom sheet has an overlaid drag handle. It can be disabled
by setting [`AdwBottomSheet:show-drag-handle`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.BottomSheet.show-drag-handle.html) to `FALSE`. Note that the
handle also controls whether the sheet can be dragged using a pointer.

Bottom sheets are modal by default, meaning that the content is dimmed and
cannot be accessed while the sheet is open. Set [`AdwBottomSheet:modal`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.BottomSheet.modal.html)
to `FALSE` if this behavior is unwanted.

To disable user interactions for opening or closing the bottom sheet (such as
swipes or clicking the bottom bar or close button), set
[`AdwBottomSheet:can-open`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.BottomSheet.can-open.html) or [`AdwBottomSheet:can-close`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.BottomSheet.can-close.html) to
`FALSE`.

In some cases, particularly when using a full-width bottom bar, it may be
necessary to shift [`AdwBottomSheet:content`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.BottomSheet.content.html) upwards. Use the
[`AdwBottomSheet:bottom-bar-height`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.BottomSheet.bottom-bar-height.html) and
[`AdwBottomSheet:sheet-height`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.BottomSheet.sheet-height.html) for that.

`AdwBottomSheet` is not adaptive, and for larger window sizes applications
may want to replace it with another UI, such as a sidebar. This can be done
using [`AdwMultiLayoutView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.MultiLayoutView.html).

## Sizing [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.BottomSheet.html\#sizing "Permanent link")

Unlike [`AdwDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Dialog.html) presented as a bottom sheet, `AdwBottomSheet` just
follows the content’s natural size, and it’s up to the applications to make
sure their content provides one. For example, when using
[`GtkScrolledWindow`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ScrolledWindow.html), make sure to set
[`GtkScrolledWindow:propagate-natural-height`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.ScrolledWindow.propagate-natural-height.html) to `TRUE`.

## Header Bar Integration [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.BottomSheet.html\#header-bar-integration "Permanent link")

When placed inside an `AdwBottomSheet`, [`AdwHeaderBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html) will not show the
title when [`AdwBottomSheet:show-drag-handle`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.BottomSheet.show-drag-handle.html) is `TRUE`, regardless of
[`AdwHeaderBar:show-title`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.show-title.html). This only applies to the default title,
titles set with [`AdwHeaderBar:title-widget`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.title-widget.html) will still be shown.

## `AdwBottomSheet` as `GtkBuildable`: [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.BottomSheet.html\#adwbottomsheet-as-gtkbuildable "Permanent link")

The `AdwBottomSheet` implementation of the [`GtkBuildable`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/iface.Buildable.html) interface
supports setting the sheet widget by specifying “sheet” as the “type”
attribute of a `<child>` element, and the bottom bar by specifying
“bottom-bar”. Specifying “content” or omitting the child type results in
setting the content child.

# Adw.Breakpoint

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Breakpoint.html

since: 1.4

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-breakpoint.c\#L19 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.Breakpoint : GObject.Object
  implements Gtk.Buildable {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.4

Describes a breakpoint for [`AdwWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Window.html) or [`AdwDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Dialog.html).

Breakpoints are used to create adaptive UI, allowing to change the layout
depending on available size.

Breakpoint is a size threshold, specified by its condition, as well as one or
more setters.

Each setter has a target object, a property and a value. When a breakpoint
is applied, each setter sets the target property on their target object to
the specified value, and reset it back to the original value when it’s unapplied.

For more complicated scenarios, [`AdwBreakpoint::apply`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.Breakpoint.apply.html) and
[`AdwBreakpoint::unapply`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.Breakpoint.unapply.html) can be used instead.

Breakpoints can be used within [`AdwWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Window.html), [`AdwApplicationWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ApplicationWindow.html),
[`AdwDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Dialog.html) or [`AdwBreakpointBin`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.BreakpointBin.html).

## `AdwBreakpoint` as `GtkBuildable`: [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Breakpoint.html\#adwbreakpoint-as-gtkbuildable "Permanent link")

`AdwBreakpoint` supports specifying its condition via the `<condition>`
element. The contents of the element must be a string in a format accepted by
[`adw_breakpoint_condition_parse()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/type_func.BreakpointCondition.parse.html).

It also supports adding setters via the `<setter>` element. Each `<setter>`
element must have the `object` attribute specifying the target object, and
the `property` attribute specifying the property name. The contents of the
element are used as the setter value.

For `G_TYPE_OBJECT` and `G_TYPE_BOXED` derived properties, empty contents are
treated as `NULL`.

Setter values can be translated with the usual `translatable`, `context` and
`comments` attributes.

Example of an `AdwBreakpoint`UI definition:

```
<object class="AdwBreakpoint">
  <condition>max-width: 400px</condition>
  <setter object="button" property="visible">True</setter>
  <setter object="box" property="orientation">vertical</setter>
  <setter object="page" property="title" translatable="yes">Example</setter>
</object>
```

Copy

# Adw.BreakpointBin

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.BreakpointBin.html

since: 1.4

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-breakpoint-bin.c\#L17 "go to source location")

```
class Adw.BreakpointBin : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.4

A widget that changes layout based on available size.

![breakpoint-bin](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/breakpoint-bin.png)

`AdwBreakpointBin` provides a way to use breakpoints without [`AdwWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Window.html),
[`AdwApplicationWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ApplicationWindow.html) or [`AdwDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Dialog.html). It can be useful for limiting
breakpoints to a single page and similar purposes. Most applications
shouldn’t need it.

`AdwBreakpointBin` is similar to [`AdwBin`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Bin.html). It has one child, set via the
[`AdwBreakpointBin:child`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.BreakpointBin.child.html) property.

When `AdwBreakpointBin` is resized, its child widget can rearrange its layout
at specific thresholds.

The thresholds and layout changes are defined via [`AdwBreakpoint`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Breakpoint.html) objects.
They can be added using [`adw_breakpoint_bin_add_breakpoint()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.BreakpointBin.add_breakpoint.html).

Each breakpoint has a condition, specifying the bin’s size and/or aspect
ratio, and setters that automatically set object properties when that
happens. The [`AdwBreakpoint::apply`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.Breakpoint.apply.html) and [`AdwBreakpoint::unapply`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.Breakpoint.unapply.html) can
be used instead for more complex scenarios.

Breakpoints are only allowed to modify widgets inside the `AdwBreakpointBin`,
but not on the `AdwBreakpointBin` itself or any other widgets.

If multiple breakpoints can be used for the current size, the last one is
always picked. The current breakpoint can be tracked using the
[`AdwBreakpointBin:current-breakpoint`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.BreakpointBin.current-breakpoint.html) property.

If none of the breakpoints can be used, that property will be set to `NULL`,
and the original property values will be used instead.

## Minimum Size [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.BreakpointBin.html\#minimum-size "Permanent link")

Adding a breakpoint to `AdwBreakpointBin` will result in it having no minimum
size. The [`GtkWidget:width-request`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Widget.width-request.html) and
[`GtkWidget:height-request`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Widget.height-request.html) properties must always be set when using
breakpoints, indicating the smallest size you want to support.

The minimum size and breakpoint conditions must be carefully selected so that
the child widget completely fits. If it doesn’t, it will overflow and a
warning message will be printed.

When choosing minimum size, consider translations and text scale factor
changes. Make sure to leave enough space for text labels, and enable
ellipsizing or wrapping if they might not fit.

For [`GtkLabel`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Label.html) this can be done via [`GtkLabel:ellipsize`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Label.ellipsize.html), or
via [`GtkLabel:wrap`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Label.wrap.html) together with [`GtkLabel:wrap-mode`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Label.wrap-mode.html).

For buttons, use [`GtkButton:can-shrink`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Button.can-shrink.html),
[`GtkMenuButton:can-shrink`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.MenuButton.can-shrink.html), [`AdwSplitButton:can-shrink`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SplitButton.can-shrink.html),
or [`AdwButtonContent:can-shrink`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ButtonContent.can-shrink.html).

## Example [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.BreakpointBin.html\#example "Permanent link")

```
GtkWidget *bin, *child;
AdwBreakpoint *breakpoint;

bin = adw_breakpoint_bin_new ();
gtk_widget_set_size_request (bin, 150, 150);

child = gtk_label_new ("Wide");
gtk_label_set_ellipsize (GTK_LABEL (label), PANGO_ELLIPSIZE_END);
gtk_widget_add_css_class (child, "title-1");
adw_breakpoint_bin_set_child (ADW_BREAKPOINT_BIN (bin), child);

breakpoint = adw_breakpoint_new (adw_breakpoint_condition_parse ("max-width: 200px"));
adw_breakpoint_add_setters (breakpoint,
                            G_OBJECT (child), "label", "Narrow",
                            NULL);
adw_breakpoint_bin_add_breakpoint (ADW_BREAKPOINT_BIN (bin), breakpoint);
```

Copy

The bin has a single label inside it, displaying “Wide”. When the bin’s width
is smaller than or equal to 200px, it changes to “Narrow”.

## `AdwBreakpointBin` as `GtkBuildable` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.BreakpointBin.html\#adwbreakpointbin-as-gtkbuildable "Permanent link")

`AdwBreakpointBin` allows adding `AdwBreakpoint` objects as children.

Example of an `AdwBreakpointBin`UI definition:

```
<object class="AdwBreakpointBin">
  <property name="width-request">150</property>
  <property name="height-request">150</property>
  <property name="child">
    <object class="GtkLabel" id="child">
      <property name="label">Wide</property>
      <property name="ellipsize">end</property>
      <style>
        <class name="title-1"/>
      </style>
    </object>
  </property>
  <child>
    <object class="AdwBreakpoint">
      <condition>max-width: 200px</condition>
      <setter object="child" property="label">Narrow</setter>
    </object>
  </child>
</object>
```

Copy

See [`AdwBreakpoint`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Breakpoint.html) documentation for details.

# Adw.ButtonContent

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ButtonContent.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-button-content.c\#L14 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.ButtonContent : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A helper widget for creating buttons.

![button-content](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/button-content.png)

`AdwButtonContent` is a box-like widget with an icon and a label.

It’s intended to be used as a direct child of [`GtkButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Button.html),
[`GtkMenuButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.MenuButton.html) or [`AdwSplitButton`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SplitButton.html), when they need to have both an
icon and a label, as follows:

```
<object class="GtkButton">
  <property name="child">
    <object class="AdwButtonContent">
      <property name="icon-name">document-open-symbolic</property>
      <property name="label" translatable="yes">_Open</property>
      <property name="use-underline">True</property>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

`AdwButtonContent` handles style classes and connecting the mnemonic to the
button automatically.

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ButtonContent.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

```
buttoncontent
╰── box
    ├── image
    ╰── label
```

Copy

`AdwButtonContent`‘s CSS node is called `buttoncontent`. It contains a `box`
subnode that serves as a container for the `image` and `label` nodes.

When inside a `GtkButton` or `AdwSplitButton`, the button will receive the
`.image-text-button` style class. When inside a `GtkMenuButton`, the
internal `GtkButton` will receive it instead.

## Accessibility [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ButtonContent.html\#accessibility "Permanent link")

`AdwButtonContent` uses the [`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_GROUP`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#group) role.

# Adw.ButtonRow

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ButtonRow.html

since: 1.6

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-button-row.c\#L15 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.ButtonRow : Adw.PreferencesRow
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Actionable, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.6

A [`GtkListBoxRow`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListBoxRow.html) that looks like a button.

![button-rows](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/button-rows.png)

The `AdwButtonRow` widget has a title and two icons: before and after the title.

It is convenient for presenting actions like “Delete” at the end of a boxed list.

`AdwButtonRow` is always activatable.

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ButtonRow.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwButtonRow` has a main CSS node with name `row` and the style class
`.button`.

It contains the subnode `box` for its main horizontal box, which contains the
nodes: `image.icon.start` for the start icon, `label.title` for the title,
and `image.icon.end` for the end icon.

## Style classes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ButtonRow.html\#style-classes "Permanent link")

The [`.suggested-action`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#suggested-action) style class
makes `AdwButtonRow` use accent color for its background. It should be used
very sparingly to denote important buttons.

![button-row-suggested-action](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/button-row-suggested-action.png)

The [`.destructive-action`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#destructive-action) style
makes the row use destructive colors. It can be used to draw attention to the
potentially damaging consequences of using it. This style acts as a warning
to the user.

![button-row-destructive-action](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/button-row-destructive-action.png).

# Adw.Carousel

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Carousel.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-carousel.c\#L24 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.Carousel : Gtk.Widget
  implements Adw.Swipeable, Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget, Gtk.Orientable {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A paginated scrolling widget.

![carousel](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/carousel.png)

The `AdwCarousel` widget can be used to display a set of pages with
swipe-based navigation between them.

[`AdwCarouselIndicatorDots`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.CarouselIndicatorDots.html) and [`AdwCarouselIndicatorLines`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.CarouselIndicatorLines.html) can be used
to provide page indicators for `AdwCarousel`.

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Carousel.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwCarousel` has a single CSS node with name `carousel`.

# Adw.CarouselIndicatorDots

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.CarouselIndicatorDots.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-carousel-indicator-dots.c\#L24 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.CarouselIndicatorDots : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget, Gtk.Orientable {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A dots indicator for [`AdwCarousel`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Carousel.html).

![carousel-indicator-dots](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/carousel-indicator-dots.png)

The `AdwCarouselIndicatorDots` widget shows a set of dots for each page of a
given [`AdwCarousel`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Carousel.html). The dot representing the carousel’s active page is
larger and more opaque than the others, the transition to the active and
inactive state is gradual to match the carousel’s position.

See also [`AdwCarouselIndicatorLines`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.CarouselIndicatorLines.html).

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.CarouselIndicatorDots.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwCarouselIndicatorDots` has a single CSS node with name
`carouselindicatordots`.

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-carousel-indicator-lines.c\#L23 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.CarouselIndicatorLines : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget, Gtk.Orientable {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A lines indicator for [`AdwCarousel`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Carousel.html).

![carousel-indicator-lines](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/carousel-indicator-lines.png)

The `AdwCarouselIndicatorLines` widget shows a set of lines for each page of
a given [`AdwCarousel`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Carousel.html). The carousel’s active page is shown as another line
that moves between them to match the carousel’s position.

See also [`AdwCarouselIndicatorDots`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.CarouselIndicatorDots.html).

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.CarouselIndicatorLines.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`carouselindicatorlines`.

# Adw.Clamp

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Clamp.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-clamp.c\#L16 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.Clamp : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget, Gtk.Orientable {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A widget constraining its child to a given size.

![clamp-wide](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/clamp-wide.png)![clamp-narrow](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/clamp-narrow.png)

The `AdwClamp` widget constrains the size of the widget it contains to a
given maximum size. It will constrain the width if it is horizontal, or the
height if it is vertical. The expansion of the child from its minimum to its
maximum size is eased out for a smooth transition.

If the child requires more than the requested maximum size, it will be
allocated the minimum size it can fit in instead.

`AdwClamp` can scale with the text scale factor, use the
[`AdwClamp:unit`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Clamp.unit.html) property to enable that behavior.

See also: [`AdwClampLayout`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ClampLayout.html), [`AdwClampScrollable`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ClampScrollable.html).

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Clamp.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwClamp` has a single CSS node with name `clamp`.

# Adw.ClampLayout

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ClampLayout.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-clamp-layout.c\#L17 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.ClampLayout : Gtk.LayoutManager
  implements Gtk.Orientable {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A layout manager constraining its children to a given size.

![clamp-wide](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/clamp-wide.png)![clamp-narrow](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/clamp-narrow.png)

`AdwClampLayout` constraints the size of the widgets it contains to a given
maximum size. It will constrain the width if it is horizontal, or the height
if it is vertical. The expansion of the children from their minimum to their
maximum size is eased out for a smooth transition.

If a child requires more than the requested maximum size, it will be
allocated the minimum size it can fit in instead.

`AdwClampLayout` can scale with the text scale factor, use the
[`AdwClampLayout:unit`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ClampLayout.unit.html) property to enable that behavior.

See also: [`AdwClamp`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Clamp.html), [`AdwClampScrollable`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ClampScrollable.html).

# Adw.ClampScrollable

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ClampScrollable.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-clamp-scrollable.c\#L16 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.ClampScrollable : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget, Gtk.Orientable, Gtk.Scrollable {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A scrollable [`AdwClamp`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Clamp.html).

`AdwClampScrollable` is a variant of [`AdwClamp`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Clamp.html) that implements the
[`GtkScrollable`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/iface.Scrollable.html) interface.

The primary use case for `AdwClampScrollable` is clamping
[`GtkListView`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListView.html).

See also: [`AdwClampLayout`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ClampLayout.html).

\[−\]

# Adw.ComboRow

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ComboRow.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-combo-row.c\#L16 "go to source location")

```
class Adw.ComboRow : Adw.ActionRow
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Actionable, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A [`GtkListBoxRow`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListBoxRow.html) used to choose from a list of items.

![combo-row](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/combo-row.png)

The `AdwComboRow` widget allows the user to choose from a list of valid
choices. The row displays the selected choice. When activated, the row
displays a popover which allows the user to make a new choice.

Example of an `AdwComboRow`UI definition:

```
<object class="AdwComboRow">
  <property name="title" translatable="yes">Combo Row</property>
  <property name="model">
    <object class="GtkStringList">
      <items>
        <item translatable="yes">Foo</item>
        <item translatable="yes">Bar</item>
        <item translatable="yes">Baz</item>
      </items>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

The [`AdwComboRow:selected`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ComboRow.selected.html) and [`AdwComboRow:selected-item`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ComboRow.selected-item.html)
properties can be used to keep track of the selected item and react to their changes.

`AdwComboRow` mirrors [`GtkDropDown`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.DropDown.html), see that widget for details.

`AdwComboRow` is [`GtkListBoxRow:activatable`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.ListBoxRow.activatable.html) if a model is set.

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ComboRow.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwComboRow` has a main CSS node with name `row` and the `.combo` style class.

Its popover has the node named `popover` with the `.menu` style class, it
contains a [`GtkScrolledWindow`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ScrolledWindow.html), which in turn contains a
[`GtkListView`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListView.html), both are accessible via their regular nodes.

## Accessibility [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ComboRow.html\#accessibility "Permanent link")

`AdwComboRow` uses the [`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_COMBO_BOX`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#combo-box) role.

# Adw.CssClassBinding

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.CssClassBinding.html

since: 1.10

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-css-class-binding.c\#L29 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.CssClassBinding : GObject.Object
{
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.10

A binding between a [`GObject`](https://docs.gtk.org/gobject/class.Object.html) property and a CSS class on a
[`GtkWidget`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Widget.html).

To create a binding, use [`adw_bind_property_to_css_class()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/func.bind_property_to_css_class.html).

Whenever the source property changes, a CSS class is toggled on the target
object; for instance, given the following binding:

```
adw_bind_property_to_css_class (source, "property",
                                target, "css-class",
                                G_BINDING_DEFAULT);
```

Copy

when `property` is a boolean property, `css-class` will be set every time the
value of `property` is changed to `TRUE`, and vice versa.

Using [`adw_bind_property_to_css_class_full()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/func.bind_property_to_css_class_full.html), it’s possible to define a
custom mapping between a property and the boolean enable state, that is,
defining a mapping between any arbitrary property type and a boolean type.
This allows for any property, not just boolean properties, to be bound to a
CSS class; for instance, the following binding

```
adw_bind_property_to_css_class_full (source, "property",
                                     target, "css-class",
                                     G_BINDING_DEFAULT,
                                     int_to_bool,
                                     bool_to_int,
                                     NULL, NULL);
```

Copy

will map an integer-typed `property` to a boolean value, and use the value of
that boolean to toggle the CSS class.

It is possible to invert the type of a boolean without using a custom map
function by using the [`G_BINDING_INVERT_BOOLEAN`](https://docs.gtk.org/gobject/flags.BindingFlags.html#invert-boolean) flag.

A binding will be removed, and any allocated resources freed, whenever either
one of the source or target instances are finalized, or when the binding
instances loses its last reference.

Languages with garbage collection, or developers wanting to fully control the
lifecycle of a binding may use [`adw_css_class_binding_unbind()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.CssClassBinding.unbind.html) to expliticly
release a binding, instead of relying on the last reference on the binding,
source, and target instances to drop.

# Adw.Dialog

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Dialog.html

since: 1.5

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-dialog.c\#L44 "go to source location")

```
class Adw.Dialog : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget, Gtk.ShortcutManager {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.5

An adaptive dialog container.

![dialog-floating](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/dialog-floating.png)![dialog-bottom](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/dialog-bottom.png)

`AdwDialog` is similar to a window, but is shown within another window. It
can be used with [`AdwWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Window.html) and [`AdwApplicationWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ApplicationWindow.html), use
[`adw_dialog_present()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Dialog.present.html) to show it.

`AdwDialog` is not resizable. Use the [`AdwDialog:content-width`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Dialog.content-width.html) and
[`AdwDialog:content-height`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Dialog.content-height.html) properties to set its size, or set
[`AdwDialog:follows-content-size`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Dialog.follows-content-size.html) to `TRUE` to make the dialog track the
content’s size as it changes. `AdwDialog` can never be larger than its parent window.

`AdwDialog` can be presented as a centered floating window or a bottom sheet.
By default it’s automatic depending on the available size.
[`AdwDialog:presentation-mode`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Dialog.presentation-mode.html) can be used to change that.

`AdwDialog` can be closed via [`adw_dialog_close()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Dialog.close.html).

When presented as a bottom sheet, `AdwDialog` can also be closed via swiping
it down.

The [`AdwDialog:can-close`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Dialog.can-close.html) can be used to prevent closing. In that case,
[`AdwDialog::close-attempt`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.Dialog.close-attempt.html) gets emitted instead.

Use [`adw_dialog_force_close()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Dialog.force_close.html) to close the dialog even when `can-close` is set to
`FALSE`.

`AdwDialog` is transient and doesn’t integrate with the window below it, for
example it’s not possible to collapse it into a bottom bar. See
[`AdwBottomSheet`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.BottomSheet.html) for persistent and more tightly integrated bottom sheets.

## Header Bar Integration [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Dialog.html\#header-bar-integration "Permanent link")

When placed inside an `AdwDialog`, [`AdwHeaderBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html) will display the dialog
title instead of window title. It will also adjust the decoration layout to
ensure it always has a close button and nothing else. Set
[`AdwHeaderBar:show-start-title-buttons`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.show-start-title-buttons.html) and
[`AdwHeaderBar:show-end-title-buttons`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.show-end-title-buttons.html) to `FALSE` to remove it if it’s unwanted.

## Breakpoints [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Dialog.html\#breakpoints "Permanent link")

`AdwDialog` can be used with [`AdwBreakpoint`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Breakpoint.html) the same way as
[`AdwBreakpointBin`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.BreakpointBin.html). Refer to that widget’s documentation for details.

Like `AdwBreakpointBin`, if breakpoints are used, `AdwDialog` doesn’t have a
minimum size, and [`GtkWidget:width-request`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Widget.width-request.html) and
[`GtkWidget:height-request`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Widget.height-request.html) properties must be set manually.

# Adw.EntryRow

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.EntryRow.html

since: 1.2

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-entry-row.c\#L21 "go to source location")

```
class Adw.EntryRow : Adw.PreferencesRow
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Actionable, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget, Gtk.Editable {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.2

A [`GtkListBoxRow`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListBoxRow.html) with an embedded text entry.

![entry-row](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/entry-row.png)

`AdwEntryRow` has a title that doubles as placeholder text. It shows an icon
indicating that it’s editable and can receive additional widgets before or
after the editable part.

If [`AdwEntryRow:show-apply-button`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.EntryRow.show-apply-button.html) is set to `TRUE`, `AdwEntryRow` can
show an apply button when editing its contents. This can be useful if
changing its contents can result in an expensive operation, such as network activity.

`AdwEntryRow` provides only minimal API and should be used with the
[`GtkEditable`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/iface.Editable.html) API.

See also [`AdwPasswordEntryRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PasswordEntryRow.html).

## AdwEntryRow as GtkBuildable [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.EntryRow.html\#adwentryrow-as-gtkbuildable "Permanent link")

The `AdwEntryRow` implementation of the [`GtkBuildable`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/iface.Buildable.html) interface
supports adding a child at its end by specifying “suffix” or omitting the
“type” attribute of a  element.

It also supports adding a child as a prefix widget by specifying “prefix” as
the “type” attribute of a  element.

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.EntryRow.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwEntryRow` has a single CSS node with name `row` and the `.entry` style class.

# Adw.ExpanderRow

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ExpanderRow.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-expander-row.c\#L13 "go to source location")

```
class Adw.ExpanderRow : Adw.PreferencesRow
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Actionable, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A [`GtkListBoxRow`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListBoxRow.html) used to reveal widgets.

![expander-row](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/expander-row.png)

The `AdwExpanderRow` widget allows the user to reveal or hide widgets below
it. It also allows the user to enable the expansion of the row, allowing to
disable all that the row contains.

## AdwExpanderRow as GtkBuildable [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ExpanderRow.html\#adwexpanderrow-as-gtkbuildable "Permanent link")

The `AdwExpanderRow` implementation of the [`GtkBuildable`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/iface.Buildable.html) interface
supports adding a child as an suffix widget by specifying “suffix” as the
“type” attribute of a  element.

It also supports adding it as a prefix widget by specifying “prefix” as the
“type” attribute of a  element.

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ExpanderRow.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwExpanderRow` has a main CSS node with name `row` and the `.expander`
style class. It has the `.empty` style class when it contains no children.

It contains the subnodes `row.header` for its main embedded row,
`list.nested` for the list it can expand, and `image.expander-row-arrow` for
its arrow.

## Style classes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ExpanderRow.html\#style-classes "Permanent link")

`AdwExpanderRow` can use the [`.`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#property-rows)
style class to emphasize the row subtitle instead of the row title, which is
useful for displaying read-only properties.

When used together with the `.monospace` style class, only the subtitle
becomes monospace, not the title or any extra widgets.

# Adw.Flap

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Flap.html

deprecated: 1.4

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-flap.c\#L23 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.Flap : Gtk.Widget
  implements Adw.Swipeable, Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget, Gtk.Orientable {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Deprecated since: 1.4

See [the migration guide](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html#replace-adwflap).

An adaptive container acting like a box or an overlay.

![flap-wide](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/flap-wide.png)![flap-narrow](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/flap-narrow.png)

The `AdwFlap` widget can display its children like a [`GtkBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Box.html) does or
like a [`GtkOverlay`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Overlay.html) does, according to the
[`AdwFlap:fold-policy`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Flap.fold-policy.html) value.

`AdwFlap` has at most three children: [`AdwFlap:content`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Flap.content.html),
[`AdwFlap:flap`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Flap.flap.html) and [`AdwFlap:separator`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Flap.separator.html). Content is the primary
child, flap is displayed next to it when unfolded, or overlays it when
folded. Flap can be shown or hidden by changing the
[`AdwFlap:reveal-flap`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Flap.reveal-flap.html) value, as well as via swipe gestures if
[`AdwFlap:swipe-to-open`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Flap.swipe-to-open.html) and/or [`AdwFlap:swipe-to-close`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Flap.swipe-to-close.html) are set
to `TRUE`.

Optionally, a separator can be provided, which would be displayed between
the content and the flap when there’s no shadow to separate them, depending
on the transition type.

[`AdwFlap:flap`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Flap.flap.html) is transparent by default; add the
[`.background`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#background) style class to it if this is unwanted.

If [`AdwFlap:modal`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Flap.modal.html) is set to `TRUE`, content becomes completely
inaccessible when the flap is revealed while folded.

The position of the flap and separator children relative to the content is
determined by orientation, as well as the [`AdwFlap:flap-position`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Flap.flap-position.html) value.

Folding the flap will automatically hide the flap widget, and unfolding it
will automatically reveal it. If this behavior is not desired, the
[`AdwFlap:locked`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Flap.locked.html) property can be used to override it.

Common use cases include sidebars, header bars that need to be able to
overlap the window content (for example, in fullscreen mode) and bottom sheets.

## AdwFlap as GtkBuildable [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Flap.html\#adwflap-as-gtkbuildable "Permanent link")

The `AdwFlap` implementation of the [`GtkBuildable`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/iface.Buildable.html) interface supports
setting the flap child by specifying “flap” as the “type” attribute of a
`<child>` element, and separator by specifying “separator”. Specifying
“content” child type or omitting it results in setting the content child.

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Flap.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwFlap` has a single CSS node with name `flap`. The node will get the style
classes `.folded` when it is folded, and `.unfolded` when it’s not.

# Adw.HeaderBar

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-header-bar.c\#L45 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.HeaderBar : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A title bar widget.

![header-bar](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/header-bar.png)

`AdwHeaderBar` is similar to [`GtkHeaderBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.HeaderBar.html), but provides additional
features compared to it. Refer to `GtkHeaderBar` for details. It is typically
used as a top bar within [`AdwToolbarView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToolbarView.html).

## Dialog Integration [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html\#dialog-integration "Permanent link")

When placed inside an [`AdwDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Dialog.html), `AdwHeaderBar` will display the dialog
title instead of window title. It will also adjust the decoration layout to
ensure it always has a close button and nothing else. Set
[`AdwHeaderBar:show-start-title-buttons`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.show-start-title-buttons.html) and
[`AdwHeaderBar:show-end-title-buttons`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.show-end-title-buttons.html) to `FALSE` to remove it if it’s unwanted.

## Navigation View Integration [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html\#navigation-view-integration "Permanent link")

When placed inside an [`AdwNavigationPage`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationPage.html), `AdwHeaderBar` will display the
page title instead of window title.

When used together with [`AdwNavigationView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationView.html) or [`AdwNavigationSplitView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationSplitView.html),
it will also display a back button that can be used to go back to the previous
page. The button also has a context menu, allowing to pop multiple pages at
once, potentially across multiple navigation views.

Set [`AdwHeaderBar:show-back-button`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.show-back-button.html) to `FALSE` to disable this behavior
in rare scenarios where it’s unwanted.

## Split View Integration [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html\#split-view-integration "Permanent link")

When placed inside [`AdwNavigationSplitView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationSplitView.html) or [`AdwOverlaySplitView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.OverlaySplitView.html),
`AdwHeaderBar` will automatically hide the title buttons other than at the
edges of the window.

## Bottom Sheet Integration [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html\#bottom-sheet-integration "Permanent link")

When played inside [`AdwBottomSheet`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.BottomSheet.html), `AdwHeaderBar` will not show the title
unless [`AdwBottomSheet:show-drag-handle`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.BottomSheet.show-drag-handle.html) is set to `FALSE`, regardless
of [`AdwHeaderBar:show-title`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.show-title.html). This only applies to the default title,
titles set with [`AdwHeaderBar:title-widget`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.title-widget.html) will still be shown.

## Centering Policy [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html\#centering-policy "Permanent link")

[`AdwHeaderBar:centering-policy`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.centering-policy.html) allows to enforce strict centering of
the title widget. This can be useful for entries inside [`AdwClamp`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Clamp.html).

## Title Buttons [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html\#title-buttons "Permanent link")

Unlike `GtkHeaderBar`, `AdwHeaderBar` allows to toggle title button
visibility for each side individually, using the
[`AdwHeaderBar:show-start-title-buttons`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.show-start-title-buttons.html) and
[`AdwHeaderBar:show-end-title-buttons`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.show-end-title-buttons.html) properties.

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

```
headerbar
╰── windowhandle
    ╰── box
        ├── widget
        │   ╰── box.start
        │       ├── windowcontrols.start
        │       ├── widget
        │       │   ╰── [button.back]
        │       ╰── [other children]
        ├── widget
        │   ╰── [Title Widget]
        ╰── widget
            ╰── box.end
                ├── [other children]
                ╰── windowcontrols.end
```

Copy

`AdwHeaderBar`‘s CSS node is called `headerbar`. It contains a `windowhandle`
subnode, which contains a `box` subnode, which contains three `widget`
subnodes at the start, center and end of the header bar. The start and end
subnodes contain a `box` subnode with the `.start` and `.end` style classes
respectively, and the center node contains a node that represents the title.

Each of the boxes contains a `windowcontrols` subnode, see
[`GtkWindowControls`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.WindowControls.html) for details, as well as other children.

When [`AdwHeaderBar:show-back-button`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.show-back-button.html) is `TRUE`, the start box also
contains a node with the name `widget` that contains a node with the name
`button` and `.back` style class.

## Accessibility [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html\#accessibility "Permanent link")

`AdwHeaderBar` uses the [`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_GROUP`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#group) role.

# Adw.InlineViewSwitcher

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.InlineViewSwitcher.html

since: 1.7

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-inline-view-switcher.c\#L33 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.InlineViewSwitcher : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget, Gtk.Orientable {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.7

A view switcher that uses a toggle group.

![inline-view-switcher](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/inline-view-switcher.png)

A view switcher showing pages of an [`AdwViewStack`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewStack.html) within an
[`AdwToggleGroup`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToggleGroup.html), similar to [`AdwViewSwitcher`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcher.html).

The toggles can display either an icon, a label or both. Use the
[`AdwInlineViewSwitcher:display-mode`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.InlineViewSwitcher.display-mode.html) to control this.

![inline-view-switcher-display-modes](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/inline-view-switcher-display-modes.png)

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.InlineViewSwitcher.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwInlineViewSwitcher` has a single CSS node with the name
`inline-view-switcher`.

## Style classes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.InlineViewSwitcher.html\#style-classes "Permanent link")

Like `AdwToggleGroup`, it can accept the [`.flat`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#flat_1)
and [`.round`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#round) style classes.

![inline-view-switcher-style-classes](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/inline-view-switcher-style-classes.png)

## Accessibility [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.InlineViewSwitcher.html\#accessibility "Permanent link")

The internal toggle group uses the [`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_TAB_LIST`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#tab-list) role.
Its toggles use the [`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_TAB`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#tab) role.

See also: [`AdwViewSwitcher`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcher.html), [`AdwViewSwitcherBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherBar.html),
[`AdwViewSwitcherSidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherSidebar.html).

# Adw.LayoutSlot

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.LayoutSlot.html

since: 1.6

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-layout-slot.c\#L17 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.LayoutSlot : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.6

A child slot within [`AdwLayout`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Layout.html).

While it contains a layout child, the [`GtkWidget:visible`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Widget.visible.html) property
of the slot is updated to match that of the layout child.

See [`AdwMultiLayoutView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.MultiLayoutView.html).

# Adw.Leaflet

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Leaflet.html

deprecated: 1.4

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-leaflet.c\#L21 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.Leaflet : Gtk.Widget
  implements Adw.Swipeable, Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget, Gtk.Orientable {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Deprecated since: 1.4

See [the migration guide](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html#replace-adwleaflet).

An adaptive container acting like a box or a stack.

![leaflet-wide](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/leaflet-wide.png)![leaflet-narrow](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/leaflet-narrow.png)

The `AdwLeaflet` widget can display its children like a [`GtkBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Box.html) does
or like a [`GtkStack`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Stack.html) does, adapting to size changes by switching
between the two modes.

When there is enough space the children are displayed side by side, otherwise
only one is displayed and the leaflet is said to be “folded”.
The threshold is dictated by the preferred minimum sizes of the children.
When a leaflet is folded, the children can be navigated using swipe gestures.

The “over” and “under” transition types stack the children one on top of the
other, while the “slide” transition puts the children side by side. While
navigating to a child on the side or below can be performed by swiping the
current child away, navigating to an upper child requires dragging it from
the edge where it resides. This doesn’t affect non-dragging swipes.

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Leaflet.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwLeaflet` has a single CSS node with name `leaflet`. The node will get the
style classes `.folded` when it is folded, `.unfolded` when it’s not, or none
if it hasn’t computed its fold yet.

# Adw.MessageDialog

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.MessageDialog.html

deprecated: 1.6since: 1.2

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-message-dialog.c\#L18 "go to source location")

```
class Adw.MessageDialog : Gtk.Window
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget, Gtk.Native, Gtk.Root, Gtk.ShortcutManager {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.2

Deprecated since: 1.6

Use [`AdwAlertDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AlertDialog.html).

A dialog presenting a message or a question.

![message-dialog](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/message-dialog.png)

Message dialogs have a heading, a body, an optional child widget, and one or
multiple responses, each presented as a button.

Each response has a unique string ID, and a button label. Additionally, each
response can be enabled or disabled, and can have a suggested or destructive appearance.

When one of the responses is activated, or the dialog is closed, the
[`AdwMessageDialog::response`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.MessageDialog.response.html) signal will be emitted. This signal is
detailed, and the detail, as well as the `response` parameter will be set to
the ID of the activated response, or to the value of the
[`AdwMessageDialog:close-response`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.MessageDialog.close-response.html) property if the dialog had been
closed without activating any of the responses.

Response buttons can be presented horizontally or vertically depending on
available space.

When a response is activated, `AdwMessageDialog` is closed automatically.

An example of using a message dialog:

```
GtkWidget *dialog;

dialog = adw_message_dialog_new (parent, _("Replace File?"), NULL);

adw_message_dialog_format_body (ADW_MESSAGE_DIALOG (dialog),
                                _("A file named “%s” already exists. Do you want to replace it?"),
                                filename);

adw_message_dialog_add_responses (ADW_MESSAGE_DIALOG (dialog),
                                  "cancel",  _("_Cancel"),
                                  "replace", _("_Replace"),
                                  NULL);

adw_message_dialog_set_response_appearance (ADW_MESSAGE_DIALOG (dialog), "replace", ADW_RESPONSE_DESTRUCTIVE);

adw_message_dialog_set_default_response (ADW_MESSAGE_DIALOG (dialog), "cancel");
adw_message_dialog_set_close_response (ADW_MESSAGE_DIALOG (dialog), "cancel");

g_signal_connect (dialog, "response", G_CALLBACK (response_cb), self);

gtk_window_present (GTK_WINDOW (dialog));
```

Copy

## Async API [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.MessageDialog.html\#async-api "Permanent link")

`AdwMessageDialog` can also be used via the [`adw_message_dialog_choose()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.MessageDialog.choose.html)
method. This API follows the GIO async pattern, for example:

```
static void
dialog_cb (AdwMessageDialog *dialog,
           GAsyncResult     *result,
           MyWindow         *self)
{
  const char *response = adw_message_dialog_choose_finish (dialog, result);

  // ...
}

static void
show_dialog (MyWindow *self)
{
  GtkWidget *dialog;

  dialog = adw_message_dialog_new (GTK_WINDOW (self), _("Replace File?"), NULL);

  adw_message_dialog_format_body (ADW_MESSAGE_DIALOG (dialog),
                                  _("A file named “%s” already exists. Do you want to replace it?"),
                                  filename);

  adw_message_dialog_add_responses (ADW_MESSAGE_DIALOG (dialog),
                                    "cancel",  _("_Cancel"),
                                    "replace", _("_Replace"),
                                    NULL);

  adw_message_dialog_set_response_appearance (ADW_MESSAGE_DIALOG (dialog), "replace", ADW_RESPONSE_DESTRUCTIVE);

  adw_message_dialog_set_default_response (ADW_MESSAGE_DIALOG (dialog), "cancel");
  adw_message_dialog_set_close_response (ADW_MESSAGE_DIALOG (dialog), "cancel");

  adw_message_dialog_choose (ADW_MESSAGE_DIALOG (dialog), NULL, (GAsyncReadyCallback) dialog_cb, self);
}
```

## AdwMessageDialog as GtkBuildable [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.MessageDialog.html\#adwmessagedialog-as-gtkbuildable "Permanent link")

`AdwMessageDialog` supports adding responses in UI definitions by via the
`<responses>` element that may contain multiple `<response>` elements, each
representing a response.

Each of the `<response>` elements must have the `id` attribute specifying the
response ID. The contents of the element are used as the response label.

Response labels can be translated with the usual `translatable`, `context`
and `comments` attributes.

The `<response>` elements can also have `enabled` and/or `appearance`
attributes. See [`adw_message_dialog_set_response_enabled()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.MessageDialog.set_response_enabled.html) and
[`adw_message_dialog_set_response_appearance()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.MessageDialog.set_response_appearance.html) for details.

Example of an `AdwMessageDialog`UI definition:

```
<object class="AdwMessageDialog" id="dialog">
  <property name="heading" translatable="yes">Save Changes?</property>
  <property name="body" translatable="yes">Open documents contain unsaved changes. Changes which are not saved will be permanently lost.</property>
  <property name="default-response">save</property>
  <property name="close-response">cancel</property>
  <signal name="response" handler="response_cb"/>
  <responses>
    <response id="cancel" translatable="yes">_Cancel</response>
    <response id="discard" translatable="yes" appearance="destructive">_Discard</response>
    <response id="save" translatable="yes" appearance="suggested" enabled="false">_Save</response>
  </responses>
</object>
```

# Adw.MultiLayoutView

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.MultiLayoutView.html

since: 1.6

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-multi-layout-view.c\#L17 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.MultiLayoutView : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.6

A widget for switching between different layouts.

`AdwMultiLayoutView` contains layouts and children. Each child has
an ID, each layout has slots inside it, each slot also has an ID. When
switching layouts, children are inserted into slots with matching IDs. The
[`GtkWidget:visible`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Widget.visible.html) property of each slot is updated to match
that of the inserted child.

This can be useful for rearranging children when it’s difficult to do so
otherwise, for example to move a child from a sidebar to a bottom bar.

The currently used layout can be switched using the
[`AdwMultiLayoutView:layout`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.MultiLayoutView.layout.html) or [`AdwMultiLayoutView:layout-name`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.MultiLayoutView.layout-name.html)
properties. For example, it can be done via a [`AdwBreakpoint`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Breakpoint.html) setter
to change layouts depending on the window size.

## AdwMultiLayoutView as GtkBuildable [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.MultiLayoutView.html\#adwmultilayoutview-as-gtkbuildable "Permanent link")

The `AdwMultiLayoutView` implementation of the [`GtkBuildable`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/iface.Buildable.html)
interface supports adding layouts via `<child>` element with the `type`
attribute omitted.

It also supports setting children via `<child type="ID">`.

Example of an `AdwMultiLayoutView`UI definition that can display a secondary
child as either a sidebar or a bottom sheet.

```
<object class="AdwMultiLayoutView">
  <child>
    <object class="AdwLayout">
      <property name="name">sidebar</property>
      <property name="content">
        <object class="AdwOverlaySplitView">
          <property name="sidebar">
            <object class="AdwLayoutSlot">
              <property name="id">secondary</property>
            </object>
          </property>
          <property name="content">
            <object class="AdwLayoutSlot">
              <property name="id">primary</property>
            </object>
          </property>
        </object>
      </property>
    </object>
  </child>
  <child>
    <object class="AdwLayout">
      <property name="name">bottom-sheet</property>
      <property name="content">
        <object class="AdwBottomSheet">
          <property name="open">True</property>
          <property name="content">
            <object class="AdwLayoutSlot">
              <property name="id">primary</property>
            </object>
          </property>
          <property name="sheet">
            <object class="AdwLayoutSlot">
              <property name="id">secondary</property>
            </object>
          </property>
        </object>
      </property>
    </object>
  </child>
  <child type="primary">
    <!-- put your primary child here -->
  </child>
  <child type="secondary">
    <!-- put your secondary child here -->
  </child>
</object>
```

# Adw.NavigationPage

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationPage.html

since: 1.4

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-navigation-view.c\#L188 "go to source location")

```
class Adw.NavigationPage : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.4

A page within [`AdwNavigationView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationView.html) or [`AdwNavigationSplitView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationSplitView.html).

Each page has a child widget, a title and optionally a tag.

The [`AdwNavigationPage::showing`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.NavigationPage.showing.html), [`AdwNavigationPage::shown`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.NavigationPage.shown.html),
[`AdwNavigationPage::hiding`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.NavigationPage.hiding.html) and [`AdwNavigationPage::hidden`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.NavigationPage.hidden.html) signals
can be used to track the page’s visibility within its `AdwNavigationView`.

## Header Bar Integration [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationPage.html\#header-bar-integration "Permanent link")

When placed inside `AdwNavigationPage`, [`AdwHeaderBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html) will display the
page title instead of window title.

When used together with [`AdwNavigationView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationView.html), it will also display a back
button that can be used to go back to the previous page. Set
[`AdwHeaderBar:show-back-button`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.show-back-button.html) to `FALSE` to disable that behavior if
it’s unwanted.

## CSS Nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationPage.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwNavigationPage` has a single CSS node with name
`navigation-view-page`.

## Accessibility [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationPage.html\#accessibility "Permanent link")

`AdwNavigationPage` uses the [`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_GROUP`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#group) role.

# Adw.NavigationSplitView

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationSplitView.html

```
final class Adw.NavigationSplitView : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
```
