
Available since: 1.4

A widget presenting sidebar and content side by side or as a navigation view.

![navigation-split-view](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/navigation-split-view.png)![navigation-split-view-collapsed](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/navigation-split-view-collapsed.png)

`AdwNavigationSplitView` has two [`AdwNavigationPage`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationPage.html) children: sidebar and
content, and displays them side by side.

When [`AdwNavigationSplitView:collapsed`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationSplitView.collapsed.html) is set to `TRUE`, it instead
puts both children inside an [`AdwNavigationView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationView.html). The
[`AdwNavigationSplitView:show-content`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationSplitView.show-content.html) controls which child is visible
while collapsed.

See also [`AdwOverlaySplitView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.OverlaySplitView.html).

`AdwNavigationSplitView` is typically used together with an [`AdwBreakpoint`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Breakpoint.html)
setting the `collapsed` property to `TRUE` on small widths, as follows:

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <property name="default-width">800</property>
  <property name="default-height">800</property>
  <child>
    <object class="AdwBreakpoint">
      <condition>max-width: 400sp</condition>
      <setter object="split_view" property="collapsed">True</setter>
    </object>
  </child>
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwNavigationSplitView" id="split_view">
      <property name="sidebar">
        <object class="AdwNavigationPage">
          <property name="title" translatable="yes">Sidebar</property>
          <property name="child">
            <object class="AdwToolbarView">
              <child type="top">
                <object class="AdwHeaderBar"/>
              </child>
              <property name="content">
                <!-- put your sidebar here, e.g.
                     AdwSidebar or AdwViewSwitcherSidebar -->
              </property>
            <object>
          </property>
        </object>
      </property>
      <property name="content">
        <object class="AdwNavigationPage">
          <property name="title" translatable="yes">Content</property>
          <property name="child">
            <object class="AdwToolbarView">
              <child type="top">
                <object class="AdwHeaderBar"/>
              </child>
              <property name="content">
                <!-- put your content here -->
              </property>
            <object>
          </property>
        </object>
      </property>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

## Sizing [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationSplitView.html\#sizing "Permanent link")

When not collapsed, `AdwNavigationSplitView` changes the sidebar width
depending on its own width.

If possible, it tries to allocate a fraction of the total width, controlled
with the [`AdwNavigationSplitView:sidebar-width-fraction`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationSplitView.sidebar-width-fraction.html) property.

The sidebar also has minimum and maximum sizes, controlled with the
[`AdwNavigationSplitView:min-sidebar-width`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationSplitView.min-sidebar-width.html) and
[`AdwNavigationSplitView:max-sidebar-width`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationSplitView.max-sidebar-width.html) properties.

The minimum and maximum sizes are using the length unit specified with the
[`AdwNavigationSplitView:sidebar-width-unit`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationSplitView.sidebar-width-unit.html).

By default, sidebar is using 25% of the total width, with 180sp as the
minimum size and 280sp as the maximum size.

## Header Bar Integration [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationSplitView.html\#header-bar-integration "Permanent link")

When used inside `AdwNavigationSplitView`, [`AdwHeaderBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html) will
automatically hide the window buttons in the middle.

When collapsed, it also displays a back button for the content widget, as
well as the page titles. See [`AdwNavigationView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationView.html) documentation for details.

## Actions [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationSplitView.html\#actions "Permanent link")

`AdwNavigationSplitView` defines the same actions as `AdwNavigationView`, but
they can be used even when the split view is not collapsed:

- `navigation.push` takes a string parameter specifying the tag of the page
to push. If it matches the tag of the content widget, it sets
[`AdwNavigationSplitView:show-content`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationSplitView.show-content.html) to `TRUE`.

- `navigation.pop` doesn’t take any parameters and sets
[`AdwNavigationSplitView:show-content`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationSplitView.show-content.html) to `FALSE`.


## `AdwNavigationSplitView` as `GtkBuildable` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationSplitView.html\#adwnavigationsplitview-as-gtkbuildable "Permanent link")

The `AdwNavigationSplitView` implementation of the [`GtkBuildable`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/iface.Buildable.html)
interface supports setting the sidebar widget by specifying “sidebar” as the
“type” attribute of a `<child>` element, Specifying “content” child type or
omitting it results in setting the content widget.

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationSplitView.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwNavigationSplitView` has a single CSS node with the name
`navigation-split-view`.

When collapsed, it contains a child node with the name `navigation-view`
containing both children.

```
navigation-split-view
╰── navigation-view
    ├── [sidebar child]
    ╰── [content child]
```

Copy

When not collapsed, it contains two nodes with the name `widget`, one with
the `.sidebar-pane` style class, the other one with `.content-view` style
class, containing the sidebar and content children respectively.

```
navigation-split-view
├── widget.sidebar-pane
│   ╰── [sidebar child]
╰── widget.content-pane
    ╰── [content child]
```

Copy

## Accessibility [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationSplitView.html\#accessibility "Permanent link")

`AdwNavigationSplitView` uses the [`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_GROUP`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#group) role.

# Adw.NavigationView

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationView.html

since: 1.4

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-navigation-view.c\#L24 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.NavigationView : Gtk.Widget
  implements Adw.Swipeable, Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.4

A page-based navigation container.

![navigation-view](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/navigation-view.png)

`AdwNavigationView` presents one child at a time, similar to
[`GtkStack`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Stack.html).

`AdwNavigationView` can only contain [`AdwNavigationPage`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationPage.html) children.

It maintains a navigation stack that can be controlled with
[`adw_navigation_view_push()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.NavigationView.push.html) and [`adw_navigation_view_pop()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.NavigationView.pop.html). The whole
navigation stack can also be replaced using [`adw_navigation_view_replace()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.NavigationView.replace.html).

`AdwNavigationView` allows to manage pages statically or dynamically.

Static pages can be added using the [`adw_navigation_view_add()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.NavigationView.add.html) method. The
`AdwNavigationView` will keep a reference to these pages, but they aren’t
accessible to the user until [`adw_navigation_view_push()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.NavigationView.push.html) is called (except
for the first page, which is pushed automatically). Use the
[`adw_navigation_view_remove()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.NavigationView.remove.html) method to remove them. This is useful for
applications that have a small number of unique pages and just need
navigation between them.

Dynamic pages are automatically destroyed once they are popped off the
navigation stack. To add a page like this, push it using the
[`adw_navigation_view_push()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.NavigationView.push.html) method without calling
[`adw_navigation_view_add()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.NavigationView.add.html) first.

## Tags [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationView.html\#tags "Permanent link")

Static pages, as well as any pages in the navigation stack, can be accessed
by their [`AdwNavigationPage:tag`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationPage.tag.html). For example,
[`adw_navigation_view_push_by_tag()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.NavigationView.push_by_tag.html) can be used to push a static page that’s
not in the navigation stack without having to keep a reference to it manually.

## Header Bar Integration [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationView.html\#header-bar-integration "Permanent link")

When used inside `AdwNavigationView`, [`AdwHeaderBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html) will automatically
display a back button that can be used to go back to the previous page when
possible. The button also has a context menu, allowing to pop multiple pages
at once, potentially across multiple navigation views.

Set [`AdwHeaderBar:show-back-button`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.show-back-button.html) to `FALSE` to disable this behavior
in rare scenarios where it’s unwanted.

`AdwHeaderBar` will also display the title of the `AdwNavigationPage` it’s
placed into, so most applications shouldn’t need to customize it at all.

## Shortcuts and Gestures [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationView.html\#shortcuts-and-gestures "Permanent link")

`AdwNavigationView` supports the following shortcuts for going to the
previous page:

- `Escape` (unless [`AdwNavigationView:pop-on-escape`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationView.pop-on-escape.html) is set to
`FALSE`)
- `Alt` + `←`
- Back mouse button

Additionally, it supports interactive gestures:

- One-finger swipe towards the right on touchscreens
- Scrolling towards the right on touchpads (usually two-finger swipe)

These gestures have transitions enabled regardless of the
[`AdwNavigationView:animate-transitions`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationView.animate-transitions.html) value.

Applications can also enable shortcuts for pushing another page onto the
navigation stack via connecting to the [`AdwNavigationView::get-next-page`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.NavigationView.get-next-page.html)
signal, in that case the following shortcuts are supported:

- `Alt` + `→`
- Forward mouse button
- Swipe/scrolling towards the left

For right-to-left locales, the gestures and shortcuts are reversed.

[`AdwNavigationPage:can-pop`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationPage.can-pop.html) can be used to disable them, along with the
header bar back buttons.

## Actions [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationView.html\#actions "Permanent link")

`AdwNavigationView` defines actions for controlling the navigation stack.
actions for controlling the navigation stack:

- `navigation.push` takes a string parameter specifying the tag of the page to
push, and is equivalent to calling [`adw_navigation_view_push_by_tag()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.NavigationView.push_by_tag.html).

- `navigation.pop` doesn’t take any parameters and pops the current page from
the navigation stack, equivalent to calling [`adw_navigation_view_pop()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.NavigationView.pop.html).


## `AdwNavigationView` as `GtkBuildable` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationView.html\#adwnavigationview-as-gtkbuildable "Permanent link")

`AdwNavigationView` allows to add pages as children, equivalent to using the
[`adw_navigation_view_add()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.NavigationView.add.html) method.

Example of an `AdwNavigationView`UI definition:

```
<object class="AdwNavigationView">
  <child>
    <object class="AdwNavigationPage">
      <property name="title" translatable="yes">Page 1</property>
      <property name="child">
        <object class="AdwToolbarView">
          <child type="top">
            <object class="AdwHeaderBar"/>
          </child>
          <property name="content">
            <object class="GtkButton">
              <property name="label" translatable="yes">Open Page 2</property>
              <property name="halign">center</property>
              <property name="valign">center</property>
              <property name="action-name">navigation.push</property>
              <property name="action-target">'page-2'</property>
              <style>
                <class name="pill"/>
               </style>
            </object>
          </property>
        </object>
      </property>
    </object>
  </child>
  <child>
    <object class="AdwNavigationPage">
      <property name="title" translatable="yes">Page 2</property>
      <property name="tag">page-2</property>
      <property name="child">
        <object class="AdwToolbarView">
          <child type="top">
            <object class="AdwHeaderBar"/>
          </child>
          <property name="content">
            <!-- put your content here -->
          </property>
        </object>
      </property>
    </object>
  </child>
</object>
```

# Adw.OverlaySplitView

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.OverlaySplitView.html

since: 1.4

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-overlay-split-view.c\#L24 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.OverlaySplitView : Gtk.Widget
  implements Adw.Swipeable, Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.4

A widget presenting sidebar and content side by side or as an overlay.

![overlay-split-view](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/overlay-split-view.png)![overlay-split-view-collapsed](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/overlay-split-view-collapsed.png)

`AdwOverlaySplitView` has two children: sidebar and content, and displays
them side by side.

When [`AdwOverlaySplitView:collapsed`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.OverlaySplitView.collapsed.html) is set to `TRUE`, the sidebar is
instead shown as an overlay above the content widget.

The sidebar can be hidden or shown using the
[`AdwOverlaySplitView:show-sidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.OverlaySplitView.show-sidebar.html) property.

Sidebar can be displayed before or after the content, this can be controlled
with the [`AdwOverlaySplitView:sidebar-position`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.OverlaySplitView.sidebar-position.html) property.

Collapsing the split view automatically hides the sidebar widget, and
uncollapsing it shows the sidebar. If this behavior is not desired, the
[`AdwOverlaySplitView:pin-sidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.OverlaySplitView.pin-sidebar.html) property can be used to override it.

`AdwOverlaySplitView` supports an edge swipe gesture for showing the sidebar,
and a swipe from the sidebar for hiding it. Gestures are only supported on
touchscreen, but not touchpad. Gestures can be controlled with the
[`AdwOverlaySplitView:enable-show-gesture`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.OverlaySplitView.enable-show-gesture.html) and
[`AdwOverlaySplitView:enable-hide-gesture`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.OverlaySplitView.enable-hide-gesture.html) properties.

See also [`AdwNavigationSplitView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationSplitView.html).

`AdwOverlaySplitView` is typically used together with an [`AdwBreakpoint`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Breakpoint.html)
setting the `collapsed` property to `TRUE` on small widths, as follows:

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <property name="default-width">800</property>
  <property name="default-height">800</property>
  <child>
    <object class="AdwBreakpoint">
      <condition>max-width: 400sp</condition>
      <setter object="split_view" property="collapsed">True</setter>
    </object>
  </child>
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwOverlaySplitView" id="split_view">
      <property name="sidebar">
        <!-- put your sidebar here -->
      </property>
      <property name="content">
        <!-- put your content here -->
      </property>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

`AdwOverlaySplitView` is often used for implementing the
[utility pane](https://developer.gnome.org/hig/patterns/containers/utility-panes.html) pattern.

## Sizing [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.OverlaySplitView.html\#sizing "Permanent link")

When not collapsed, `AdwOverlaySplitView` changes the sidebar width
depending on its own width.

If possible, it tries to allocate a fraction of the total width, controlled
with the [`AdwOverlaySplitView:sidebar-width-fraction`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.OverlaySplitView.sidebar-width-fraction.html) property.

The sidebar also has minimum and maximum sizes, controlled with the
[`AdwOverlaySplitView:min-sidebar-width`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.OverlaySplitView.min-sidebar-width.html) and
[`AdwOverlaySplitView:max-sidebar-width`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.OverlaySplitView.max-sidebar-width.html) properties.

The minimum and maximum sizes are using the length unit specified with the
[`AdwOverlaySplitView:sidebar-width-unit`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.OverlaySplitView.sidebar-width-unit.html).

By default, sidebar is using 25% of the total width, with 180sp as the
minimum size and 280sp as the maximum size.

When collapsed, the preferred width fraction is ignored and the sidebar uses
[`AdwOverlaySplitView:max-sidebar-width`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.OverlaySplitView.max-sidebar-width.html) when possible.

## Header Bar Integration [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.OverlaySplitView.html\#header-bar-integration "Permanent link")

When used inside `AdwOverlaySplitView`, [`AdwHeaderBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html) will automatically
hide the window buttons in the middle.

## `AdwOverlaySplitView` as `GtkBuildable` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.OverlaySplitView.html\#adwoverlaysplitview-as-gtkbuildable "Permanent link")

The `AdwOverlaySplitView` implementation of the [`GtkBuildable`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/iface.Buildable.html)
interface supports setting the sidebar widget by specifying “sidebar” as the
“type” attribute of a `<child>` element, Specifying “content” child type or
omitting it results in setting the content widget.

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.OverlaySplitView.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwOverlaySplitView` has a single CSS node with the name
`overlay-split-view`.

It contains two nodes with the name `widget`, containing the sidebar and
content children.

When not collapsed, they have the `.sidebar-view` and `.content-view` style
classes respectively.

```
overlay-split-view
├── widget.sidebar-pane
│   ╰── [sidebar child]
╰── widget.content-pane
    ╰── [content child]
```

Copy

When collapsed, the one containing the sidebar child has the `.overlay-pane`
style class and the other one has no style classes.

```
overlay-split-view
├── widget.overlay-pane
│   ╰── [sidebar child]
╰── widget
    ╰── [content child]
```

Copy

# Adw.PasswordEntryRow

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PasswordEntryRow.html

since: 1.2

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-password-entry-row.c\#L15 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.PasswordEntryRow : Adw.EntryRow
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Actionable, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget, Gtk.Editable {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.2

A [`AdwEntryRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.EntryRow.html) tailored for entering secrets.

![password-entry-row](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/password-entry-row.png)

It does not show its contents in clear text, does not allow to copy it to the
clipboard, and shows a warning when Caps Lock is engaged. If the underlying
platform allows it, `AdwPasswordEntryRow` will also place the text in a
non-pageable memory area, to avoid it being written out to disk by the
operating system.

It offer a way to reveal the contents in clear text.

## CSS Nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PasswordEntryRow.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwPasswordEntryRow` has a single CSS node with name `row` that carries
`.entry` and `.password` style classes.

# Adw.PreferencesDialog

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesDialog.html

since: 1.5

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-preferences-dialog.c\#L26 "go to source location")

```
class Adw.PreferencesDialog : Adw.Dialog
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget, Gtk.ShortcutManager {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.5

A dialog showing application’s preferences.

![preferences-dialog](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/preferences-dialog.png)

The `AdwPreferencesDialog` widget presents an application’s preferences
gathered into pages and groups. The preferences are searchable by the user.

## Actions [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesDialog.html\#actions "Permanent link")

`AdwPrefencesDialog` defines the `navigation.pop` action, it doesn’t take any
parameters and pops the current subpage from the navigation stack, equivalent
to calling [`adw_preferences_dialog_pop_subpage()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.PreferencesDialog.pop_subpage.html).

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesDialog.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwPreferencesDialog` has a main CSS node with the name `dialog` and the
style class `.preferences`.

```
class Adw.PreferencesGroup : Gtk.Widget

```

A group of preference rows.

![preferences-group](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/preferences-group.png)

An `AdwPreferencesGroup` represents a group or tightly related preferences,
which in turn are represented by [`AdwPreferencesRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesRow.html).

To summarize the role of the preferences it gathers, a group can have both a
title and a description. The title will be used by [`AdwPreferencesDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesDialog.html)
to let the user look for a preference.

The [`AdwPreferencesGroup:separate-rows`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.PreferencesGroup.separate-rows.html) property can be used to
separate the rows within the group, same as when using the
[`.boxed-list-separate`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#boxed-lists-cards) style class
instead of `.boxed-list`.

## AdwPreferencesGroup as GtkBuildable [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesGroup.html\#adwpreferencesgroup-as-gtkbuildable "Permanent link")

The `AdwPreferencesGroup` implementation of the [`GtkBuildable`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/iface.Buildable.html) interface
supports adding [`AdwPreferencesRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesRow.html) s to the list by omitting “type”. If “type”
is omitted and the widget isn’t a [`AdwPreferencesRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesRow.html) the child is added to
a box below the list.

When the “type” attribute of a child is `header-suffix`, the child
is set as the suffix on the end of the title and description.

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesGroup.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwPreferencesGroup` has a single CSS node with name `preferencesgroup`.

## Accessibility [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesGroup.html\#accessibility "Permanent link")

`AdwPreferencesGroup` uses the [`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_GROUP`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#group) role.

# Adw.PreferencesRow

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesRow.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-preferences-row.c\#L11 "go to source location")

```
class Adw.PreferencesRow : Gtk.ListBoxRow
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Actionable, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A [`GtkListBoxRow`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListBoxRow.html) used to present preferences.

The `AdwPreferencesRow` widget has a title that [`AdwPreferencesDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesDialog.html)
will use to let the user look for a preference. It doesn’t present the title
in any way and lets you present the preference as you please.

[`AdwActionRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ActionRow.html) and its derivatives are convenient to use as preference
rows as they take care of presenting the preference’s title while letting you
compose the inputs of the preference around it.

\[−\]

# Adw.PreferencesWindow

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesWindow.html

deprecated: 1.6

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-preferences-window.c\#L26 "go to source location")

```
class Adw.PreferencesWindow : Adw.Window
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget, Gtk.Native, Gtk.Root, Gtk.ShortcutManager {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Deprecated since: 1.6

Use [`AdwPreferencesDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesDialog.html).

A window to present an application’s preferences.

![preferences-window](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/preferences-window.png)

The `AdwPreferencesWindow` widget presents an application’s preferences
gathered into pages and groups. The preferences are searchable by the user.

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesWindow.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwPreferencesWindow` has a main CSS node with the name `window` and the
style class `.preferences`.

# Adw.ShortcutLabel

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ShortcutLabel.html

since: 1.8

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-shortcut-label.c\#L24 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.ShortcutLabel : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.8

A widget that displays a keyboard shortcut.

![shortcut-label](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/shortcut-label.png)

The shown shortcut can be set using the [`AdwShortcutLabel:accelerator`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ShortcutLabel.accelerator.html) property.

Optionally, if no shortcut is set, `AdwShortcutLabel` will display a
placeholder set with the [`AdwShortcutLabel:disabled-text`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ShortcutLabel.disabled-text.html) property.

The following types of shortcuts can be displayed:

- A single shortcut in [`gtk_accelerator_parse()`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/func.accelerator_parse.html) format, e.g. `<Control>C`:

![shortcut-label-single](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/shortcut-label-single.png)

- Multiple alternative shortcuts, separated with spaces, e.g. `<Shift>A Home`:

![shortcut-label-alternative](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/shortcut-label-alternative.png)

- A range of shortcuts, separated with `...`, e.g. `<Alt>1...9`:

![shortcut-label-range](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/shortcut-label-range.png)

- Multiple keys pressed at once, separated with `&`, e.g. `Control_L&Control_R`:

![shortcut-label-multiple](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/shortcut-label-multiple.png)

- Multiple shortcuts or keys, pressed sequentially, separated with `+`, e.g. `<Control>C+<Control>X`:

![shortcut-label-sequence](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/shortcut-label-sequence.png)


Note

`<`, `>` and `&` need to be escaped as `&lt;`, `&gt;` and `&amp;` when used in UI files.

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ShortcutLabel.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwShortcutLabel` has a single CSS node with name `shortcut-label`. The
individual keycap labels each have the `.keycap` style class, while the
labels separating them have the `.dimmed` style class.

## Accessibility [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ShortcutLabel.html\#accessibility "Permanent link")

`AdwShortcutLabel` uses the [`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_LABEL`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#label) role.

See also: [`AdwShortcutsDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ShortcutsDialog.html).

# Adw.ShortcutsDialog

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ShortcutsDialog.html

since: 1.8

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-shortcuts-dialog.c\#L24 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.ShortcutsDialog : Adw.Dialog
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget, Gtk.ShortcutManager {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.8

A dialog that displays application’s keyboard shortcuts.

![shortcuts-dialog](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/shortcuts-dialog.png)

Shortcuts are grouped into sections, represented by [`AdwShortcutsSection`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ShortcutsSection.html)
objects. Each section has one or more items, represented by
[`AdwShortcutsItem`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ShortcutsItem.html) objects.

To add a section to the dialog, use [`adw_shortcuts_dialog_add()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.ShortcutsDialog.add.html), or add it
as a child when using UI files.

Sections without titles can be used to further subdivide each section into groups.

Example of an `AdwShortcutsDialog`UI definition:

```
<object class="AdwShortcutsDialog" id="shortcuts_dialog">
  <child>
    <object class="AdwShortcutsSection">
      <property name="title" translatable="yes">General</property>
      <child>
        <object class="AdwShortcutsItem">
          <property name="title" translatable="yes">Open Menu</property>
          <property name="accelerator">F10</property>
        </object>
      </child>
      <child>
        <object class="AdwShortcutsItem">
          <property name="title" translatable="yes">Quit</property>
          <property name="action-name">app.quit</property>
        </object>
      </child>
    </object>
  </child>
  <child>
    <object class="AdwShortcutsSection">
      <child>
        <object class="AdwShortcutsItem">
          <property name="title" translatable="yes">Move Tab Left</property>
          <property name="accelerator">&lt;Shift&gt;&lt;Ctrl&gt;Page_Up</property>
          <property name="direction">ltr</property>
        </object>
      </child>
      <child>
        <object class="AdwShortcutsItem">
          <property name="title" translatable="yes">Move Tab Right</property>
          <property name="accelerator">&lt;Shift&gt;&lt;Ctrl&gt;Page_Down</property>
          <property name="direction">ltr</property>
        </object>
      </child>
      <child>
        <object class="AdwShortcutsItem">
          <property name="title" translatable="yes">Move Tab Right</property>
          <property name="accelerator">&lt;Shift&gt;&lt;Ctrl&gt;Page_Up</property>
          <property name="direction">rtl</property>
        </object>
      </child>
      <child>
        <object class="AdwShortcutsItem">
          <property name="title" translatable="yes">Move Tab Left</property>
          <property name="accelerator">&lt;Shift&gt;&lt;Ctrl&gt;Page_Down</property>
          <property name="direction">rtl</property>
        </object>
      </child>
    </object>
  </child>
</object>
```

Copy

If the `app.quit` action has the `Ctrl`  `Q` accelerator
associated with it, the result will look as follows:

![shortcuts-dialog-example](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/shortcuts-dialog-example.png)

The recommended way to use `AdwShortcutsDialog` is via [`AdwApplication`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Application.html)‘s
automatic resource loading.

See also: [`AdwShortcutLabel`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ShortcutLabel.html).

# Adw.ShortcutsItem

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ShortcutsItem.html

since: 1.8

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-shortcuts-item.c\#L13 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.ShortcutsItem : GObject.Object
{
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.8

An object representing an individual shortcut in [`AdwShortcutsSection`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ShortcutsSection.html).

A shortcut has a title, an optional subtitle, and an accelerator.

Accelerator must be specified in the format [`AdwShortcutLabel`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ShortcutLabel.html) accepts.

Alternatively, the [`AdwShortcutsItem:action-name`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ShortcutsItem.action-name.html) property can be used
to automatically get accelerator associated with the specified action, as set
via [`gtk_application_set_accels_for_action()`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/method.Application.set_accels_for_action.html).

If both are specified, the accelerator will be used if the action couldn’t
be found or doesn’t have an accelerator associated for it.

If [`AdwShortcutsItem:direction`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ShortcutsItem.direction.html) is set, the shortcut will only be
displayed for the specified text direction. This allows to display different
shortcuts for different text directions.

# Adw.ShortcutsSection

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ShortcutsSection.html

since: 1.8

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-shortcuts-section.c\#L15 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.ShortcutsSection : GObject.Object
  implements Gio.ListModel, Gtk.Buildable {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.8

An object representing a section in [`AdwShortcutsDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ShortcutsDialog.html).

It contains [`AdwShortcutsItem`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ShortcutsItem.html) objects, use [`adw_shortcuts_section_add()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.ShortcutsSection.add.html) to
add them.

`AdwShortcutsSection` implements the [`GListModel`](https://docs.gtk.org/gio/iface.ListModel.html) interface and
allows to access the added shortcut items through it.

## `AdwShortcutsSection` as `GtkBuildable` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ShortcutsSection.html\#adwshortcutssection-as-gtkbuildable "Permanent link")

`AdwShortcutsSection` allows adding `AdwShortcutsItem` objects as children.

```
final class Adw.Sidebar : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */

```

Available since: 1.9

Adaptive sidebar widget.

![sidebar](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/sidebar.png)

`AdwSidebar` contains [`AdwSidebarSection`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SidebarSection.html) objects, which in turn contain
[`AdwSidebarItem`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SidebarItem.html) objects.

To add sections, use [`adw_sidebar_append()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Sidebar.append.html), [`adw_sidebar_prepend()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Sidebar.prepend.html) or
[`adw_sidebar_insert()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Sidebar.insert.html).

To remove sections, use [`adw_sidebar_remove()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Sidebar.remove.html) or
[`adw_sidebar_remove_all()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Sidebar.remove_all.html).

To inspect the items, use [`adw_sidebar_get_item()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Sidebar.get_item.html) or
[`AdwSidebar:items`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Sidebar.items.html).

To inspect sections themselves, use [`adw_sidebar_get_section()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Sidebar.get_section.html) or
[`AdwSidebar:sections`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Sidebar.sections.html).

## Selection and activation [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Sidebar.html\#selection-and-activation "Permanent link")

`AdwSidebar` has zero or one selected items. The index of the item can be
accessed and changed via [`AdwSidebar:selected`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Sidebar.selected.html). Set it to
[`GTK_INVALID_LIST_POSITION`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/const.INVALID_LIST_POSITION.html) to remove selection.

Selection cannot be permanently disabled.

[`AdwSidebar:selected-item`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Sidebar.selected-item.html) can be used to access the selected item.

Connect to the [`AdwSidebar::activated`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.Sidebar.activated.html) signal to run code when an item
has been activated. This can be used to toggle the visible pane when used in
a split view.

See also: [`AdwViewSwitcherSidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherSidebar.html).

## Modes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Sidebar.html\#modes "Permanent link")

![sidebar-modes](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/sidebar-modes.png)

`AdwSidebar` is adaptive and can act as either a regular sidebar, or a page
of boxed lists.

Use the [`AdwSidebar:mode`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Sidebar.mode.html) to determine its look and behavior.

A typical use case involves using `AdwSidebar` inside the sidebar pane of a
[`AdwNavigationSplitView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationSplitView.html), and switching mode to page whenever it’s
collapsed, as follows:

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <property name="default-width">800</property>
  <property name="default-height">600</property>
  <child>
    <object class="AdwBreakpoint">
      <condition>max-width: 400sp</condition>
      <setter object="split_view" property="collapsed">True</setter>
      <setter object="sidebar" property="mode">page</setter>
    </object>
  </child>
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwNavigationSplitView" id="split_view">
      <property name="sidebar">
        <object class="AdwNavigationPage">
          <property name="title" translatable="yes">Items</property>
          <property name="child">
            <object class="AdwToolbarView">
              <child type="top">
                <object class="AdwHeaderBar"/>
              </child>
              <property name="content">
                <object class="AdwSidebar" id="sidebar">
                  <!-- Calls adw_navigation_split_view_set_show_content (split_view, TRUE); -->
                  <signal name="activated" handler="sidebar_activated_cb"/>
                  <!-- put your items here -->
                </object>
              </property>
            </object>
          </property>
        </object>
      </property>
      <property name="content">
        <object class="AdwNavigationPage">
          <property name="title" translatable="yes">Details</property>
          <property name="child">
            <!-- put your details view here -->
          </property>
        </object>
      </property>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

When used with [`AdwOverlaySplitView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.OverlaySplitView.html), the sidebar should stay in sidebar
mode, as the sidebar pane is still a sidebar when collapsed.

## Search [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Sidebar.html\#search "Permanent link")

`AdwSidebar` supports filtering items via the [`AdwSidebar:filter`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Sidebar.filter.html) property.

Use [`AdwSidebar:placeholder`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Sidebar.placeholder.html) to provide an empty state widget. It will
be shown when all items have been filtered out, or the sidebar has no items otherwise.

## Context Menu [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Sidebar.html\#context-menu "Permanent link")

To create a context menu for the sidebar items, use the
[`AdwSidebar:menu-model`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Sidebar.menu-model.html) property to provide a menu model, and the
[`AdwSidebar::setup-menu`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.Sidebar.setup-menu.html) signal to set up actions for the given item.

To set or override the menu for just one section, use
[`AdwSidebarSection:menu-model`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SidebarSection.menu-model.html) instead.

## Drag-and-Drop [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Sidebar.html\#drag-and-drop "Permanent link")

`AdwSidebar` items can have a drop target for arbitrary content.

Use [`adw_sidebar_setup_drop_target()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Sidebar.setup_drop_target.html) to set it up, specifying the
supported content types and drag actions, then connect to
[`AdwSidebar::drop`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.Sidebar.drop.html) to handle drops.

In some cases, it may be necessary to determine the used action based on the
dragged content, or the hovered item.

To determine it based on the sidebar item, connect to the
[`AdwSidebar::drop-enter`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.Sidebar.drop-enter.html) signal and return the action from its handler.

To determine it based on the content, set [`AdwSidebar:drop-preload`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Sidebar.drop-preload.html) to
`TRUE`, then connect to [`AdwSidebar::drop-value-loaded`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.Sidebar.drop-value-loaded.html) signal and return
the action from its handler.

In both cases the action will be passed as a parameter to the
[`AdwSidebar::drop`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.Sidebar.drop.html) signal.

Regardless of whether a drop target was set up, dragging content over sidebar
items activates them after a timeout. To disable this behavior for specific
items, set [`AdwSidebarItem:drag-motion-activate`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SidebarItem.drag-motion-activate.html) to `FALSE` on them.

## Prefix and Suffix [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Sidebar.html\#prefix-and-suffix "Permanent link")

`AdwSidebar` can display additional widgets before and after the sidebar
items. Use the [`AdwSidebar:prefix`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Sidebar.prefix.html) and [`AdwSidebar:suffix`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Sidebar.suffix.html)
properties to add them.

## `AdwSidebar` as `GtkBuildable` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Sidebar.html\#adwsidebar-as-gtkbuildable "Permanent link")

`AdwSidebar` allows adding sections as children.

Example of an `AdwSidebar`UI definition:

```
<object class="AdwSidebar">
  <child>
    <object class="AdwSidebarSection">
      <child>
        <object class="AdwSidebarItem">
          <property name="title" translatable="yes">Recent</property>
          <property name="icon-name">document-open-recent-symbolic</property>
        </object>
      </child>
      <child>
        <object class="AdwSidebarItem">
          <property name="title" translatable="yes">Starred</property>
          <property name="icon-name">starred-symbolic</property>
        </object>
      </child>
    </object>
  </child>
  <child>
    <object class="AdwSidebarSection">
      <property name="title" translatable="yes">Places</property>
      <child>
        <object class="AdwSidebarItem">
          <property name="title" translatable="yes">Music</property>
          <property name="icon-name">folder-music-symbolic</property>
        </object>
      </child>
      <child>
        <object class="AdwSidebarItem">
          <property name="title" translatable="yes">Pictures</property>
          <property name="icon-name">folder-pictures-symbolic</property>
        </object>
      </child>
      <child>
        <object class="AdwSidebarItem">
          <property name="title" translatable="yes">Videos</property>
          <property name="icon-name">folder-videos-symbolic</property>
        </object>
      </child>
    </object>
  </child>
  <child>
    <object class="AdwSidebarSection">
      <child>
        <object class="AdwSidebarItem">
          <property name="title" translatable="yes">Trash</property>
          <property name="icon-name">user-trash-symbolic</property>
        </object>
      </child>
    </object>
  </child>
</object>
```

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Sidebar.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwSidebar` has a main CSS node with the name `sidebar`.

Internally, it’s using a [`GtkListBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListBox.html) with the
[`.navigation-sidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#sidebars) style class in sidebar
mode, or an [`AdwPreferencesPage`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesPage.html) in page mode.

## Accessibility [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Sidebar.html\#accessibility "Permanent link")

`AdwSidebar` uses the [`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_GENERIC`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#generic) role.

# Adw.SidebarItem

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SidebarItem.html

since: 1.9

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-sidebar-item.c\#L15 "go to source location")

```
class Adw.SidebarItem : GObject.Object
{
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.9

An item within [`AdwSidebarSection`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SidebarSection.html).

Sidebar items must have a title, set via [`AdwSidebarItem:title`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SidebarItem.title.html).

Sidebar items should, but are not required to, have an icon. Icons can be set
from an icon name, via [`AdwSidebarItem:icon-name`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SidebarItem.icon-name.html), or a
[`GdkPaintable`](https://docs.gtk.org/gdk4/iface.Paintable.html), via [`AdwSidebarItem:icon-paintable`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SidebarItem.icon-paintable.html).

Items can also have subtitles, set with the [`AdwSidebarItem:subtitle`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SidebarItem.subtitle.html)
property. Subtitles should be used sparingly.

To add a tooltip, use [`AdwSidebarItem:tooltip`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SidebarItem.tooltip.html). Tooltips always use
Pango markup.

Items can have an arbitrary prefix and suffix widgets, set with the
[`AdwSidebarItem:prefix`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SidebarItem.prefix.html) and [`AdwSidebarItem:suffix`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SidebarItem.suffix.html) properties.
They will be displayed at the start (before icon) and end of its row, and
before the arrow in the [`ADW_SIDEBAR_MODE_PAGE`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.SidebarMode.html#page) mode.

To hide or disable the item, use the [`AdwSidebarItem:visible`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SidebarItem.visible.html) and
[`AdwSidebarItem:enabled`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SidebarItem.enabled.html) properties respectively.

To access the items’s section, use [`AdwSidebarItem:section`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SidebarItem.section.html).

It’s also possible to access the index of the item in both the section and
the sidebar, using [`adw_sidebar_item_get_section_index()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.SidebarItem.get_section_index.html) and
[`adw_sidebar_item_get_index()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.SidebarItem.get_index.html) respectively.

Dragging content over sidebar items activates them by default. To disable
this behavior, set [`AdwSidebarItem:drag-motion-activate`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SidebarItem.drag-motion-activate.html) to `FALSE`.

`AdwSidebarItem` is derivable, and applications that need to associate each
page with data can store it in the items themselves this way.

# Adw.SidebarSection

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SidebarSection.html

since: 1.9

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-sidebar-section.c\#L15 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.SidebarSection : GObject.Object
  implements Gtk.Buildable {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.9

A section within [`AdwSidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Sidebar.html).

`AdwSidebarSection` contains [`AdwSidebarItem`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SidebarItem.html) objects.

Section can optionally have a title, set with the
[`AdwSidebarSection:title`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SidebarSection.title.html) property. If a title is not set, the section
will have a separator in front of it, or just spacing in the
[`ADW_SIDEBAR_MODE_PAGE`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.SidebarMode.html#page) mode.

Sections can also have an arbitrary suffix widget, set with the
[`AdwSidebarSection:suffix`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SidebarSection.suffix.html) properties. It will be displayed at the end
of its header.

To add items, use [`adw_sidebar_section_append()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.SidebarSection.append.html),
[`adw_sidebar_section_prepend()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.SidebarSection.prepend.html) or [`adw_sidebar_section_insert()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.SidebarSection.insert.html).

To remove items, use [`adw_sidebar_section_remove()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.SidebarSection.remove.html) or
[`adw_sidebar_section_remove_all()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.SidebarSection.remove_all.html).

To inspect the items, use [`adw_sidebar_section_get_item()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.SidebarSection.get_item.html) or
[`AdwSidebarSection:items`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SidebarSection.items.html).

To get the sidebar the section is in, use [`AdwSidebarSection:sidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SidebarSection.sidebar.html).

## Binding models [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SidebarSection.html\#binding-models "Permanent link")

`AdwSidebarSection` can show items from a provided [`GListModel`](https://docs.gtk.org/gio/iface.ListModel.html),
using [`adw_sidebar_section_bind_model()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.SidebarSection.bind_model.html). It works the same way as
[`gtk_list_box_bind_model()`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/method.ListBox.bind_model.html), except the provided function creates an
[`AdwSidebarItem`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SidebarItem.html) rather than a [`GtkListBoxRow`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListBoxRow.html).

While a model is bound, adding or removing items manually is not allowed.
Inspecting them is still allowed, but discouraged.

## `AdwSidebarSection` as `GtkBuildable` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SidebarSection.html\#adwsidebarsection-as-gtkbuildable "Permanent link")

`AdwSidebarSection` allows adding items as children.

Example of an `AdwSidebarSection`UI definition:

```
<object class="AdwSidebarSection">
  <property name="title" translatable="yes">Places</property>
  <child>
    <object class="AdwSidebarItem">
      <property name="title" translatable="yes">Music</property>
      <property name="icon-name">folder-music-symbolic</property>
    </object>
  </child>
  <child>
    <object class="AdwSidebarItem">
      <property name="title" translatable="yes">Pictures</property>
      <property name="icon-name">folder-pictures-symbolic</property>
    </object>
  </child>
  <child>
    <object class="AdwSidebarItem">
      <property name="title" translatable="yes">Videos</property>
      <property name="icon-name">folder-videos-symbolic</property>
    </object>
  </child>
</object>
```

# Adw.Spinner

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Spinner.html

since: 1.6

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-spinner.c\#L17 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.Spinner : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.6

A widget showing a loading spinner.

![spinner](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/spinner.png)

The size of the spinner depends on the available size, never smaller than
16×16 pixels and never larger than 64×64 pixels.

Use the [`GtkWidget:halign`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Widget.halign.html) and [`GtkWidget:valign`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Widget.valign.html)
properties in combination with [`GtkWidget:width-request`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Widget.width-request.html) and
[`GtkWidget:height-request`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Widget.height-request.html) for fine sizing control.

For example, the following snippet shows the spinner at 48×48 pixels:

```
<object class="AdwSpinner">
  <property name="halign">center</property>
  <property name="valign">center</property>
  <property name="width-request">48</property>
  <property name="height-request">48</property>
</object>
```

Copy

See [`AdwSpinnerPaintable`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SpinnerPaintable.html) for cases where using a widget is impractical or
impossible, such as [`AdwStatusPage:paintable`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.StatusPage.paintable.html).

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Spinner.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwSpinner` has a single node with the name `image` and the style class
`.spinner`.

## Accessibility [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Spinner.html\#accessibility "Permanent link")

`AdwSpinner` uses the [`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_PROGRESS_BAR`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#progress-bar) role.

# Adw.SpinnerPaintable

```
final class Adw.SpinnerPaintable : GObject.Object
  implements Gdk.Paintable, Gtk.SymbolicPaintable {
```

Available since: 1.6

A paintable showing a loading spinner.

![spinner](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/spinner.png)

`AdwSpinnerPaintable` size varies depending on the available space, but is
capped at 64×64 pixels.

To be able to animate, `AdwSpinnerPaintable` needs a widget. It will be
animated according to that widget’s frame clock, and only if that widget is
mapped. Ideally it should be the same widget the paintable is displayed in,
but that’s not a requirement.

Most applications should be using [`AdwSpinner`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Spinner.html) instead.
`AdwSpinnerPaintable` is provided for the cases where using a widget is
impractical or impossible, such as [`AdwStatusPage:paintable`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.StatusPage.paintable.html):

```
<object class="AdwStatusPage" id="status_page">
  <property name="paintable">
    <object class="AdwSpinnerPaintable">
      <property name="widget">status_page</property>
    </object>
  </property>
  <!-- ... -->
</object>
```

Copy

# Adw.SpinRow

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SpinRow.html

since: 1.4

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-spin-row.c\#L19 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.SpinRow : Adw.ActionRow
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Actionable, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget, Gtk.Editable {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.4

An [`AdwActionRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ActionRow.html) with an embedded spin button.

![spin-row](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/spin-row.png)

Example of an `AdwSpinRow`UI definition:

```
<object class="AdwSpinRow">
  <property name="title" translatable="yes">Spin Row</property>
  <property name="adjustment">
    <object class="GtkAdjustment">
      <property name="lower">0</property>
      <property name="upper">100</property>
      <property name="value">50</property>
      <property name="page-increment">10</property>
      <property name="step-increment">1</property>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

See [`GtkSpinButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.SpinButton.html) for details.

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SpinRow.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwSpinRow` has the same structure as [`AdwActionRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ActionRow.html), as well as the
`.spin` style class on the main node.

## Accessibility [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SpinRow.html\#accessibility "Permanent link")

`AdwSpinRow` uses an internal `GtkSpinButton` with the
[`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_SPIN_BUTTON`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#spin-button) role.

# Adw.SplitButton

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SplitButton.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-split-button.c\#L16 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.SplitButton : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Actionable, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A combined button and dropdown widget.

![split-button](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/split-button.png)

`AdwSplitButton` is typically used to present a set of actions in a menu,
but allow access to one of them with a single click.

The API is very similar to [`GtkButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Button.html) and [`GtkMenuButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.MenuButton.html), see
their documentation for details.

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SplitButton.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

```
splitbutton[.image-button][.text-button]
├── button
│   ╰── <content>
├── separator
╰── menubutton
    ╰── button.toggle
        ╰── arrow
```

Copy

`AdwSplitButton`‘s CSS node is called `splitbutton`. It contains the css
nodes: `button`, `separator`, `menubutton`. See [`GtkMenuButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.MenuButton.html)
documentation for the `menubutton` contents.

The main CSS node will contain the `.image-button` or `.text-button` style
classes matching the button contents. The nested button nodes will never
contain them.

## Style classes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SplitButton.html\#style-classes "Permanent link")

`AdwSplitButton` can use some of the same style classes as [`GtkButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Button.html):

- [`.suggested-action`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#suggested-action)
- [`.destructive-action`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#destructive-action)
- [`.flat`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#flat)
- [`.raised`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#raised)

Other style classes, like `.pill`, cannot be used.

## Accessibility [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SplitButton.html\#accessibility "Permanent link")

`AdwSplitButton` uses the [`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_GROUP`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#group) role.

\[−\]

# Adw.SpringAnimation

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SpringAnimation.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-spring-animation.c\#L18 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.SpringAnimation : Adw.Animation
{
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A spring-based [`AdwAnimation`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Animation.html).

`AdwSpringAnimation` implements an animation driven by a physical model of a
spring described by [`AdwSpringParams`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/struct.SpringParams.html), with a resting position in
[`AdwSpringAnimation:value-to`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SpringAnimation.value-to.html), stretched to
[`AdwSpringAnimation:value-from`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SpringAnimation.value-from.html).

Since the animation is physically simulated, spring animations don’t have a
fixed duration. The animation will stop when the simulated spring comes to a
rest - when the amplitude of the oscillations becomes smaller than
[`AdwSpringAnimation:epsilon`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SpringAnimation.epsilon.html), or immediately when it reaches
[`AdwSpringAnimation:value-to`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SpringAnimation.value-to.html) if
[`AdwSpringAnimation:clamp`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SpringAnimation.clamp.html) is set to `TRUE`. The estimated duration can
be obtained with [`AdwSpringAnimation:estimated-duration`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SpringAnimation.estimated-duration.html).

Due to the nature of spring-driven motion the animation can overshoot
[`AdwSpringAnimation:value-to`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SpringAnimation.value-to.html) before coming to a rest. Whether the
animation will overshoot or not depends on the damping ratio of the spring.
See [`AdwSpringParams`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/struct.SpringParams.html) for more information about specific damping ratio values.

If [`AdwSpringAnimation:clamp`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SpringAnimation.clamp.html) is `TRUE`, the animation will abruptly
end as soon as it reaches the final value, preventing overshooting.

Animations can have an initial velocity value, set via
[`AdwSpringAnimation:initial-velocity`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SpringAnimation.initial-velocity.html), which adjusts the curve without
changing the duration. This makes spring animations useful for deceleration
at the end of gestures.

If the initial and final values are equal, and the initial velocity is not 0,
the animation value will bounce and return to its resting position.

# Adw.Squeezer

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Squeezer.html

deprecated: 1.4

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-squeezer.c\#L26 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.Squeezer : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget, Gtk.Orientable {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Deprecated since: 1.4

See [the migration guide](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html#replace-adwsqueezer).

A best fit container.

![squeezer-wide](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/squeezer-wide.png)![squeezer-narrow](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/squeezer-narrow.png)

The `AdwSqueezer` widget is a container which only shows the first of its
children that fits in the available size. It is convenient to offer different
widgets to represent the same data with different levels of detail, making
the widget seem to squeeze itself to fit in the available space.

Transitions between children can be animated as fades. This can be controlled
with [`AdwSqueezer:transition-type`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Squeezer.transition-type.html).

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Squeezer.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwSqueezer` has a single CSS node with name `squeezer`.

# Adw.StatusPage

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.StatusPage.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-status-page.c\#L15 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.StatusPage : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A page used for empty/error states and similar use-cases.

![status-page](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/status-page.png)

The `AdwStatusPage` widget can have an icon, a title, a description and a
custom widget which is displayed below them.

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.StatusPage.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwStatusPage` has a main CSS node with name `statuspage`.

When setting an [`AdwSpinnerPaintable`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SpinnerPaintable.html) as [`AdwStatusPage:paintable`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.StatusPage.paintable.html),
the main nodes gains the `.spinner` style class for a more compact appearance.

## Style classes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.StatusPage.html\#style-classes "Permanent link")

`AdwStatusPage` can use the
[`.compact`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#compact-status-page) style class for when it
needs to fit into a small space such a sidebar or a popover, similar to when
using a spinner as the paintable.

![status-page-compact](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/status-page-compact.png).

# Adw.StyleManager

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.StyleManager.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-style-manager.c\#L35 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.StyleManager : GObject.Object
{
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A class for managing application-wide styling.

`AdwStyleManager` provides a way to query and influence the application
styles, such as whether to use dark style, the system accent color or high
contrast appearance.

It allows to set the color scheme via the
[`AdwStyleManager:color-scheme`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.StyleManager.color-scheme.html) property, and to query the current
appearance, as well as whether a system-wide color scheme and accent color
preferences exists.

# Adw.SwipeTracker

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SwipeTracker.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-swipe-tracker.c\#L36 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.SwipeTracker : GObject.Object
  implements Gtk.Orientable {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A swipe tracker used in [`AdwCarousel`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Carousel.html), [`AdwNavigationView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationView.html) and
[`AdwOverlaySplitView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.OverlaySplitView.html).

The `AdwSwipeTracker` object can be used for implementing widgets with swipe
gestures. It supports touch-based swipes, pointer dragging, and touchpad scrolling.

The widgets will probably want to expose the [`AdwSwipeTracker:enabled`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SwipeTracker.enabled.html)
property. If they expect to use horizontal orientation,
[`AdwSwipeTracker:reversed`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SwipeTracker.reversed.html) can be used for supporting RTL text direction.

\[−\]

# Adw.SwitchRow

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SwitchRow.html

since: 1.4

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-switch-row.c\#L11 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.SwitchRow : Adw.ActionRow
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Actionable, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.4

A [`GtkListBoxRow`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListBoxRow.html) used to represent two states.

![switch-row](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/switch-row.png)

The `AdwSwitchRow` widget contains a [`GtkSwitch`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Switch.html) that allows the user
to select between two states: “on” or “off”. When activated, the row will
invert its active state.

The user can control the switch by activating the row or by dragging on the
switch handle.

See [`GtkSwitch`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Switch.html) for details.

Example of an `AdwSwitchRow`UI definition:

```
<object class="AdwSwitchRow">
  <property name="title" translatable="yes">Switch Row</property>
  <signal name="notify::active" handler="switch_row_notify_active_cb"/>
</object>
```

Copy

The [`AdwSwitchRow:active`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SwitchRow.active.html) property should be connected to in order to
monitor changes to the active state.

## Accessibility [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SwitchRow.html\#accessibility "Permanent link")

`AdwSwitchRow` uses the [`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_SWITCH`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#switch) role.
