# Adw.TabBar

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabBar.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-tab-bar.c\#L18 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.TabBar : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A tab bar for [`AdwTabView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabView.html).

![tab-bar](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/tab-bar.png)

The `AdwTabBar` widget is a tab bar that can be used with conjunction with
`AdwTabView`. It is typically used as a top bar within [`AdwToolbarView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToolbarView.html).

`AdwTabBar` can autohide and can optionally contain action widgets on both
sides of the tabs.

When there’s not enough space to show all the tabs, `AdwTabBar` will scroll
them. Pinned tabs always stay visible and aren’t a part of the scrollable area.

## Drag-and-Drop [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabBar.html\#drag-and-drop "Permanent link")

`AdwTabBar` tabs can have an additional drop target for arbitrary content.

Use [`adw_tab_bar_setup_extra_drop_target()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.TabBar.setup_extra_drop_target.html) to set it up, specifying the
supported content types and drag actions, then connect to
[`AdwTabBar::extra-drag-drop`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.TabBar.extra-drag-drop.html) to handle a drop.

In some cases, it may be necessary to determine the used action based on the
content. In that case, set [`AdwTabBar:extra-drag-preload`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TabBar.extra-drag-preload.html) to `TRUE`
and connect to [`AdwTabBar::extra-drag-value`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.TabBar.extra-drag-value.html) signal, then return the
action from its handler. To access this action from the
[`AdwTabBar::extra-drag-drop`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.TabBar.extra-drag-drop.html) handler, use the
[`AdwTabBar:extra-drag-preferred-action`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TabBar.extra-drag-preferred-action.html) property.

[`AdwTabBar::extra-drag-value`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.TabBar.extra-drag-value.html) is also always emitted when starting to
hover an item, with a `NULL` value. This happens even when
[`AdwTabBar:extra-drag-preload`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TabBar.extra-drag-preload.html) is `FALSE`.

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabBar.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwTabBar` has a single CSS node with name `tabbar`.

## Style classes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabBar.html\#style-classes "Permanent link")

By default `AdwTabBar` look like a part of an `AdwHeaderBar` and is intended
to be used directly attached to one or used as a [`AdwToolbarView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToolbarView.html) toolbar.
The [`.inline`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#inline) style class removes its background,
so that it can be used in different contexts instead.

![tab-bar-inline](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/tab-bar-inline.png).

# Adw.TabButton

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabButton.html

since: 1.3

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-tab-button.c\#L18 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.TabButton : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Actionable, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.3

A button that displays the number of [`AdwTabView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabView.html) pages.

![tab-button](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/tab-button.png)

`AdwTabButton` is a button that displays the number of pages in a given
`AdwTabView`, as well as whether one of the inactive pages needs attention.

It’s intended to be used as a visible indicator when there’s no visible tab
bar, typically opening an [`AdwTabOverview`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabOverview.html) on click, e.g. via the
`overview.open` action name:

```
<object class="AdwTabButton">
  <property name="view">view</property>
  <property name="action-name">overview.open</property>
</object>
```

Copy

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabButton.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwTabButton` has a main CSS node with name `tabbutton`.

# Accessibility [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabButton.html\#accessibility "Permanent link")

`AdwTabButton` uses the [`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_BUTTON`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#button) role.

# Adw.TabOverview

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabOverview.html

since: 1.3

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-tab-overview.c\#L34 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.TabOverview : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.3

A tab overview for [`AdwTabView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabView.html).

![tab-overview](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/tab-overview.png)

`AdwTabOverview` is a widget that can display tabs from an `AdwTabView` in a grid.

`AdwTabOverview` shows a thumbnail for each tab. By default thumbnails are
static for all pages except the selected one. They can be made always live
by setting [`AdwTabPage:live-thumbnail`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TabPage.live-thumbnail.html) to `TRUE`, or refreshed with
[`adw_tab_page_invalidate_thumbnail()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.TabPage.invalidate_thumbnail.html) or
[`adw_tab_view_invalidate_thumbnails()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.TabView.invalidate_thumbnails.html) otherwise.

If the pages are too tall or too wide, the thumbnails will be cropped; use
[`AdwTabPage:thumbnail-xalign`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TabPage.thumbnail-xalign.html) and [`AdwTabPage:thumbnail-yalign`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TabPage.thumbnail-yalign.html) to
control which part of the page should be visible in this case.

Pinned tabs are shown as smaller cards without thumbnails above the other
tabs. Unlike in [`AdwTabBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabBar.html), they still have titles, as well as an unpin button.

`AdwTabOverview` provides search in open tabs. It searches in tab titles and
tooltips, as well as [`AdwTabPage:keyword`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TabPage.keyword.html).

If [`AdwTabOverview:enable-new-tab`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TabOverview.enable-new-tab.html) is set to `TRUE`, a new tab button
will be shown. Connect to the [`AdwTabOverview::create-tab`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.TabOverview.create-tab.html) signal to use it.

[`AdwTabOverview:secondary-menu`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TabOverview.secondary-menu.html) can be used to provide a secondary menu
for the overview. Use it to add extra actions, e.g. to open a new window or
undo closed tab.

`AdwTabOverview` is intended to be used as the direct child of the window,
with the rest of the window contents set as the [`AdwTabOverview:child`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TabOverview.child.html).
The child is expected to contain an [`AdwTabView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabView.html).

`AdwTabOverview` shows window buttons by default. They can be disabled by
setting [`AdwTabOverview:show-start-title-buttons`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TabOverview.show-start-title-buttons.html) and/or
[`AdwTabOverview:show-start-title-buttons`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TabOverview.show-start-title-buttons.html) and/or
[`AdwTabOverview:show-end-title-buttons`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TabOverview.show-end-title-buttons.html) to `FALSE`.

If search and window buttons are disabled, and secondary menu is not set, the
header bar will be hidden.

## Drag-and-Drop [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabOverview.html\#drag-and-drop "Permanent link")

`AdwTabOverview` thumbnails can have an additional drop target for arbitrary content.

Use [`adw_tab_overview_setup_extra_drop_target()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.TabOverview.setup_extra_drop_target.html) to set it up, specifying the
supported content types and drag actions, then connect to
[`AdwTabOverview::extra-drag-drop`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.TabOverview.extra-drag-drop.html) to handle a drop.

In some cases, it may be necessary to determine the used action based on the
content. In that case, set [`AdwTabOverview:extra-drag-preload`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TabOverview.extra-drag-preload.html) to
`TRUE` and connect to [`AdwTabOverview::extra-drag-value`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.TabOverview.extra-drag-value.html) signal, then
return the action from its handler. To access this action from the
[`AdwTabOverview::extra-drag-drop`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.TabOverview.extra-drag-drop.html) handler, use the
[`AdwTabOverview:extra-drag-preferred-action`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TabOverview.extra-drag-preferred-action.html) property.

[`AdwTabOverview::extra-drag-value`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.TabOverview.extra-drag-value.html) is also always emitted when starting to
hover an item, with a `NULL` value. This happens even when
[`AdwTabOverview:extra-drag-preload`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TabOverview.extra-drag-preload.html) is `FALSE`.

## Actions [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabOverview.html\#actions "Permanent link")

`AdwTabOverview` defines the `overview.open` and `overview.close` actions for
opening and closing itself. They can be convenient when used together with
[`AdwTabButton`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabButton.html).

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabOverview.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwTabOverview` has a single CSS node with name `taboverview`.

# Adw.TabView

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabView.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-tab-view.c\#L31 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.TabView : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A dynamic tabbed container.

`AdwTabView` is a container which shows one child at a time. While it
provides keyboard shortcuts for switching between pages, it does not provide
a visible tab switcher and relies on external widgets for that, such as
[`AdwTabBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabBar.html), [`AdwTabOverview`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabOverview.html) and [`AdwTabButton`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabButton.html).

`AdwTabView` maintains a [`AdwTabPage`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabPage.html) object for each page, which holds
additional per-page properties. You can obtain the `AdwTabPage` for a page
with [`adw_tab_view_get_page()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.TabView.get_page.html), and as the return value for
[`adw_tab_view_append()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.TabView.append.html) and other functions for adding children.

`AdwTabView` only aims to be useful for dynamic tabs in multi-window
document-based applications, such as web browsers, file managers, text
editors or terminals. It does not aim to replace [`GtkNotebook`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Notebook.html) for use
cases such as tabbed dialogs.

As such, it does not support disabling page reordering or detaching.

`AdwTabView` adds a number of global page switching and reordering shortcuts.
The [`AdwTabView:shortcuts`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TabView.shortcuts.html) property can be used to manage them.

See [`AdwTabViewShortcuts`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/flags.TabViewShortcuts.html) for the list of the available shortcuts. All of
the shortcuts are enabled by default.

[`adw_tab_view_add_shortcuts()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.TabView.add_shortcuts.html) and [`adw_tab_view_remove_shortcuts()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.TabView.remove_shortcuts.html) can be
used to manage shortcuts in a convenient way, for example:

```
adw_tab_view_remove_shortcuts (view, ADW_TAB_VIEW_SHORTCUT_CONTROL_HOME |
                                     ADW_TAB_VIEW_SHORTCUT_CONTROL_END);
```

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabView.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwTabView` has a main CSS node with the name `tabview`.

## Accessibility [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabView.html\#accessibility "Permanent link")

`AdwTabView` uses the [`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_TAB_PANEL`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#tab-panel) role for the tab
pages which are the accessible parent objects of the child widgets.

# Adw.TimedAnimation

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TimedAnimation.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-timed-animation.c\#L14 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.TimedAnimation : Adw.Animation
{
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A time-based [`AdwAnimation`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Animation.html).

`AdwTimedAnimation` implements a simple animation interpolating the given
value from [`AdwTimedAnimation:value-from`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TimedAnimation.value-from.html) to
[`AdwTimedAnimation:value-to`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TimedAnimation.value-to.html) over
[`AdwTimedAnimation:duration`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TimedAnimation.duration.html) milliseconds using the curve described by
[`AdwTimedAnimation:easing`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TimedAnimation.easing.html).

If [`AdwTimedAnimation:reverse`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TimedAnimation.reverse.html) is set to `TRUE`, `AdwTimedAnimation`
will instead animate from [`AdwTimedAnimation:value-to`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TimedAnimation.value-to.html) to
[`AdwTimedAnimation:value-from`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TimedAnimation.value-from.html), and the easing curve will be inverted.

The animation can repeat a certain amount of times, or endlessly, depending
on the [`AdwTimedAnimation:repeat-count`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TimedAnimation.repeat-count.html) value. If
[`AdwTimedAnimation:alternate`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.TimedAnimation.alternate.html) is set to `TRUE`, it will also change the
direction every other iteration.

# Adw.Toast

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Toast.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-toast.c\#L24 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.Toast : GObject.Object
{
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A helper object for [`AdwToastOverlay`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToastOverlay.html).

Toasts are meant to be passed into [`adw_toast_overlay_add_toast()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.ToastOverlay.add_toast.html) as follows:

```
adw_toast_overlay_add_toast (overlay, adw_toast_new (_("Simple Toast")));
```

Copy

![toast-simple](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/toast-simple.png)

Toasts always have a close button. They emit the [`AdwToast::dismissed`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.Toast.dismissed.html)
signal when disappearing.

[`AdwToast:timeout`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Toast.timeout.html) determines how long the toast stays on screen, while
[`AdwToast:priority`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Toast.priority.html) determines how it behaves if another toast is
already being displayed.

Toast titles use Pango markup by default, set [`AdwToast:use-markup`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Toast.use-markup.html) to
`FALSE` if this is unwanted.

[`AdwToast:custom-title`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Toast.custom-title.html) can be used to replace the title label with a
custom widget.

## Actions [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Toast.html\#actions "Permanent link")

Toasts can have one button on them, with a label and an attached
[`GAction`](https://docs.gtk.org/gio/iface.Action.html).

```
AdwToast *toast = adw_toast_new (_("Toast with Action"));

adw_toast_set_button_label (toast, _("_Example"));
adw_toast_set_action_name (toast, "win.example");

```

## Modifying toasts [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Toast.html\#modifying-toasts "Permanent link")

Toasts can be modified after they have been shown. For this, an `AdwToast`
reference must be kept around while the toast is visible.

A common use case for this is using toasts as undo prompts that stack with
each other, allowing to batch undo the last deleted items:

```
static void
toast_undo_cb (GtkWidget  *sender,
               const char *action,
               GVariant   *param)
{
  // Undo the deletion
}

static void
dismissed_cb (MyWindow *self)
{
  self->undo_toast = NULL;

  // Permanently delete the items
}

static void
delete_item (MyWindow *self,
             MyItem   *item)
{
  g_autofree char *title = NULL;
  int n_items;

  // Mark the item as waiting for deletion
  n_items = ... // The number of waiting items

  if (!self->undo_toast) {
    self->undo_toast = adw_toast_new_format (_("‘%s’ deleted"), ...);

    adw_toast_set_priority (self->undo_toast, ADW_TOAST_PRIORITY_HIGH);
    adw_toast_set_button_label (self->undo_toast, _("_Undo"));
    adw_toast_set_action_name (self->undo_toast, "toast.undo");

    g_signal_connect_swapped (self->undo_toast, "dismissed",
                              G_CALLBACK (dismissed_cb), self);

    adw_toast_overlay_add_toast (self->toast_overlay, self->undo_toast);

    return;
  }

  title =
    g_strdup_printf (ngettext ("<span font_features='tnum=1'>%d</span> item deleted",
                               "<span font_features='tnum=1'>%d</span> items deleted",
                               n_items), n_items);

  adw_toast_set_title (self->undo_toast, title);

  // Bump the toast timeout
  adw_toast_overlay_add_toast (self->toast_overlay, g_object_ref (self->undo_toast));
}

static void
my_window_class_init (MyWindowClass *klass)
{
  GtkWidgetClass *widget_class = GTK_WIDGET_CLASS (klass);

  gtk_widget_class_install_action (widget_class, "toast.undo", NULL, toast_undo_cb);
}
```

Copy

![toast-undo](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/toast-undo.png).

# Adw.ToastOverlay

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToastOverlay.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-toast-overlay.c\#L26 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.ToastOverlay : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A widget showing toasts above its content.

![toast-overlay](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/toast-overlay.png)

Much like [`GtkOverlay`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Overlay.html), `AdwToastOverlay` is a container with a single
main child, on top of which it can display a [`AdwToast`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Toast.html), overlaid.
Toasts can be shown with [`adw_toast_overlay_add_toast()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.ToastOverlay.add_toast.html).

Use [`adw_toast_overlay_dismiss_all()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.ToastOverlay.dismiss_all.html) to dismiss all toasts at once, or
[`adw_toast_dismiss()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Toast.dismiss.html) to dismiss a single toast.

See [`AdwToast`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Toast.html) for details.

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToastOverlay.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

```
toastoverlay
├── [child]
├── toast
┊   ├── widget
┊   │   ├── [label.heading]
    │   ╰── [custom title]
    ├── [button]
    ╰── button.circular.flat
```

Copy

`AdwToastOverlay`‘s CSS node is called `toastoverlay`. It contains the child,
as well as zero or more `toast` subnodes.

Each of the `toast` nodes contains a `widget` subnode, optionally a `button`
subnode, and another `button` subnode with `.circular` and `.flat` style classes.

The `widget` subnode contains a `label` subnode with the `.heading` style
class, or a custom widget provided by the application.

## Accessibility [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToastOverlay.html\#accessibility "Permanent link")

`AdwToastOverlay` uses the [`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_GROUP`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#group) role.

# Adw.Toggle

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Toggle.html

since: 1.7

```
final class Adw.Toggle : GObject.Object
{
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.7

A toggle within [`AdwToggleGroup`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToggleGroup.html).

`AdwToggle` can optionally have a name, set with [`AdwToggle:name`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Toggle.name.html).
If the name is set, [`AdwToggleGroup:active-name`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ToggleGroup.active-name.html) can be used to access
toggles instead of index.

# Adw.ToggleGroup

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToggleGroup.html

since: 1.7

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-toggle-group.c\#L14 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.ToggleGroup : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget, Gtk.Orientable {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.7

A group of exclusive toggles.

![toggle-group](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/toggle-group.png)

`AdwToggleGroup` presents a set of exclusive toggles, represented as
[`AdwToggle`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Toggle.html) objects. Each toggle can display an icon, a label, an icon
and a label, or a custom child.

Toggles are indexed by their position, with the first toggle being equivalent
to 0, and so on. Use the [`AdwToggleGroup:active`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ToggleGroup.active.html) to get that position.

Toggles can also have optional names, set via the [`AdwToggle:name`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Toggle.name.html)
property. The name of the active toggle can be accessed via the
[`AdwToggleGroup:active-name`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ToggleGroup.active-name.html) property.

`AdwToggle` objects can be retrieved via their index or name, using
[`adw_toggle_group_get_toggle()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.ToggleGroup.get_toggle.html) or [`adw_toggle_group_get_toggle_by_name()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.ToggleGroup.get_toggle_by_name.html)
respectively. `AdwToggleGroup` also provides a [`GtkSelectionModel`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/iface.SelectionModel.html) of
its toggles via the [`AdwToggleGroup:toggles`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ToggleGroup.toggles.html) property.

`AdwToggleGroup` is orientable, and the toggles can be displayed horizontally
or vertically. This is mostly useful for icon-only toggles.

Use the [`AdwToggleGroup:homogeneous`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ToggleGroup.homogeneous.html) property to make the toggles take
the same size, and the [`AdwToggleGroup:can-shrink`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ToggleGroup.can-shrink.html) to control whether
the toggles can ellipsize.

Example of an `AdwToggleGroup`UI definition:

```
 <object class="AdwToggleGroup">
   <property name="active-name">picture</property>
   <child>
     <object class="AdwToggle">
       <property name="icon-name">camera-photo-symbolic</property>
       <property name="tooltip" translatable="yes">Picture Mode</property>
       <property name="name">picture</property>
     </object>
   </child>
   <child>
     <object class="AdwToggle">
       <property name="icon-name">camera-video-symbolic</property>
       <property name="tooltip" translatable="yes">Recording Mode</property>
       <property name="name">recording</property>
     </object>
   </child>
 </object>
```

Copy

See also: [`AdwInlineViewSwitcher`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.InlineViewSwitcher.html).

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToggleGroup.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwToggleGroup` has a main CSS node with the name `toggle-group`.

Its toggles have CSS nodes with the name `toggle`, and its separators have nodes
with the name `separator`.

Toggle nodes will have a different style classes depending on their content:
`.text-button` for labels, `.image-button` for icons, `.image-text-button`
for both or no style class for custom children.

The hidden separators use the `.hidden` style class.

## Style classes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToggleGroup.html\#style-classes "Permanent link")

`AdwToggleGroup` can use the [`.flat`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#flat_1) style class
to remove its background and make it look like a group of buttons.

![toggle-group-flat](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/toggle-group-flat.png)

It can also use the [`.round`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#round) style class to make
its toggles and the group itself rounded.

![toggle-group-round](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/toggle-group-round.png)

They can also be combined with each other.

![toggle-group-flat-round](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/toggle-group-flat-round.png)

## Accessibility [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToggleGroup.html\#accessibility "Permanent link")

`AdwToggleGroup` uses the [`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_RADIO_GROUP`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#radio-group) role. Its
toggles use the [`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_RADIO`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#radio) role.

# Adw.ToolbarView

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToolbarView.html

since: 1.4

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-toolbar-view.c\#L15 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.ToolbarView : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.4

A widget containing a page, as well as top and/or bottom bars.

![toolbar-view](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/toolbar-view.png)

`AdwToolbarView` has a single content widget and one or multiple top and
bottom bars, shown at the top and bottom sides respectively.

Example of an `AdwToolbarView`UI definition:

```
<object class="AdwToolbarView">
  <child type="top">
    <object class="AdwHeaderBar"/>
  </child>
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwPreferencesPage">
      <!-- ... -->
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

The following kinds of top and bottom bars are supported:

- [`AdwHeaderBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html)
- [`AdwTabBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabBar.html)
- [`AdwViewSwitcherBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherBar.html)
- [`GtkActionBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ActionBar.html)
- [`GtkHeaderBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.HeaderBar.html)
- [`GtkPopoverMenuBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.PopoverMenuBar.html)
- [`GtkSearchBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.SearchBar.html)
- Any [`GtkBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Box.html) or a similar widget with the
[`.toolbar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#toolbars) style class

By default, top and bottom bars are flat and scrolling content has a subtle
undershoot shadow, same as when using the
[`.undershoot-top`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#undershoot-indicators) and
[`.undershoot-bottom`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#undershoot-indicators) style
classes. This works well in most cases, e.g. with [`AdwStatusPage`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.StatusPage.html) or
[`AdwPreferencesPage`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesPage.html), where the background at the top and bottom parts of
the page is uniform. Additionally, windows with sidebars should always use
this style.

[`AdwToolbarView:top-bar-style`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ToolbarView.top-bar-style.html) and
[`AdwToolbarView:bottom-bar-style`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ToolbarView.bottom-bar-style.html) properties can be used add an opaque
background and a persistent shadow to top and bottom bars, this can be useful
for content such as [utility panes](https://developer.gnome.org/hig/patterns/containers/utility-panes.html),
where some elements are adjacent to the top/bottom bars, or [`AdwTabView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabView.html),
where each page can have a different background.

![toolbar-view-flat-1](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/toolbar-view-flat-1.png)![toolbar-view-flat-2](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/toolbar-view-flat-2.png)![toolbar-view-raised](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/toolbar-view-raised.png)

`AdwToolbarView` ensures the top and bottom bars have consistent backdrop
styles and vertical spacing. For comparison:

![toolbar-view-spacing](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/toolbar-view-spacing.png)![toolbar-view-spacing-box](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/toolbar-view-spacing-box.png)

Any top and bottom bars can also be dragged to move the window, equivalent
to putting them into a [`GtkWindowHandle`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.WindowHandle.html).

Content is typically place between top and bottom bars, but can also extend
behind them. This is controlled with the
[`AdwToolbarView:extend-content-to-top-edge`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ToolbarView.extend-content-to-top-edge.html) and
[`AdwToolbarView:extend-content-to-bottom-edge`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ToolbarView.extend-content-to-bottom-edge.html) properties.

Top and bottom bars can be hidden and revealed with an animation using the
[`AdwToolbarView:reveal-top-bars`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ToolbarView.reveal-top-bars.html) and
[`AdwToolbarView:reveal-bottom-bars`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ToolbarView.reveal-bottom-bars.html) properties.

## `AdwToolbarView` as `GtkBuildable` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToolbarView.html\#adwtoolbarview-as-gtkbuildable "Permanent link")

The `AdwToolbarView` implementation of the [`GtkBuildable`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/iface.Buildable.html) interface
supports adding a top bar by specifying “top” as the “type” attribute of a
`<child>` element, or adding a bottom bar by specifying “bottom”.

## Accessibility [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToolbarView.html\#accessibility "Permanent link")

`AdwToolbarView` uses the [`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_GROUP`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#group) role.

# Adw.ViewStack

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewStack.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-view-stack.c\#L22 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.ViewStack : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A view container for [`AdwViewSwitcher`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcher.html).

`AdwViewStack` is a container which only shows one page at a time.
It is typically used to hold an application’s main views.

It doesn’t provide a way to transition between pages.
Instead, a separate widget such as [`AdwViewSwitcher`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcher.html),
[`AdwInlineViewSwitcher`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.InlineViewSwitcher.html) or [`AdwViewSwitcherSidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherSidebar.html) can be used with
`AdwViewStack` to provide this functionality.

`AdwViewStack` pages can have a title, an icon, an attention request, and a
numbered badge that [`AdwViewSwitcher`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcher.html) will use to let users identify which
page is which. Set them using the [`AdwViewStackPage:title`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ViewStackPage.title.html),
[`AdwViewStackPage:icon-name`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ViewStackPage.icon-name.html),
[`AdwViewStackPage:needs-attention`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ViewStackPage.needs-attention.html), and
[`AdwViewStackPage:badge-number`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ViewStackPage.badge-number.html) properties.

`AdwViewStack` pages can also be grouped into sections, using the
[`AdwViewStackPage:starts-section`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ViewStackPage.starts-section.html) and
[`AdwViewStackPage:section-title`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ViewStackPage.section-title.html) properties. Currently, only
[`AdwViewSwitcherSidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherSidebar.html) displays groups.

Unlike [`GtkStack`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Stack.html), transitions between views can only be animated via
a crossfade and size changes are always interpolated. Animations are disabled
by default. Use [`AdwViewStack:enable-transitions`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ViewStack.enable-transitions.html) to enable them.

`AdwViewStack` maintains a [`AdwViewStackPage`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewStackPage.html) object for each added child,
which holds additional per-child properties. You obtain the
[`AdwViewStackPage`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewStackPage.html) for a child with [`adw_view_stack_get_page()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.ViewStack.get_page.html) and you
can obtain a [`GtkSelectionModel`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/iface.SelectionModel.html) containing all the pages with
[`adw_view_stack_get_pages()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.ViewStack.get_pages.html).

## AdwViewStack as GtkBuildable [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewStack.html\#adwviewstack-as-gtkbuildable "Permanent link")

To set child-specific properties in a .ui file, create
[`AdwViewStackPage`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewStackPage.html) objects explicitly, and set the child widget as a
property on it:

```
  <object class="AdwViewStack" id="stack">
    <child>
      <object class="AdwViewStackPage">
        <property name="name">overview</property>
        <property name="title">Overview</property>
        <property name="child">
          <object class="AdwStatusPage">
            <property name="title">Welcome!</property>
          </object>
        </property>
      </object>
    </child>
  </object>
```

Copy

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewStack.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwViewStack` has a single CSS node named `stack`.

## Accessibility [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewStack.html\#accessibility "Permanent link")

`AdwViewStack` uses the [`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_TAB_PANEL`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#tab-panel) for the stack
pages which are the accessible parent objects of the child widgets.

# Adw.ViewSwitcher

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcher.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-view-switcher.c\#L18 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.ViewSwitcher : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

An adaptive view switcher.

![view-switcher](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/view-switcher.png)

An adaptive view switcher designed to switch between multiple views
contained in a [`AdwViewStack`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewStack.html) in a similar fashion to
[`GtkStackSwitcher`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.StackSwitcher.html).

`AdwViewSwitcher` buttons always have an icon and a label. They can be
displayed side by side, or icon on top of the label. This can be controlled
via the [`AdwViewSwitcher:policy`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ViewSwitcher.policy.html) property.

`AdwViewSwitcher` is intended to be used in a header bar together with
[`AdwViewSwitcherBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherBar.html) at the bottom of the window, and a [`AdwBreakpoint`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Breakpoint.html)
showing the view switcher bar on narrow sizes, while removing the view
switcher from the header bar, as follows:

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <child>
    <object class="AdwBreakpoint">
      <condition>max-width: 550sp</condition>
      <setter object="switcher_bar" property="reveal">True</setter>
      <setter object="header_bar" property="title-widget"/>
    </object>
  </child>
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwToolbarView">
      <child type="top">
        <object class="AdwHeaderBar" id="header_bar">
          <property name="title-widget">
            <object class="AdwViewSwitcher">
              <property name="stack">stack</property>
              <property name="policy">wide</property>
            </object>
          </property>
        </object>
      </child>
      <property name="content">
        <object class="AdwViewStack" id="stack"/>
      </property>
      <child type="bottom">
        <object class="AdwViewSwitcherBar" id="switcher_bar">
          <property name="stack">stack</property>
        </object>
      </child>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

It’s recommended to set [`AdwViewSwitcher:policy`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ViewSwitcher.policy.html) to
[`ADW_VIEW_SWITCHER_POLICY_WIDE`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.ViewSwitcherPolicy.html#wide) in this case.

You may have to adjust the breakpoint condition for your specific pages.

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcher.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwViewSwitcher` has a single CSS node with name `viewswitcher`. It can have
the style classes `.wide` and `.narrow`, matching its policy.

## Accessibility [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcher.html\#accessibility "Permanent link")

`AdwViewSwitcher` uses the [`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_TAB_LIST`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#tab-list) role and the
[`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_TAB`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#tab) role for its buttons.

See also: [`AdwViewSwitcherBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherBar.html), [`AdwInlineViewSwitcher`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.InlineViewSwitcher.html),
[`AdwViewSwitcherSidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherSidebar.html).

# Adw.ViewSwitcherBar

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherBar.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-view-switcher-bar.c\#L14 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.ViewSwitcherBar : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A view switcher action bar.

![view-switcher-bar](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/view-switcher-bar.png)

An action bar letting you switch between multiple views contained in a
[`AdwViewStack`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewStack.html), via an [`AdwViewSwitcher`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcher.html). It is designed to be put at
the bottom of a window and to be revealed only on really narrow windows, e.g.
on mobile phones. It can’t be revealed if there are less than two pages.

`AdwViewSwitcherBar` is intended to be used together with
`AdwViewSwitcher` in a header bar, and a [`AdwBreakpoint`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Breakpoint.html) showing the view
switcher bar on narrow sizes, while removing the view switcher from the
header bar, as follows:

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <child>
    <object class="AdwBreakpoint">
      <condition>max-width: 550sp</condition>
      <setter object="switcher_bar" property="reveal">True</setter>
      <setter object="header_bar" property="title-widget"/>
    </object>
  </child>
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwToolbarView">
      <child type="top">
        <object class="AdwHeaderBar" id="header_bar">
          <property name="title-widget">
            <object class="AdwViewSwitcher">
              <property name="stack">stack</property>
              <property name="policy">wide</property>
            </object>
          </property>
        </object>
      </child>
      <property name="content">
        <object class="AdwViewStack" id="stack"/>
      </property>
      <child type="bottom">
        <object class="AdwViewSwitcherBar" id="switcher_bar">
          <property name="stack">stack</property>
        </object>
      </child>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

It’s recommended to set [`AdwViewSwitcher:policy`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ViewSwitcher.policy.html) to
[`ADW_VIEW_SWITCHER_POLICY_WIDE`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.ViewSwitcherPolicy.html#wide) in this case.

You may have to adjust the breakpoint condition for your specific pages.

# Adw.ViewSwitcherSidebar

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherSidebar.html

since: 1.9

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-view-switcher-sidebar.c\#L17 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.ViewSwitcherSidebar : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.9

An adaptive sidebar that controls an [`AdwViewStack`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewStack.html).

![view-switcher-sidebar](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/view-switcher-sidebar.png)

`AdwViewSwitcherSidebar` is a view switcher implemented using a
[`AdwSidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Sidebar.html), in a similar fashion to [`GtkStackSidebar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.StackSidebar.html).

`AdwViewSwitcherSidebar` items have an icon, a label, as well as an unread
dot or a badge.

Unlike other switchers, `AdwViewSwitcherSidebar` supports grouping pages into
sections, using the [`AdwViewStackPage:starts-section`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ViewStackPage.starts-section.html) and
[`AdwViewStackPage:section-title`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ViewStackPage.section-title.html) properties.

Like [`AdwSidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Sidebar.html), `AdwViewSwitcherSidebar` is adaptive and can behave as
a sidebar or a page, via the [`AdwViewSwitcherSidebar:mode`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ViewSwitcherSidebar.mode.html) property.

![view-switcher-sidebar-modes](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/view-switcher-sidebar-modes.png)

Connect to the [`AdwViewSwitcherSidebar::activated`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.ViewSwitcherSidebar.activated.html) signal to run code when
an item has been activated. This can be used to toggle the visible pane when
used in a split view.

Like `AdwSidebar`, `AdwViewSwitcherSidebar` supports filtering items via the
[`AdwViewSwitcherSidebar:filter`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ViewSwitcherSidebar.filter.html) property.

Use [`AdwViewSwitcherSidebar:placeholder`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ViewSwitcherSidebar.placeholder.html) to provide an empty state
widget. It will be shown when all items have been filtered out, or the
sidebar has no items otherwise.

Like `AdwSidebar`, `AdwViewSwitcherSidebar` supports prefix and suffix
widgets via the [`AdwSidebar:prefix`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Sidebar.prefix.html) and [`AdwSidebar:suffix`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Sidebar.suffix.html) properties.

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherSidebar.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwViewSwitcherSidebar` has a single CSS node with name
`view-switcher-sidebar`.

See also: [`AdwViewSwitcher`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcher.html), [`AdwViewSwitcherBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherBar.html),
[`AdwInlineViewSwitcher`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.InlineViewSwitcher.html).

# Adw.ViewSwitcherTitle

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherTitle.html

deprecated: 1.4

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-view-switcher-title.c\#L15 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.ViewSwitcherTitle : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Deprecated since: 1.4

See [the migration guide](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html#replace-adwviewswitchertitle).

A view switcher title.

![view-switcher-title](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/view-switcher-title.png)

A widget letting you switch between multiple views contained by a
[`AdwViewStack`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewStack.html) via an [`AdwViewSwitcher`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcher.html).

It is designed to be used as the title widget of a [`AdwHeaderBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html), and
will display the window’s title when the window is too narrow to fit the view
switcher e.g. on mobile phones, or if there are less than two views.

In order to center the title in narrow windows, the header bar should have
[`AdwHeaderBar:centering-policy`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.centering-policy.html) set to
[`ADW_CENTERING_POLICY_STRICT`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.CenteringPolicy.html#strict).

`AdwViewSwitcherTitle` is intended to be used together with
[`AdwViewSwitcherBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherBar.html).

A common use case is to bind the [`AdwViewSwitcherBar:reveal`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ViewSwitcherBar.reveal.html) property
to [`AdwViewSwitcherTitle:title-visible`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ViewSwitcherTitle.title-visible.html) to automatically reveal the
view switcher bar when the title label is displayed in place of the view
switcher, as follows:

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwToolbarView">
      <child type="top">
        <object class="AdwHeaderBar">
          <property name="centering-policy">strict</property>
          <property name="title-widget">
            <object class="AdwViewSwitcherTitle" id="title">
              <property name="stack">stack</property>
            </object>
          </property>
        </object>
      </child>
      <property name="content">
        <object class="AdwViewStack" id="stack"/>
      </property>
      <child type="bottom">
        <object class="AdwViewSwitcherBar">
          <property name="stack">stack</property>
          <binding name="reveal">
            <lookup name="title-visible">title</lookup>
          </binding>
        </object>
      </child>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

# Adw.Window

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Window.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-window.c\#L21 "go to source location")

```
class Adw.Window : Gtk.Window
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget, Gtk.Native, Gtk.Root, Gtk.ShortcutManager {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A freeform window.

![window](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/window.png)

The `AdwWindow` widget is a subclass of [`GtkWindow`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Window.html) which has no
titlebar area. Instead, [`AdwToolbarView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToolbarView.html) can be used together with
[`AdwHeaderBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html) or [`GtkHeaderBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.HeaderBar.html) as follows:

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwToolbarView">
      <child type="top">
        <object class="AdwHeaderBar"/>
      </child>
      <property name="content">
        <!-- put your content here -->
      </property>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

Using [`GtkWindow:titlebar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Window.titlebar.html) or [`GtkWindow:child`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Window.child.html)
is not supported and will result in a crash. Use [`AdwWindow:content`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Window.content.html) instead.

## Dialogs [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Window.html\#dialogs "Permanent link")

`AdwWindow` can contain [`AdwDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Dialog.html). Use [`adw_dialog_present()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Dialog.present.html) with the
window or a widget within a window to show a dialog.

## Breakpoints [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Window.html\#breakpoints "Permanent link")

`AdwWindow` can be used with [`AdwBreakpoint`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Breakpoint.html) the same way as
[`AdwBreakpointBin`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.BreakpointBin.html). Refer to that widget’s documentation for details.

Example:

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwToolbarView">
      <child type="top">
        <object class="AdwHeaderBar"/>
      </child>
      <property name="content">
        <!-- put your content here -->
      </property>
      <child type="bottom">
        <object class="GtkActionBar" id="bottom_bar">
          <property name="revealed">True</property>
          <property name="visible">False</property>
        </object>
      </child>
    </object>
  </property>
  <child>
    <object class="AdwBreakpoint">
      <condition>max-width: 500px</condition>
      <setter object="bottom_bar" property="visible">True</setter>
    </object>
  </child>
</object>
```

Copy

When breakpoints are used, the minimum size must be larger than the smallest
UI state. `AdwWindow` defaults to the minimum size of 360×200 px. If that’s
too small, set the [`GtkWidget:width-request`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Widget.width-request.html) and
[`GtkWidget:height-request`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Widget.height-request.html) properties manually.

## Adaptive Preview [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Window.html\#adaptive-preview "Permanent link")

`AdwWindow` has a debug tool called adaptive preview. It can be opened from
GTK Inspector or by pressing `Ctrl` + `Shift` + `M`,
and controlled via the [`AdwWindow:adaptive-preview`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Window.adaptive-preview.html) property.

# Adw.WindowTitle

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.WindowTitle.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-window-title.c\#L11 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.WindowTitle : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

A helper widget for setting a window’s title and subtitle.

![window-title](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/window-title.png)

`AdwWindowTitle` shows a title and subtitle. It’s intended to be used as the
title child of [`GtkHeaderBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.HeaderBar.html) or [`AdwHeaderBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html).

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.WindowTitle.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwWindowTitle` has a single CSS node with name `windowtitle`.

# Adw.WrapBox

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.WrapBox.html

since: 1.7

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-wrap-box.c\#L17 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.WrapBox : Gtk.Widget
  implements Gtk.Accessible, Gtk.Buildable, Gtk.ConstraintTarget, Gtk.Orientable {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.7

A box-like widget that can wrap into multiple lines.

![wrap-box](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/wrap-box.png)

`AdwWrapBox` is similar to [`GtkBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Box.html), but can wrap lines when the
widgets cannot fit otherwise. Unlike [`GtkFlowBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.FlowBox.html), the children aren’t
arranged into a grid and behave more like words in a wrapping label.

Like `GtkBox`, `AdwWrapBox` is orientable and has spacing:

- [`AdwWrapBox:child-spacing`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapBox.child-spacing.html) between children in the same line;
- [`AdwWrapBox:line-spacing`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapBox.line-spacing.html) between lines.

Note

Unlike `GtkBox`, `AdwWrapBox` cannot follow the CSS`border-spacing`
property.

Use the [`AdwWrapBox:natural-line-length`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapBox.natural-line-length.html) property to determine the
layout’s natural size, e.g. when using it in a [`GtkPopover`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Popover.html).

Normally, a horizontal `AdwWrapBox` wraps left to right and top to bottom
for left-to-right languages. Both of these directions can be reversed, using
the [`AdwWrapBox:pack-direction`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapBox.pack-direction.html) and [`AdwWrapBox:wrap-reverse`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapBox.wrap-reverse.html)
properties. Additionally, the alignment of each line can be controlled with
the [`AdwWrapBox:align`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapBox.align.html) property.

Lines can be justified using the [`AdwWrapBox:justify`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapBox.justify.html) property, filling
the entire line by either increasing child size or spacing depending on the
value. Set [`AdwWrapBox:justify-last-line`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapBox.justify-last-line.html) to justify the last line as well.

By default, `AdwWrapBox` wraps as soon as the previous line cannot fit any
more children without shrinking them past their natural size. Set
[`AdwWrapBox:wrap-policy`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapBox.wrap-policy.html) to [`ADW_WRAP_MINIMUM`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.WrapPolicy.html#minimum) to only wrap
once all the children in the previous line have been shrunk to their minimum size.

To make each line take the same amount of space, set
[`AdwWrapBox:line-homogeneous`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapBox.line-homogeneous.html) to `TRUE`.

Spacing and natural line length can scale with the text scale factor, use the
[`AdwWrapBox:child-spacing-unit`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapBox.child-spacing-unit.html), [`AdwWrapBox:line-spacing-unit`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapBox.line-spacing-unit.html)
and/or [`AdwWrapBox:natural-line-length-unit`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapBox.natural-line-length-unit.html) properties to enable that behavior.

See [`AdwWrapLayout`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.WrapLayout.html).

## CSS nodes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.WrapBox.html\#css-nodes "Permanent link")

`AdwWrapBox` uses a single CSS node with name `wrap-box`.

## Accessibility [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.WrapBox.html\#accessibility "Permanent link")

`AdwWrapBox` uses the [`GTK_ACCESSIBLE_ROLE_GROUP`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.AccessibleRole.html#group) role.

# Adw.WrapLayout

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.WrapLayout.html

since: 1.7

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-wrap-layout.c\#L17 "go to source location")

```
final class Adw.WrapLayout : Gtk.LayoutManager
  implements Gtk.Orientable {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Available since: 1.7

A box-like layout that can wrap into multiple lines.

![wrap-box](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/wrap-box.png)

`AdwWrapLayout` is similar to [`GtkBoxLayout`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.BoxLayout.html), but can wrap lines when
the widgets cannot fit otherwise. Unlike [`GtkFlowBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.FlowBox.html), the children
aren’t arranged into a grid and behave more like words in a wrapping label.

Like `GtkBoxLayout`, `AdwWrapLayout` is orientable and has spacing:

- [`AdwWrapLayout:child-spacing`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapLayout.child-spacing.html) between children in the same line;
- [`AdwWrapLayout:line-spacing`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapLayout.line-spacing.html) between lines.

Note

Unlike `GtkBoxLayout`, `AdwWrapLayout` cannot follow the CSS`border-spacing` property.

Use the [`AdwWrapLayout:natural-line-length`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapLayout.natural-line-length.html) property to determine the
layout’s natural size, e.g. when using it in a [`GtkPopover`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Popover.html).

Normally, a horizontal `AdwWrapLayout` wraps left to right and top to bottom
for left-to-right languages. Both of these directions can be reversed, using
the [`AdwWrapLayout:pack-direction`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapLayout.pack-direction.html) and
[`AdwWrapLayout:wrap-reverse`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapLayout.wrap-reverse.html) properties. Additionally, the alignment
of each line can be controlled with the [`AdwWrapLayout:align`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapLayout.align.html) property.

Lines can be justified using the [`AdwWrapLayout:justify`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapLayout.justify.html) property,
filling the entire line by either increasing child size or spacing depending
on the value. Set [`AdwWrapLayout:justify-last-line`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapLayout.justify-last-line.html) to justify the last
line as well.

By default, `AdwWrapLayout` wraps as soon as the previous line cannot fit
any more children without shrinking them past their natural size. Set
[`AdwWrapLayout:wrap-policy`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapLayout.wrap-policy.html) to [`ADW_WRAP_MINIMUM`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.WrapPolicy.html#minimum) to only
wrap once all the children in the previous line have been shrunk to their
minimum size.

To make each line take the same amount of space, set
[`AdwWrapLayout:line-homogeneous`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapLayout.line-homogeneous.html) to `TRUE`.

Spacing and natural line length can scale with the text scale factor, use the
[`AdwWrapLayout:child-spacing-unit`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapLayout.child-spacing-unit.html),
[`AdwWrapLayout:line-spacing-unit`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapLayout.line-spacing-unit.html) and/or
[`AdwWrapLayout:natural-line-length-unit`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.WrapLayout.natural-line-length-unit.html) properties to enable that behavior.

See [`AdwWrapBox`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.WrapBox.html).

\[−\]

#### Description

Indicates an [`AdwAnimation`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Animation.html) with an infinite duration.

This value is mostly used internally.

# Adw – 1: CSS Variables

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html

#### CSS Variables

# CSS Variables [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html\#css-variables "Permanent link")

The Adwaita stylesheet provides a number of predefined CSS variables for colors
that can be used from applications.

# UI Colors [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html\#ui-colors "Permanent link")

These colors are used throughout the UI. They can differ between the light and
dark styles.

Many colors are grouped as background/foreground pairs. These colors are always
meant to be used together as the background and foreground color, for example:

```
my-widget {
  background-color: var(--accent-bg-color);
  color: var(--accent-fg-color);
}
```

Copy

Applications can override these colors by re-declaring them, for example:

```
:root {
  --accent-bg-color: #e01b24;
}
```

Copy

## Standalone colors [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html\#standalone-colors "Permanent link")

Some colors also have standalone versions. They are similar to the background
version, but provide better contrast when used as foreground colors on top of a
neutral background - for example, colorful text in a window.

```
my-widget {
  color: var(--accent-color);
}
```

Copy

Standalone colors are typically darker than the corresponding background color
for the light style, and lighter than the background for the dark style. They
are automatically derived from the background color, so it’s not necesssary to
override them manually when setting app-wide accent color.

However, when overriding the background colors for specific widgets, the
standalone colors must be overridden too, as follows:

```
my-widget {
  --accent-bg-color: var(--purple-3);
  --accent-color: oklab(from var(--accent-bg-color) var(--standalone-color-oklab));
}
```

Copy

The `--standalone-color-oklab` variable has the following values for light and
dark styles:

| Name | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--standalone-color-oklab` | `min(l, 0.5) a b` | `max(l, 0.85) a b` |

Note

Adjusting colors in the Oklab color space may produce colors outside of sRGB
gamut. These colors need to be gamut mapped in order to be displayed on
screen. This page lists colors after gamut mapping, and out of gamut colors
will be marked with an asterisk.

For example, the dark standalone color for blue accent color is
`oklab(0.850000 -0.081818 -0.053404)`, so
`color(srgb 0.504313 0.817230 1.218717)` when converted to sRGB. However,
the blue channel in this color is outside the \[0-1\] range and is clipped to
it before being displayed, so the end result is
`color(srgb 0.504313 0.817230 1)`, or `#81d0ff`.

## Accent Colors [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html\#accent-colors "Permanent link")

The accent color is used across many different widgets, often to indicate that a
widget is important, interactive, or currently active. Try to avoid using it on
large surfaces, or on too many items on the same view.

The [`.accent`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#colors) style class allows to use it for
widgets such as [`GtkLabel`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Label.html).

The background color is available as `--accent-bg-color`, the foreground as
`--accent-fg-color` and the standalone color as `--accent-color`.

The `--accent-color` color is derived from `--accent-bg-color` as detailed above.

The default values of these colors depend on the system preferences, and will
always be one of the following:

| Color |  | Background |  | Foreground |  | Standalone (Light) |  | Standalone (Dark) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Blue |  | `#3584e4` |  | `#ffffff` |  | `#0461be` |  | `#81d0ff` [\*](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#out-of-gamut-colors) |
| Teal |  | `#2190a4` |  | `#ffffff` |  | `#007184` [\*](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#out-of-gamut-colors) |  | `#7bdff4` |
| Green |  | `#3a944a` |  | `#ffffff` |  | `#15772e` |  | `#8de698` |
| Yellow |  | `#c88800` |  | `#ffffff` |  | `#905300` [\*](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#out-of-gamut-colors) |  | `#ffc057` [\*](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#out-of-gamut-colors) |
| Orange |  | `#ed5b00` |  | `#ffffff` |  | `#b62200` [\*](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#out-of-gamut-colors) |  | `#ff9c5b` [\*](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#out-of-gamut-colors) |
| Red |  | `#e62d42` |  | `#ffffff` |  | `#c00023` [\*](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#out-of-gamut-colors) |  | `#ff888c` [\*](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#out-of-gamut-colors) |
| Pink |  | `#d56199` |  | `#ffffff` |  | `#a2326c` |  | `#ffa0d8` [\*](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#out-of-gamut-colors) |
| Purple |  | `#9141ac` |  | `#ffffff` |  | `#8939a4` |  | `#fba7ff` [\*](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#out-of-gamut-colors) |
| Slate |  | `#6f8396` |  | `#ffffff` |  | `#526678` |  | `#bbd1e5` |

Each background color is also available as a variable, as follows:

| Name |  | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--accent-blue` |  | `#3584e4` |
| `--accent-teal` |  | `#2190a4` |
| `--accent-green` |  | `#3a944a` |
| `--accent-yellow` |  | `#c88800` |
| `--accent-orange` |  | `#ed5b00` |
| `--accent-red` |  | `#e62d42` |
| `--accent-pink` |  | `#d56199` |
| `--accent-purple` |  | `#9141ac` |
| `--accent-slate` |  | `#6f8396` |

## Destructive Colors [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html\#destructive-colors "Permanent link")

It’s used by [`GtkButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Button.html) and [`AdwButtonRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ButtonRow.html) with the
[`.destructive-action`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#destructive-action) style class.

The `--destructive-color` color is derived from `--destructive-bg-color` as
detailed above.

| Name |  | Light |  | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--destructive-bg-color` |  | `#e01b24` |  | `#c01c28` |
| `--destructive-fg-color` |  | `#ffffff` |  | `#ffffff` |
| `--destructive-color` |  | `#c30000` [\*](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#out-of-gamut-colors) |  | `#ff938c` [\*](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#out-of-gamut-colors) |
