## Header Bar Colors [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html\#header-bar-colors "Permanent link")

These colors are used for header bars and similar widgets, generally attached to
the top or bottom sides of a window. The full list of widgets using them:

- [`AdwToolbarView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToolbarView.html) uses it for the top and bottom bars
- [`AdwHeaderBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html) except with the
[`.flat`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#flat-header-bar) style class
- [`AdwTabBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabBar.html) except with the
[`.inline`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#inline-tab-bars-search-bars) style class
- [`GtkHeaderBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.HeaderBar.html) except with the
[`.flat`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#flat-header-bar) style class
- [`GtkSearchBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.SearchBar.html) except with the
[`.inline`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#inline-tab-bars-search-bars) style class
- [`GtkActionBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ActionBar.html)

| Name |  | Light |  | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--headerbar-bg-color` |  | `#ffffff` |  | `#2e2e32` |
| `--headerbar-fg-color` |  | `rgb(0 0 6 / 80%)` |  | `#ffffff` |
| `--headerbar-border-color` |  | `rgb(0 0 6 / 80%)` |  | `#ffffff` |
| `--headerbar-backdrop-color` |  | `#fafafb` |  | `#222226` |
| `--headerbar-shade-color` |  | `rgb(0 0 6 / 12%)` |  | `rgb(0 0 6 / 36%)` |
| `--headerbar-darker-shade-color` |  | `rgb(0 0 6 / 12%)` |  | `rgb(0 0 6 / 90%)` |

`--headerbar-border-color` has the same default value as `--headerbar-fg-color`,
but doesn’t change along with it. This can be useful if a light window has a
dark header bar with light text; in this case it may be desirable to keep the
border dark. This variable is only used for vertical borders - for example,
separators between the 2 header bars in a split header bar layout.

`--headerbar-backdrop-color` is used instead of `--headerbar-bg-color` when the
window is not focused. By default it’s an alias of
[`--window-bg-color`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#window-colors) and changes together with it. When
overriding header bar colors, make sure to set it to a value matching your
`--headerbar-bg-color`.

`--headerbar-shade-color` is used to provide a dark shadow or a border for
header bars and similar widgets. This color should always be partially
transparent black.

`--headerbar-darker-shade-color` is used for the [`ADW_TOOLBAR_RAISED_BORDER`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.ToolbarStyle.html#raised-border)
border. This color should always be partially transparent black, and is intended
to be darker than both `--headerbar-bg-color` and `--headerbar-backdrop-color`
on top of white color.

## Sidebar Colors [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html\#sidebar-colors "Permanent link")

These colors are used for sidebars, generally attached to the left or right
sides of a window. They are used by [`AdwNavigationSplitView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationSplitView.html) and
[`AdwOverlaySplitView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.OverlaySplitView.html) when they are not collapsed.

| Name |  | Light |  | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--sidebar-bg-color` |  | `#ebebed` |  | `#2e2e32` |
| `--sidebar-fg-color` |  | `rgb(0 0 6 / 80%)` |  | `#ffffff` |
| `--sidebar-backdrop-color` |  | `#f2f2f4` |  | `#28282c` |
| `--sidebar-border-color` |  | `rgb(0 0 6 / 7%)` |  | `rgb(0 0 6 / 36%)` |
| `--sidebar-shade-color` |  | `rgb(0 0 6 / 7%)` |  | `rgb(0 0 6 / 25%)` |

`--sidebar-backdrop-color` is used instead of `--sidebar-bg-color` when the
window is not focused. When overriding sidebar colors, make sure to set it to a
value matching your `--sidebar-bg-color`.

`--sidebar-shade-color` is used to provide a dark border for sidebars, scroll
undershoots within sidebars, as well as transitions in [`AdwNavigationView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationView.html),
[`AdwOverlaySplitView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.OverlaySplitView.html), [`AdwLeaflet`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Leaflet.html) and [`AdwFlap`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Flap.html). This color should
always be partially transparent black, with the opacity tuned to be well visible
on top of `--sidebar-bg-color`.

`--sidebar-border-color` is used to provide a dark border for sidebars. This
color should always be partially transparent black, with the opacity tuned to be
well visible on top of `--sidebar-bg-color` next to `--window-bg-color` or
`--view-bg-color`.

`--sidebar-shade-color`is used to provide scroll undershoots within sidebars, as
well as transitions in [`AdwNavigationView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationView.html), [`AdwOverlaySplitView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.OverlaySplitView.html),
[`AdwLeaflet`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Leaflet.html) and [`AdwFlap`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Flap.html). This color should always be partially
transparent black, with the opacity tuned to be well visible on top of
`--sidebar-bg-color`.

Since: 1.4

always be partially transparent black, with the opacity tuned to be well visible
on top of `--secondary-sidebar-bg-color`.

`--secondary-sidebar-shade-color` is used to provide a dark border for secondary
sidebars, scroll undershoots within secondary sidebars, as well as transitions
in [`AdwNavigationView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationView.html), [`AdwOverlaySplitView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.OverlaySplitView.html), [`AdwLeaflet`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Leaflet.html) and
[`AdwFlap`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Flap.html). This color should always be partially transparent black, with the
opacity tuned to be well visible on top of `--secondary-sidebar-bg-color`.

## Miscellaneous Colors [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html\#miscellaneous-colors "Permanent link")

| Name |  | Light |  | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--shade-color` |  | `rgb(0 0 6 / 7%)` |  | `rgb(0 0 6 / 25%)` |
| `--scrollbar-outline-color` |  | `#ffffff` |  | `rgb(0 0 6 / 50%)` |

`--shade-color` is used for scroll undershoots, as well as transitions in
[`AdwNavigationView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationView.html), [`AdwOverlaySplitView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.OverlaySplitView.html), [`AdwLeaflet`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Leaflet.html) and
[`AdwFlap`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Flap.html). This color should always be partially transparent black, with the
opacity tuned to be well visible on top of `--window-bg-color`.

`--scrollbar-outline-color` is used by [`GtkScrollbar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Scrollbar.html) to ensure that
overlay scrollbars are visible regardless of the content color. It should always
be the opposite of the scrollbar color - light with a dark scrollbar and dark otherwise.

# Fonts [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html\#fonts "Permanent link")

These variables allow to access system fonts. For each font, two variables are
defined, corresponding to the font family and size. Most of the time, they
should be used together, as follows:

```
.my-content {
  font-family: var(--monospace-font-family);
  font-size: var(--monospace-font-size);
}
```

Copy

## Document Font [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html\#document-font "Permanent link")

Document font should be used in articles, messages and other content.

It’s used for the [`.document`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#document)
style class.

| Name | Example Value |
| --- | --- |
| `--document-font-family` | Adwaita Sans |
| `--document-font-size` | 12pt |

## Monospace Font [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html\#monospace-font "Permanent link")

Monospace font should be used for displaying code, logs or shell commands.

It’s used for the [`.monospace`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#monospace)
style class.

| Name | Example Value |

| `--monospace-font-family` | Adwaita Mono |

# Helpers [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html\#helpers "Permanent link")

These variables are provided for convenience (particularly, automatic high
contrast mode support) and should not be overridden.

## Opacity [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html\#opacity "Permanent link")

| Name | Regular | High contrast |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--border-opacity` | `15%` | `50%` |
| `--dim-opacity` | `55%` | `90%` |
| `--disabled-opacity` | `50%` | `40%` |

These variables represent the commonly used opacity values.

`--border-opacity` is used for borders. (see [`--border-color`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#border-color))

`--dim-opacity` is used for the [`.dim`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#dimmed)
style class and other similar contexts, like window and row subtitles.

`--disabled-opacity` is used for disabled widgets.
(see [`GtkWidget:sensitive`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Widget.sensitive.html))

These variables can be used to automatically support high contrast mode.

## Border Color [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html\#border-color "Permanent link")

| Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `--border-color` | `color-mix(in srgb, currentColor var(--border-opacity), transparent)` |

Border color is derived from the current foreground color (`currentColor`) and
changes between regular and high contrast modes. It should be used to support
the high contrast mode automatically.

## Window Radius [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html\#window-radius "Permanent link")

| Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `--window-radius` | 15px |

Matches the current window radius, whether it’s floating or maximized. Can be
used for e.g. rounding focus rings next to the edge of the window while
automatically accounting for maximized, fullscreen etc modes.

# Compatibility Colors [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html\#compatibility-colors "Permanent link")

A number of colors have been available in Adwaita in GTK3. They are aliases of
UI colors or otherwise derived from them. These colors use the older
GTK-specific syntax for named colors rather than CSS variables, and don’t pick
up overridden colors. As such, it’s recommended to avoid using these colors entirely.

| `@theme_selected_bg_color` | [`@accent_bg_color`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#accent-colors) |
| `@theme_selected_fg_color` | [`@accent_fg_color`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#accent-colors) |

`ADW_EASE`

Cubic bezier tweening, with control points in (0.25, 0.1) and (0.25, 1.0).

Increases in velocity towards the middle of the animation, slowing back down
at the end.

- Value: `31`
- Available since: 1.7

`ADW_EASE_IN`

Cubic bezier tweening, with control points in (0.42, 0.0) and (1.0, 1.0).

Starts off slowly, with the speed of the animation increasing until complete.

- Value: `32`
- Available since: 1.7

`ADW_EASE_OUT`

Cubic bezier tweening, with control points in (0.0, 0.0) and (0.58, 1.0).

Starts quickly, slowing down the animation until complete.

- Value: `33`
- Available since: 1.7

`ADW_EASE_IN_OUT`

Cubic bezier tweening, with control points in (0.42, 0.0) and (0.58, 1.0).

Starts off slowly, speeds up in the middle, and then slows down again.

- Value: `34`
- Available since: 1.7

# Adw.FlapTransitionType

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.FlapTransitionType.html

deprecated: 1.4

\[−\]

#### Declaration

```
enum Adw.FlapTransitionType
```

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-flap.c\#L100 "go to source location")

Deprecated since: 1.4

See [the migration guide](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html#replace-adwflap).

Describes transitions types of a [`AdwFlap`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Flap.html) widget.

It determines the type of animation when transitioning between children in a
[`AdwFlap`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Flap.html) widget, as well as which areas can be swiped via
[`AdwFlap:swipe-to-open`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Flap.swipe-to-open.html) and [`AdwFlap:swipe-to-close`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Flap.swipe-to-close.html).

\[−\]

#### Members

`ADW_FLAP_TRANSITION_TYPE_OVER`

The flap slides over the content, which is
dimmed. When folded, only the flap can be swiped.

- Value: `0`
- Available since: 1

`ADW_FLAP_TRANSITION_TYPE_UNDER`

The content slides over the flap. Only the

# Adw.ToolbarStyle

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.ToolbarStyle.html

#### Declaration

```
enum Adw.ToolbarStyle
```

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-toolbar-view.c\#L120 "go to source location")

Available since: 1.4

Describes the possible top or bottom bar styles in an [`AdwToolbarView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToolbarView.html) widget.

[`ADW_TOOLBAR_FLAT`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.ToolbarStyle.html#flat) is suitable for simple content, such as
[`AdwStatusPage`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.StatusPage.html) or [`AdwPreferencesPage`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesPage.html), where the background at the

sidebars should always use this style.

![toolbar-view-flat-1](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/toolbar-view-flat-1.png)![toolbar-view-flat-2](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/toolbar-view-flat-2.png)

[`ADW_TOOLBAR_RAISED`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.ToolbarStyle.html#raised) style is suitable for content such as
[utility panes](https://developer.gnome.org/hig/patterns/containers/utility-panes.html),
where some elements are directly adjacent to the top/bottom bars, or
[`AdwTabView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabView.html), where each page can have a different background.

[`ADW_TOOLBAR_RAISED_BORDER`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.ToolbarStyle.html#raised-border) style is similar to
[`ADW_TOOLBAR_RAISED`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.ToolbarStyle.html#raised), but with the shadow replaced with a more
subtle border. It’s intended to be used in applications like image viewers,
where a shadow over the content might be undesired.

![toolbar-view-raised](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/toolbar-view-raised.png)![toolbar-view-raised-border](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/toolbar-view-raised-border.png)

See [`AdwToolbarView:top-bar-style`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ToolbarView.top-bar-style.html) and
[`AdwToolbarView:bottom-bar-style`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ToolbarView.bottom-bar-style.html).

New values may be added to this enumeration over time.

\[−\]

#### Members

`ADW_TOOLBAR_FLAT`

No background, shadow only for scrolled content.

- Value: `0`
- Available since: 1.4

`ADW_TOOLBAR_RAISED`

Opaque background with a persistent shadow.

- Value: `1`
- Available since: 1.4

# Adw.bind_property_to_css_class_full

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/func.bind_property_to_css_class_full.html

since: 1.10

\[−\]

#### Declaration  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-css-class-binding.h\#L82 "go to source location")

```
AdwCssClassBinding*
adw_bind_property_to_css_class_full (
  GObject* source,
  const char* source_property,
  GtkWidget* target,
  const char* target_css_class,
  GBindingFlags flags,
  AdwCssClassBindingMapToClassFunc map_to_class,
  AdwCssClassBindingMapToPropertyFunc map_to_property,
  gpointer user_data,
  GDestroyNotify notify
)
```

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-css-class-binding.c\#L698 "go to source location")

Creates a binding between a property on `source` and a CSS class on `target`
with a custom mapping.

Complete version of [`adw_bind_property_to_css_class()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/func.bind_property_to_css_class.html).

Whenever `source_property` is changed the `target_css_class` is toggled either
on or off on `target` using the boolean value of `source_property`.

For instance:

```
adw_bind_property_to_css_class (action, "active", widget, "active-widget", 0);
```

Copy

will result in the `active-widget`CSS class on the widget instance being
applied when `active` is `TRUE`, and `active-widget` being removed when
`active` is `FALSE`.

The binding will automatically be removed when either the `source` or `target`
instances are finalized. To remove the binding without affecting the `source`
or `target`, call [`g_object_unref()`](https://docs.gtk.org/gobject/method.Object.unref.html) on the returned binding. It is
recommended to only call [`g_object_unref()`](https://docs.gtk.org/gobject/method.Object.unref.html) when it is clear that
both `source` and `target` will outlive the binding.

This function is not thread safe. A source can have multiple bindings.

Available since: 1.10

This function is not directly available to language bindings.

# Adw.bind_property_to_css_class_with_closures

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/func.bind_property_to_css_class_with_closures.html

since: 1.10

\[−\]

#### Declaration  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-css-class-binding.h\#L93 "go to source location")

```
AdwCssClassBinding*
adw_bind_property_to_css_class_with_closures (
  GObject* source,
  const char* source_property,
  GtkWidget* target,
  const char* target_css_class,
  GBindingFlags flags,
  GClosure* map_to_class,
  GClosure* map_to_property
)
```

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-css-class-binding.c\#L933 "go to source location")

Creates a binding between a property on `source` and a CSS class on `target`
with a custom mapping using closures.

This function is the language bindings friendly version of
[`adw_bind_property_to_css_class_full()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/func.bind_property_to_css_class_full.html).

The binding will automatically be removed when either the `source` or `target`
instances are finalized. To remove the binding without affecting the `source`
or `target`, call [`g_object_unref()`](https://docs.gtk.org/gobject/method.Object.unref.html) on the returned binding. It is
recommended to only call [`g_object_unref()`](https://docs.gtk.org/gobject/method.Object.unref.html) when it is clear that
both `source` and `target` will outlive the binding.

This function is not thread safe. A source can have multiple bindings.

See also: [`adw_bind_property_to_css_class()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/func.bind_property_to_css_class.html).

Available since: 1.10

This function is renamed to [`adw_bind_property_to_css_class_full()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/func.bind_property_to_css_class_full.html) in language bindings.

# Adw.bind_property_to_css_class

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/func.bind_property_to_css_class.html

since: 1.10

\[−\]

#### Declaration  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-css-class-binding.h\#L75 "go to source location")

```
AdwCssClassBinding*
adw_bind_property_to_css_class (
  GObject* source,
  const char* source_property,
  GtkWidget* target,
  const char* target_css_class,
  GBindingFlags flags
)
```

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-css-class-binding.c\#L647 "go to source location")

Creates a binding between a property on `source` and a CSS class on `target`.

Whenever `source_property` is changed the `target_css_class` is toggled either
on or off on `target` using the boolean value of `source_property`.

For instance:

```
adw_bind_property_to_css_class (action, "active", widget, "active-widget", 0);
```

Copy

will result in the `active-widget`CSS class on the widget instance being
applied when `active` is `TRUE`, and `active-widget` being removed when
`active` is `FALSE`.

The binding will automatically be removed when either the `source` or `target`
instances are finalized. To remove the binding without affecting the `source`
or `target`, call [`g_object_unref()`](https://docs.gtk.org/gobject/method.Object.unref.html) on the returned binding. It is
recommended to only call [`g_object_unref()`](https://docs.gtk.org/gobject/method.Object.unref.html) when it is clear that
both `source` and `target` will outlive the binding.

This function is not thread safe. A source can have multiple bindings.

See also: [`adw_bind_property_to_css_class_full()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/func.bind_property_to_css_class_full.html).

Available since: 1.10

\[−\]

#### Parameters

`source`

_Type:_ [`GObject`](https://docs.gtk.org/gobject/class.Object.html)

The source object.

|     |
| --- |
| The data is owned by the caller of the function. |

`source_property`

_Type:_`const char*`

The property on `source` to bind.

|     |
| --- |
| The data is owned by the caller of the function. |
| The value is a NUL terminated UTF-8 string. |

`target`

_Type:_ [`GtkWidget`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Widget.html)

The target widget.

|     |
| --- |
| The data is owned by the caller of the function. |

`target_css_class`

_Type:_`const char*`

The CSS class on `target` to bind.

|     |
| --- |
| The data is owned by the caller of the function. |
| The value is a NUL terminated UTF-8 string. |

`flags`

_Type:_ [`GBindingFlags`](https://docs.gtk.org/gobject/flags.BindingFlags.html)

Flags to pass to `self`.

|
|


\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-main.c\#L63 "go to source location")

Initializes Libadwaita.

This function can be used instead of [`gtk_init()`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/func.init.html) as it initializes GTK implicitly.

There’s no need to call this function if you’re using [`AdwApplication`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Application.html).

If Libadwaita has already been initialized, the function will simply return.

This makes sure translations, types, themes, and icons for the Adwaita
library are set up properly.

# Adw.Swipeable

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/iface.Swipeable.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-swipeable.c\#L11 "go to source location")

```
interface Adw.Swipeable : Gtk.Widget
```

An interface for swipeable widgets.

The `AdwSwipeable` interface is implemented by all swipeable widgets.

See [`AdwSwipeTracker`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SwipeTracker.html) for details about implementing it.

\[−\]

In order to implement Swipeable, your type must inherit from [`GtkWidget`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Widget.html).

# Adw – 1: Initialization

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/initialization.html

#### Initialization

# Initialization [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/initialization.html\#initialization "Permanent link")

Before using Libadwaita, it must be initialized. There are two ways of doing this.

## Using `AdwApplication` (Recommended) [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/initialization.html\#using-adwapplication-recommended "Permanent link")

[`AdwApplication`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Application.html) automatically initializes Libadwaita if used instead of
[`GtkApplication`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Application.html).

Example:

```
#include <adwaita.h>

static void
activate_cb (GtkApplication *app)
{
  GtkWidget *window = gtk_application_window_new (app);
  GtkWidget *label = gtk_label_new ("Hello World");

  gtk_window_set_title (GTK_WINDOW (window), "Hello");
  gtk_window_set_default_size (GTK_WINDOW (window), 200, 200);
  gtk_window_set_child (GTK_WINDOW (window), label);
  gtk_window_present (GTK_WINDOW (window));
}

int
main (int   argc,
      char *argv[])
{
  g_autoptr (AdwApplication) app = NULL;

  app = adw_application_new ("org.example.Hello", G_APPLICATION_DEFAULT_FLAGS);

  g_signal_connect (app, "activate", G_CALLBACK (activate_cb), NULL);

  return g_application_run (G_APPLICATION (app), argc, argv);
}
```

Copy

After building and running, the application will look like this:

![hello-world](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/hello-world.png)

## Using `adw_init()` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/initialization.html\#using-adw_init "Permanent link")

If using [`AdwApplication`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Application.html) is not possible, use [`adw_init()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/func.init.html) instead. It can be
called instead of [`gtk_init()`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/func.init.html).

Example:

```
#include <adwaita.h>

int
main (int   argc,
      char *argv[])
{
  GtkWidget *window, *label;

  adw_init ();

  window = gtk_window_new ();
  label = gtk_label_new ("Hello World");

  gtk_window_set_title (GTK_WINDOW (window), "Hello");
  gtk_window_set_default_size (GTK_WINDOW (window), 200, 200);
  gtk_window_set_child (GTK_WINDOW (window), label);
  gtk_window_present (GTK_WINDOW (window));

   while (g_list_model_get_n_items (gtk_window_get_toplevels ()) > 0)
    g_main_context_iteration (NULL, TRUE);

  return 0;
}
```

Copy

# Adw – 1: Migrating from Libhandy 1.4 to Libadwaita

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html

#### Migrating from Libhandy 1.4 to Libadwaita

# Migrating from Libhandy 1.4 to Libadwaita [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#migrating-from-libhandy-14-to-libadwaita "Permanent link")

Libadwaita is being developed as a successor to Libhandy 1.4. As such, it
offers to GTK 4 many features Libhandy was offering to GTK 3.

Migrating from Libhandy 1.4 to Libadwaita implies migrating from GTK 3 to 4.
This guide only focuses on on Libhandy and Libadwaita, and is designed to be
used together with the [GTK 3 to 4 migration guide](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/migrating-3to4.html).

If you notice that some differences between Libhandy and Libadwaita are missing
in this guide, [please report them](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/issues/).

# Preparation in Libhandy 1.4 [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#preparation-in-libhandy-14 "Permanent link")

The steps outlined in the following sections assume that your software is
working with Libhandy 1.4, which is the latest stable release of Libhandy 1.x.
It includes all the necessary APIs and tools to help you port your software to
Libadwaita. If you are using an older version of Libhandy, you should first get
your software to build and work with Libhandy 1.4.

## Do not Use Deprecated Symbols [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#do-not-use-deprecated-symbols "Permanent link")

Over the years, a number of functions, and in some cases, entire widgets have
been deprecated. These deprecations are clearly spelled out in the API
reference, with hints about the recommended replacements. The API reference for
Libhandy 1.4 also includes an [index](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libhandy/doc/1-latest/deprecated-api-index.html)
of all deprecated symbols.

## Subclassing [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#subclassing "Permanent link")

Following GTK4’s emphasis on composition and delegation over subclassing,
[`AdwLeaflet`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Leaflet.html) and [`AdwHeaderBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html) are no longer derivable. As a replacement,
you can subclass `GtkBin` or [`GtkBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Box.html) and include a leaflet or a header
bar as a child widget.

## Stop Using `HdyKeypad` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#stop-using-hdykeypad "Permanent link")

`HdyKeypad` has been removed from Libadwaita. Applications that had used it can
copy it in tree instead.

## Stop Using Named WM Colors [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#stop-using-named-wm-colors "Permanent link")

The following named colors have been removed from the stylesheet in Libadwaita:

- `@content_view_bg`
- `@text_view_bg`
- `@wm_title`
- `@wm_unfocused_title`
- `@wm_highlight`
- `@wm_borders_edge`
- `@wm_bg_a`
- `@wm_bg_b`
- `@wm_shadow`
- `@wm_border`
- `@wm_button_hover_color_a`
- `@wm_button_hover_color_b`
- `@wm_button_active_color_a`
- `@wm_button_active_color_b`
- `@wm_button_active_color_c`

Applications should not use them.

## Use `HdyFlap` Properties for Adding Children Instead of `gtk_container_add()` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#use-hdyflap-properties-for-adding-children-instead-of-gtk_container_add "Permanent link")

`HdyFlap` provides the `content`, `flap` and `separator` properties that can be
used for managing children instead of `GtkContainer`API. In Libadwaita
[`AdwFlap:content`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Flap.content.html), [`AdwFlap:flap`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Flap.flap.html) and [`AdwFlap:separator`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Flap.separator.html) are
the only way to manage [`AdwFlap`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Flap.html) children.

## Stop Using `HdyValueObject` with non-string values [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#stop-using-hdyvalueobject-with-non-string-values "Permanent link")

`HdyValueObject` has been removed. While it’s not practical to replace the cases
where it’s storing strings in GTK3, as the preferred replacement only exists in
4, it can also be used with any other [`GValue`](https://docs.gtk.org/gobject/struct.Value.html). That use has no
replacement and you can instead create your own objects to store those values.

## Use `HdyStyleManager` Instead of [`GtkSettings:gtk-application-prefer-dark-theme`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Settings.gtk-application-prefer-dark-theme.html) [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#use-hdystylemanager-instead-of-gtksettingsgtk-application-prefer-dark-theme "Permanent link")

If your application is setting [`GtkSettings:gtk-application-prefer-dark-theme`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Settings.gtk-application-prefer-dark-theme.html)
to `TRUE` to request dark appearance, consider setting `HdyStyleManager:color-scheme`
to `HDY_COLOR_SCHEME_PREFER_DARK` and making sure the application can work with
light appearance as well. If that’s not possible, set it to
`HDY_COLOR_SCHEME_FORCE_DARK` instead.

If your application is using light appearance, consider setting the color scheme
to `HDY_COLOR_SCHEME_PREFER_LIGHT` and support dark appearance.

In libadwaita color schemes will be the only way to request dark appearance.

# Changes that Need to Be Done at the Time of the Switch [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#changes-that-need-to-be-done-at-the-time-of-the-switch "Permanent link")

This section outlines porting tasks that you need to tackle when you get to the
point that you actually build your application against Libadwaita 1. Making it
possible to prepare for these in GTK 3 would have been either impossible or impractical.

## Adapt to `GtkContainer` Removal [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-gtkcontainer-removal "Permanent link")

Same as GTK itself, all widgets that have children have a new API to replace
`gtk_container_add()` and `gtk_container_remove()`.

The following widgets that formerly subclassed `GtkBin` have a `child` property now:

- [`AdwClamp`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Clamp.html)
- [`AdwStatusPage`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.StatusPage.html)

[`AdwWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Window.html) and [`AdwApplicationWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ApplicationWindow.html) have a `content` property instead.

For other widgets use the following replacements:

| Widget | `gtk_container_add()` replacement | `gtk_container_remove()` replacement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`AdwActionRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ActionRow.html) | [`adw_action_row_add_suffix()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.ActionRow.add_suffix.html) | [`adw_action_row_remove()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.ActionRow.remove.html) |
| [`AdwCarousel`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Carousel.html) | [`adw_carousel_append()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Carousel.append.html) | [`adw_carousel_remove()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Carousel.remove.html) |
| [`AdwExpanderRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ExpanderRow.html) | [`adw_expander_row_add_row()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.ExpanderRow.add_row.html) | [`adw_expander_row_remove()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.ExpanderRow.remove.html) |
| [`AdwLeaflet`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Leaflet.html) | [`adw_leaflet_append()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Leaflet.append.html) | [`adw_leaflet_remove()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Leaflet.remove.html) |
| [`AdwPreferencesGroup`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesGroup.html) | [`adw_preferences_group_add()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.PreferencesGroup.add.html) | [`adw_preferences_group_remove()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.PreferencesGroup.remove.html) |
| [`AdwPreferencesPage`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesPage.html) | [`adw_preferences_page_add()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.PreferencesPage.add.html) | [`adw_preferences_page_remove()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.PreferencesPage.remove.html) |
| [`AdwPreferencesWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesWindow.html) | [`adw_preferences_window_add()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.PreferencesWindow.add.html) | [`adw_preferences_window_remove()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.PreferencesWindow.remove.html) |

Adding children in a UI file still works.

## Adapt to `HdySearchBar` Removal [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-hdysearchbar-removal "Permanent link")

`HdySearchBar` has been removed, use [`GtkSearchBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.SearchBar.html) instead.

## Adapt to `HdyWindowHandle` Removal [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-hdywindowhandle-removal "Permanent link")

`HdyWindowHandle` has been removed, use [`GtkWindowHandle`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.WindowHandle.html) instead.

## Adapt to [`AdwActionRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ActionRow.html) and [`AdwExpanderRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ExpanderRow.html) API Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-adwactionrow-and-adwexpanderrow-api-changes "Permanent link")

The `use-underline` property and its accessors have been removed. Use
[`AdwPreferencesRow:use-underline`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.PreferencesRow.use-underline.html) and its accessors instead.

The title and subtitle have markup enabled, make sure to escape it with
[`g_markup_escape_text()`](https://docs.gtk.org/glib/func.markup_escape_text.html) if this is unwanted.

## Adapt to [`AdwClamp`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Clamp.html) API Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-adwclamp-api-changes "Permanent link")

`HdyClamp` previously had `.small`, `.medium` or `.large` style classes
depending on the current size of its child. These style classes are now
added to the child instead of the clamp itself.

## Adapt to [`AdwComboRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ComboRow.html) API Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-adwcomborow-api-changes "Permanent link")

[`AdwComboRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ComboRow.html) API has been completely overhauled compared to `HdyComboRow`
and closely mirrors [`GtkDropDown`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.DropDown.html). Refer to [`GtkDropDown`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.DropDown.html)‘s
documentation for details.

`hdy_combo_row_bind_name_model()` can be replaced with using the
[`AdwComboRow:model`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ComboRow.model.html) property in conjunction with
[`AdwComboRow:expression`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ComboRow.expression.html).

`hdy_combo_row_bind_model()` can be replaced with using the
[`AdwComboRow:model`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ComboRow.model.html) property in conjunction with
[`AdwComboRow:factory`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ComboRow.factory.html) and/or [`AdwComboRow:list-factory`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ComboRow.list-factory.html).

`hdy_combo_row_set_for_enum()` can be replaced with a [`GtkEnumList`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.EnumList.html)
in conjunction with the [`AdwComboRow:expression`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ComboRow.expression.html) property, for example:

```
expr = gtk_property_expression_new (GTK_TYPE_ENUM_LIST_ITEM, NULL, "nick");
model = G_LIST_MODEL (gtk_enum_list_model_new (GTK_TYPE_ORIENTATION));

adw_combo_row_set_expression (row, expr);
adw_combo_row_set_model (row, model);
```

Copy

As with [`GtkDropDown`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.DropDown.html), if the model is a [`GtkStringList`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.StringList.html), the
model items can be converted into human-readable strings automatically without
requiring an expression.

The `HdyComboRow:selected-index` property has been renamed to
[`AdwComboRow:selected`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ComboRow.selected.html) and its type changed from `gint` to `guint`, matching [`GtkDropDown`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.DropDown.html).

## Adapt to [`AdwPreferencesGroup`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesGroup.html) API Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-adwpreferencesgroup-api-changes "Permanent link")

`HdyPreferencesGroup:use-markup` has been removed, the labels always use markup now.

## Adapt to `HdyEnumValueObject` API Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-hdyenumvalueobject-api-changes "Permanent link")

`HdyEnumValueObject` has been replaced with [`GtkEnumListItem`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.EnumListItem.html) and can no longer
be manually created. It’s only intended to be used with [`GtkEnumList`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.EnumList.html).

## Stop Using `HdyValueObject` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#stop-using-hdyvalueobject "Permanent link")

`HdyValueObject` has been removed. The typical use for storing strings in
combination with [`GListStore`](https://docs.gtk.org/gio/class.ListStore.html) can be replaced by using
[`GtkStringList`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.StringList.html).

## Adapt to [`AdwHeaderBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html) API Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-adwheaderbar-api-changes "Permanent link")

[`AdwHeaderBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html) API mostly mirrors [`GtkHeaderBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.HeaderBar.html), refer to the
[GTK 3 to 4 migration guide](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/migrating-3to4.html#adapt-to-gtkheaderbar-and-gtkactionbar-api-changes)
for details

The [`GtkHeaderBar:show-title-buttons`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.HeaderBar.show-title-buttons.html) property has been split into
[`AdwHeaderBar:show-start-title-buttons`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.show-start-title-buttons.html) and
[`AdwHeaderBar:show-end-title-buttons`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.show-end-title-buttons.html) to simplify creating multi-pane
layouts. The corresponding getter and the setter have been split as well.

The [`AdwWindowTitle`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.WindowTitle.html) widget may be useful for replacing the title and subtitle.

## Adapt to `HdyHeaderGroup` Removal [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-hdyheadergroup-removal "Permanent link")

`HdyHeaderGroup` has been removed. Its behavior can be replicated by changing
the [`AdwHeaderBar:show-start-title-buttons`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.show-start-title-buttons.html) and
[`AdwHeaderBar:show-end-title-buttons`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.show-end-title-buttons.html) properties depending on the layout,
for example binding them to the [`AdwLeaflet:folded`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Leaflet.folded.html) property as follows:

```
<object class="AdwLeaflet" id="leaflet">
  <child>
    <object class="GtkBox">
      <property name="orientation">vertical</property>
      <object class="AdwHeaderBar">
        <binding name="show-end-title-buttons">
          <lookup name="folded">leaflet</lookup>
        </binding>
      </object>
      ...
    </object>
  </child>
  ...
  <child>
    <object class="GtkBox">
       <property name="orientation">vertical</property>
      <object class="AdwHeaderBar">
        <binding name="show-start-title-buttons">
          <lookup name="folded">leaflet</lookup>
        </binding>
      </object>
      ...
    </object>
  </child>
</object>
```

## Adapt to `HdyDeck` Removal [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-hdydeck-removal "Permanent link")

`HdyDeck` has been removed. Instead, an [`AdwLeaflet`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Leaflet.html) can be used the same way
by setting the [`AdwLeaflet:can-unfold`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Leaflet.can-unfold.html) property to `FALSE`.

## Adapt to [`AdwLeaflet`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Leaflet.html) and [`AdwSqueezer`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Squeezer.html) API Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-adwleaflet-and-adwsqueezer-api-changes "Permanent link")

The child properties of `HdyLeaflet` and `HdySqueezer` have been converted into
page objects, similarly to [`GtkStack`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Stack.html). For example,
[`adw_squeezer_page_set_enabled()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.SqueezerPage.set_enabled.html) should be used to replace
`hdy_squeezer_set_child_enabled()`.

The `can-swipe-back` and `can-swipe-forward` properties have been renamed to
[`AdwLeaflet:can-navigate-back`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Leaflet.can-navigate-back.html) and
[`AdwLeaflet:can-navigate-forward`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Leaflet.can-navigate-forward.html), along with their accessors. The new
properties also handle keyboard and mouse shortcuts in addition to swipes.

The `hhomogeneous-folded`, `vhomogeneous-folded`, `hhomogeneous-unfolded`, and
`vhomogeneous-unfolded` properties have been replaced by a single
[`AdwLeaflet:homogeneous`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Leaflet.homogeneous.html) property, set to `TRUE` by default, applied when
the leaflet is folded for the opposite orientation.

When unfolded, children are never homogeneous. Use [`GtkSizeGroup`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.SizeGroup.html)
to make them homogeneous if needed.

The `interpolate-size` property has been removed with no replacement, it’s
always enabled when [`AdwLeaflet:homogeneous`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Leaflet.homogeneous.html) is set to `FALSE`.

`AdwLeaflet` now uses spring animations instead of timed animations for child
transitions. As such, the `child-transition-duration` property has been replaced
with [`AdwLeaflet:child-transition-params`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Leaflet.child-transition-params.html), allowing to customize the
animation. Unlike the duration, spring parameters are also used for animation
triggered by swipe gestures.

## Adapt to [`AdwFlap`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Flap.html) API Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-adwflap-api-changes "Permanent link")

`AdwFlap` now uses spring animations instead of timed animations for reveal
animations. As such, the `reveal-duration` property has been replaced with
[`AdwFlap:reveal-params`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Flap.reveal-params.html), allowing to customize the animation. Unlike
the duration, spring parameters are also used for transitions triggered by swipe gestures.

## Adapt to [`AdwCarousel`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Carousel.html) API changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-adwcarousel-api-changes "Permanent link")

`AdwCarousel` now uses spring animations instead of timed animations for
scrolling. As such, the `animation-duration` property has been replaced with
[`AdwCarousel:scroll-params`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Carousel.scroll-params.html), allowing to customize the animation. Unlike
the duration, spring parameters are also used for animation triggered by swipe gestures.

The `adw_carousel_scroll_to_full()` method has been removed. Instead,
[`adw_carousel_scroll_to()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Carousel.scroll_to.html) has got an additional parameter `animate`.

## Adapt to View Switcher API Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-view-switcher-api-changes "Permanent link")

[`AdwViewSwitcher`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcher.html), [`AdwViewSwitcherBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherBar.html) and [`AdwViewSwitcherTitle`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherTitle.html) now
use [`AdwViewStack`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewStack.html) instead of [`GtkStack`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Stack.html).

You should stop using [`GtkStack:transition-type`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Stack.transition-type.html),
[`GtkStack:transition-duration`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Stack.transition-duration.html),
[`GtkStack:transition-running`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Stack.transition-running.html) and
[`GtkStack:interpolate-size`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Stack.interpolate-size.html) properties before switching to
[`AdwViewStack`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewStack.html).

The `auto` view switcher policy has been removed. [`AdwViewSwitcher`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcher.html) only has
narrow and wide policies; if you had used the `auto` policy, use an
[`AdwSqueezer`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Squeezer.html) with two view switchers inside.

### Adapt to [`AdwViewSwitcher`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcher.html) API Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-adwviewswitcher-api-changes "Permanent link")

The `narrow-ellipsize` property has been removed. Narrow view switchers always
ellipsize their labels, wide switchers never do.

### Adapt to [`AdwViewSwitcherBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherBar.html) API Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-adwviewswitcherbar-api-changes "Permanent link")

The `policy` property has been removed. If you had used it, use a plain
[`AdwViewSwitcher`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcher.html) in a [`GtkActionBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ActionBar.html) instead.

### Adapt to [`AdwViewSwitcherTitle`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherTitle.html) API Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-adwviewswitchertitle-api-changes "Permanent link")

The `policy` property has been removed, the behavior is similar to the removed
`auto` policy. If you had used `wide` or `narrow` policies, use an
[`AdwSqueezer`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Squeezer.html) with an [`AdwViewSwitcher`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcher.html) and an [`AdwWindowTitle`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.WindowTitle.html) inside,
with the switcher having the desired policy.

## Adapt to [`AdwAvatar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Avatar.html) API Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-adwavatar-api-changes "Permanent link")

The `HdyAvatar:loadable-icon` property has been removed along with its getter
and setter. It can be replaced by [`AdwAvatar:custom-image`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Avatar.custom-image.html).

The `hdy_avatar_draw_to_pixbuf()` and `hdy_avatar_draw_to_pixbuf_async()`
functions have been removed, use the newly added [`adw_avatar_draw_to_texture()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Avatar.draw_to_texture.html)
instead. [`GdkTexture`](https://docs.gtk.org/gdk4/class.Texture.html) implements [`GIcon`](https://docs.gtk.org/gio/iface.Icon.html), so it should just work
for that case.

[`adw_avatar_draw_to_texture()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Avatar.draw_to_texture.html) does not have the `size` parameter. Instead, it
uses the avatar’s current size, with no replacement.

## Adapt to [`AdwStyleManager`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.StyleManager.html) API Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-adwstylemanager-api-changes "Permanent link")

When used with the default style manager, [`ADW_COLOR_SCHEME_DEFAULT`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.ColorScheme.html#default) is now
equivalent to [`ADW_COLOR_SCHEME_PREFER_LIGHT`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.ColorScheme.html#prefer-light) instead of
`HDY_COLOR_SCHEME_FORCE_LIGHT`, following the system dark style preference by
default. Make sure your application works with it, or otherwise set the
[`ADW_COLOR_SCHEME_FORCE_LIGHT`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.ColorScheme.html#force-light) color scheme manually.

## Adapt to [`AdwSwipeTracker`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SwipeTracker.html) API Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-adwswipetracker-api-changes "Permanent link")

The [`AdwSwipeTracker::begin-swipe`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.SwipeTracker.begin-swipe.html) signal is now emitted immediately before
the swipe starts, after the drag threshold has been reached, and it has lost its
`direction` parameter. The new [`AdwSwipeTracker::prepare`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.SwipeTracker.prepare.html) signal behaves
exactly like `begin-swipe` did, and can be used instead of it.

The type of the `duration` parameter in [`AdwSwipeTracker::end-swipe`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.SwipeTracker.end-swipe.html) has
changed from `gint64` to `guint`.

## Adapt to [`AdwTabView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabView.html) API Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-adwtabview-api-changes "Permanent link")

The `HdyTabView:shortcut-widget` property has been removed with no replacement;
[`AdwTabView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabView.html) automatically installs shortcuts with the
[`GTK_SHORTCUT_SCOPE_MANAGED`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.ShortcutScope.html#managed) scope, so they are automatically available
throughout the window without the need to set shortcut widget.

If some of these shortcuts conflict with another widget, the latter has
priority, and it should work automatically if the widget correctly stops event propagation.

## Adapt to [`AdwPreferencesWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesWindow.html) API Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-adwpreferenceswindow-api-changes "Permanent link")

The `can-swipe-back` property have been renamed to
[`AdwPreferencesWindow:can-navigate-back`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.PreferencesWindow.can-navigate-back.html), along with its accessors. The
new properties also handle keyboard and mouse shortcuts in addition to swipes.

## Adapt to Miscellaneous Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-miscellaneous-changes "Permanent link")

The `hdy_ease_out_cubic()` function has been removed. Instead,
[`adw_easing_ease()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/type_func.Easing.ease.html) can be used with the [`ADW_EASE_OUT_CUBIC`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.Easing.html#ease-out-cubic) parameter.

## Adapt to Stylesheet Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-stylesheet-changes "Permanent link")

If you were using
[`@theme_selected_bg_color`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#compatibility-colors)
as a text color, use
[`@accent_color`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#accent-colors) instead to
make sure the text is readable. You can also use the
[`.accent`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#colors) style class to apply the correct color.

## Stop Using the `.sidebar` Style Class [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#stop-using-the-sidebar-style-class "Permanent link")

The [`.sidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#sidebar) style class is now deprecated,
although still works for compatibility reasons. The main use case - adjusting
the background color of [`GtkListBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListBox.html) and [`GtkListView`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListView.html) \- can now
be done with the [`.navigation-sidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#sidebars) style
class on those widgets instead, along with adjusting the item selection style.
The border can be replicated by manually adding a [`GtkSeparator`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Separator.html).

## Adapt to the `popover.combo` Style Removal [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-the-popovercombo-style-removal "Permanent link")

The `.combo` popover style class has been removed. Use
[`.menu`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#menu-popovers) instead. You may need to remove
manually added margins, padding or minimum height from the list items inside
while doing it.

## Adapt to the `button.list-button` Style Removal [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-the-buttonlist-button-style-removal "Permanent link")

The `.list-button` style class has been removed with no replacement. The regular
button style should be used instead.

## Adapt to the `content-view` Style Removal [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-the-content-view-style-removal "Permanent link")

The `.content-view` style class has been removed. The selection mode
[`GtkCheckButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.CheckButton.html) style had inside content views has been split out into a
separate style class
[`.selection-mode`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#selection-mode-check-buttons) that can be
applied directly onto check buttons instead of the view. The unique background
color has no replacement and the default background should be used instead.

### Adapt to Header Bar, Action Bar, Search Bar and Toolbar Style Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-header-bar-action-bar-search-bar-and-toolbar-style-changes "Permanent link")

When possible, buttons in [`GtkHeaderBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.HeaderBar.html), [`GtkActionBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ActionBar.html) and
[`GtkSearchBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.SearchBar.html) will use flat appearance by default.

The following rules are used when deciding when to make buttons flat or not:

The following buttons get flat appearance:

- Icon-only buttons;
- Buttons with an icon and a label (using [`AdwButtonContent`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ButtonContent.html));
- Menu buttons containing an arrow;
- [`AdwSplitButton`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SplitButton.html);
- Any other button with the [`.flat`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#flat) style class.

The following buttons keep default appearance:

- Text-only buttons;
- Buttons with other content;
- Buttons within widgets containing the
[`.linked`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#linked-controls) class;
- Buttons with the [`.suggested-action`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#suggested-action) or
[`.opaque`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#opaque) style classes;
- Buttons with the [`.destructive-action`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#destructive-action)
style class;
- Buttons with the [`.raised`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#raised) style class.

It’s important to avoid ambiguous layouts, for example text-only buttons with
no icon, since such a button would be indistinguishable from the window title
without hovering it.

In rare cases, the existing layout may need a redesign to work with the new style.

The same rules are also used for the [`.toolbar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#toolbars)
style class now, instead of making every button appear flat.

### Adapt to List Style Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adapt-to-list-style-changes "Permanent link")

For boxed lists we now have the
[`.boxed-list`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#boxed-lists-cards) style class that matches
the name of the design pattern. If you were using the
[`.content`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#content) style class, you should use
`.boxed-list` instead.

The `.content` style class currently remains for compatibility purposes.

Neither the `.content` style class nor the `.boxed-list` style class work
for [`GtkListView`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListView.html), as the widget cannot currently be used for the
boxed list pattern.

### Adjusting Icons [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adjusting-icons "Permanent link")

If you’re bundling icons from the icon library with your application, make sure
to update them. Many icons have been redrawn to be larger to work better without
button frames.

If you’re using the `object-select-symbolic` icon in a header bar button
(typically for selection mode), use `selection-mode-symbolic` instead.

### Adjusting Icon+Arrow Menu Buttons [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adjusting-iconarrow-menu-buttons "Permanent link")

If you had menu buttons containing an icon and a dropdown arrow, switch to
[`GtkMenuButton:icon-name`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.MenuButton.icon-name.html) and set the
[`GtkMenuButton:always-show-arrow`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.MenuButton.always-show-arrow.html) property to `TRUE`.

### Adjusting Text-only Buttons [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adjusting-text-only-buttons "Permanent link")

If you had text-only buttons, consider using [`AdwButtonContent`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ButtonContent.html). For example,
the following button:

```
<object class="GtkButton">
  <property name="label" translatable="yes">_Open</property>
  <property name="use-underline">True</property>
</object>
```

Copy

can be changed into:

```
<object class="GtkButton">
  <property name="child">
    <object class="AdwButtonContent">
      <property name="icon-name">document-open-symbolic</property>
      <property name="label" translatable="yes">_Open</property>
      <property name="use-underline">True</property>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

One exception are the two primary buttons in a dialog, for example, “Cancel” and
“Open”. Those buttons should retain their default appearance.

### Adjusting Split Buttons [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adjusting-split-buttons "Permanent link")

If you had split buttons implemented via a [`GtkBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Box.html) with the
[`.linked`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#linked-controls) style class and two buttons
packed inside, use [`AdwSplitButton`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SplitButton.html) as follows:

```
<object class="AdwSplitButton">
  <property name="menu-model">some_menu</property>
  <property name="icon-name">view-list-symbolic</property>
</object>
```

Copy

### Adjusting Linked Buttons [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#adjusting-linked-buttons "Permanent link")

For other linked together buttons, simply stop linking them.

If multiple linked groups were used to separate different groups of actions,
insert extra spacing as follows:

```
<object class="GtkSeparator">
  <style>
    <class name="spacer"/>
  </style>
</object>
```

Copy

### Custom Adjustments [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html\#custom-adjustments "Permanent link")

The [`.flat`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#flat) and
[`.raised`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#raised) style classes can always be used to
override the default appearance.

Important

The [`GtkButton:has-frame`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Button.has-frame.html) property will **not** be set to `FALSE`
when a button gets the flat appearance automatically. It also cannot be set
to `TRUE` to make a button raised, the style class should be used directly instead.
