# Adw – 1: Migrating to Adaptive Dialogs

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-adaptive-dialogs.html

#### Migrating to Adaptive Dialogs

# Migrating to Adaptive Dialogs [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-adaptive-dialogs.html\#migrating-to-adaptive-dialogs "Permanent link")

Libadwaita 1.5 introduces [`AdwDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Dialog.html) and replacements for
[`AdwMessageDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.MessageDialog.html), [`AdwPreferencesWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesWindow.html) and [`AdwAboutWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AboutWindow.html) that
derive from it. The old widgets have been deprecated.

# Use `AdwWindow` or `AdwApplicationWindow` for the Parent Window [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-adaptive-dialogs.html\#use-adwwindow-or-adwapplicationwindow-for-the-parent-window "Permanent link")

To use [`AdwDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Dialog.html), your parent window must be an instance of either
[`AdwWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Window.html) or [`AdwApplicationWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ApplicationWindow.html). You should migrate to these widgets
if you’re still using [`GtkWindow`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Window.html) or [`GtkApplicationWindow`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ApplicationWindow.html), respectively.

Stop using window titlebar, instead, create an [`AdwToolbarView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToolbarView.html) and add the
titlebar to it as a top bar. Set the window child as the toolbar view content.
Set the toolbar view as the [`AdwWindow:content`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Window.content.html) property on the window.

If you have [`GtkSearchBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.SearchBar.html), [`GtkActionBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ActionBar.html) etc in a
[`GtkBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Box.html), move them to the toolbar view as well as top/bottom bars respectively.

Example:

```
<object class="GtkWindow">
  <property name="titlebar">
    <object class="AdwHeaderBar"/>
  </property>
  <property name="child">
    <object class="GtkBox">
      <property name="orientation">vertical</property>
      <child>
        <!-- content -->
      </child>
      <child>
        <object class="GtkActionBar"/>
      </child>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

becomes this:

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwToolbarView">
      <child type="top">
        <object class="AdwHeaderBar"/>
      </child>
      <property name="content">
        <!-- content -->
      </property>
      <child type="bottom">
        <object class="GtkActionBar"/>
      </child>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

# Porting to `AdwDialog` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-adaptive-dialogs.html\#porting-to-adwdialog "Permanent link")

The API of [`AdwDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Dialog.html) is somewhat like a subset of the API of [`AdwWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Window.html).

| `GtkWindow` | `AdwDialog` |
| --- | --- |
| [`GtkWindow:child`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Window.child.html) | [`AdwDialog:child`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Dialog.child.html) |
| [`GtkWindow:title`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Window.title.html) | [`AdwDialog:title`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Dialog.title.html) |
| [`GtkWindow:default-width`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Window.default-width.html) | [`AdwDialog:content-width`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Dialog.content-width.html) |
| [`GtkWindow:default-height`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Window.default-height.html) | [`AdwDialog:content-height`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Dialog.content-height.html) |
| [`GtkWindow:resizable`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Window.resizable.html) | [`AdwDialog:follows-content-size`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Dialog.follows-content-size.html) |
| [`GtkWindow:focus-widget`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Window.focus-widget.html) | [`AdwDialog:focus-widget`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Dialog.focus-widget.html) |
| [`GtkWindow:default-widget`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Window.default-widget.html) | [`AdwDialog:default-widget`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Dialog.default-widget.html) |
| [`gtk_window_close()`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/method.Window.close.html) | [`adw_dialog_close()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Dialog.close.html) |
| [`gtk_window_destroy()`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/method.Window.destroy.html) | [`adw_dialog_force_close()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Dialog.force_close.html) |
| [`gtk_window_present()`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/method.Window.present.html) | [`adw_dialog_present()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Dialog.present.html) |

| `AdwWindow` | `AdwDialog` |
| --- | --- |
| [`AdwWindow:content`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Window.content.html) | [`AdwDialog:child`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Dialog.child.html) |
| [`AdwWindow:current-breakpoint`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Window.current-breakpoint.html) | [`AdwDialog:current-breakpoint`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Dialog.current-breakpoint.html) |
| [`adw_window_add_breakpoint()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Window.add_breakpoint.html) | [`adw_dialog_add_breakpoint()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Dialog.add_breakpoint.html) |

Since these dialogs are within the parent window, they are always destroyed with
parent, so there’s no replacement for [`GtkWindow:destroy-with-parent`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Window.destroy-with-parent.html).

[`GtkWindow`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Window.html) sizing can behave in two ways: when resizable, its size is
controlled with [`GtkWindow:default-width`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Window.default-width.html) and
[`GtkWindow:default-height`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Window.default-height.html). If the content shrinks, the window keeps
the size it had before. If the content grows, the window grows with it. When not
resizable, it follows the content’s size precisely.

While dialogs are not resizable, they can behave in both ways as well. By
default, their size is controlled with [`AdwDialog:content-width`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Dialog.content-width.html) and
[`AdwDialog:content-height`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Dialog.content-height.html), like for resizable windows. Set
[`AdwDialog:follows-content-size`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Dialog.follows-content-size.html) to `FALSE` to follow the content size
precisely, like for non-resizable windows.

Since the dialog size is constrained by the parent window, you may want to
adjust the content sizes. For example, if it had a small default height just so
it doesn’t grow larger than its parent window, that can be increased or removed.

Dialogs are regular widgets, so they can be closed and presented again endlessly
as long as you hold a reference to them. If you were setting the
[`GtkWindow:hide-on-close`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Window.hide-on-close.html) property to `TRUE`, do that instead.

Dialogs are always modal. The [`GtkWindow:transient-for`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Window.transient-for.html) property is
replaced by a parameter in [`adw_dialog_present()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Dialog.present.html).

Tip

The widget passed into `adw_dialog_present()` doesn’t have to be a window.
You can pass any widget within a window to get the same effect as passing
the window itself. This is done both for convenience and to allow for more
flexibility in future.

[`GtkWindow::close-request`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/signal.Window.close-request.html) doesn’t have a direct replacement. When
presented as a bottom sheet, dialogs can be swiped down, and because of that you
have to specify whether the dialog can be closed right now ahead of time.

- If you were using `::close-request` to completely prevent window closing, set
the [`AdwDialog:can-close`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Dialog.can-close.html) property to `FALSE`.
- To have a close confirmation, use the [`AdwDialog::close-attempt`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.Dialog.close-attempt.html) signal.
- [`adw_dialog_force_close()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Dialog.force_close.html) closes the dialog even when `:can-close` is set to
`FALSE`, and can be used to close the dialog after the confirmation.
- If you were using `::close-request` just to track when the window is closed,
use the [`AdwDialog::closed`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.Dialog.closed.html) signal instead.

## Use `AdwHeaderBar` Instead of `GtkHeaderBar` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-adaptive-dialogs.html\#use-adwheaderbar-instead-of-gtkheaderbar "Permanent link")

[`AdwHeaderBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html) will use the dialog’s title and adjust decoration layout to
always include a close button and nothing else. Since [`GtkHeaderBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.HeaderBar.html)
doesn’t do this, the dialog will not behave correctly.

Replace your `GtkHeaderBar` with `AdwHeaderBar`, and
[`GtkHeaderBar:show-title-buttons`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.HeaderBar.show-title-buttons.html) with a combination of
[`AdwHeaderBar:show-start-title-buttons`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.show-start-title-buttons.html) and
[`AdwHeaderBar:show-end-title-buttons`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.show-end-title-buttons.html).

## Remove Close Shortcut [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-adaptive-dialogs.html\#remove-close-shortcut "Permanent link")

`AdwDialog` can be closed by pressing `Esc`. If you were handling that
manually, you can stop doing it.

# Port `AdwAboutWindow` to `AdwAboutDialog` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-adaptive-dialogs.html\#port-adwaboutwindow-to-adwaboutdialog "Permanent link")

[`AdwAboutDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AboutDialog.html) has identical API to [`AdwAboutWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AboutWindow.html), so just replace
the function calls as appropriate - for example, [`adw_about_window_add_link()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.AboutWindow.add_link.html)
with [`adw_about_dialog_add_link()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.AboutDialog.add_link.html) and so on.

# Port `AdwPreferencesWindow` to `AdwPreferencesDialog` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-adaptive-dialogs.html\#port-adwpreferenceswindow-to-adwpreferencesdialog "Permanent link")

[`AdwPreferencesDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesDialog.html) has very similar API to [`AdwPreferencesWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.PreferencesWindow.html),
and only needs a few adjustments.

## Stop Using Deprecated API [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-adaptive-dialogs.html\#stop-using-deprecated-api "Permanent link")

The deprecated subpage API has been removed. Refer to the [breakpoints migration\\
guide](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html#migrate-adwpreferenceswindow-subpages) for
information on how to replace it.

## Adapt to Search Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-adaptive-dialogs.html\#adapt-to-search-changes "Permanent link")

`AdwPreferencesDialog` changes the default of the
[`AdwPreferencesWindow:search-enabled`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.PreferencesWindow.search-enabled.html) property to `FALSE`.

If you want search, make sure to set it to `TRUE` manually, and if you were
disabling it, you can stop doing so.

Otherwise, replace the function calls as appropriate, for example
[`adw_preferences_window_add_toast()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.PreferencesWindow.add_toast.html) with [`adw_preferences_dialog_add_toast()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.PreferencesDialog.add_toast.html)
and so on.

# Port `AdwMessageDialog` to `AdwAlertDialog` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-adaptive-dialogs.html\#port-adwmessagedialog-to-adwalertdialog "Permanent link")

[`AdwAlertDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.AlertDialog.html) has mostly similar API to [`AdwMessageDialog`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.MessageDialog.html).

## Adapt to Constructor Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-adaptive-dialogs.html\#adapt-to-constructor-changes "Permanent link")

[`adw_alert_dialog_new()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/ctor.AlertDialog.new.html) doesn’t accept a parent window anymore, so remove that
parameter. Instead, pass it as a parameter to [`adw_dialog_present()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Dialog.present.html) or
[`adw_alert_dialog_choose()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.AlertDialog.choose.html).

## Adapt to `adw_alert_dialog_choose()` Changes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-adaptive-dialogs.html\#adapt-to-adw_alert_dialog_choose-changes "Permanent link")

Just like [`adw_dialog_present()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Dialog.present.html), [`adw_alert_dialog_choose()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.AlertDialog.choose.html) now takes the
parent widget as a parameter.

Tip

The widget passed into `adw_alert_dialog_choose()` doesn’t have to be a
window. You can pass any widget within a window to get the same effect as
passing the window itself. This is done both for convenience and to allow
for more flexibility in future.

## Stop Using `adw_message_dialog_response()` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-adaptive-dialogs.html\#stop-using-adw_message_dialog_response "Permanent link")

[`adw_message_dialog_response()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.MessageDialog.response.html) has no replacement. Most applications shouldn’t
be using it in the first place, but if you really do, emit the
[`AdwAlertDialog::response`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.AlertDialog.response.html) signal manually instead.

Otherwise, replace the function calls as appropriate, for example
[`adw_message_dialog_add_response()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.MessageDialog.add_response.html) with [`adw_alert_dialog_add_response()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.AlertDialog.add_response.html)
and so on.

## Adapt to Scrolling [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-adaptive-dialogs.html\#adapt-to-scrolling "Permanent link")

`AdwAlertDialog` can scroll its content. If you were setting a
[`GtkScrolledWindow`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ScrolledWindow.html) as [`AdwMessageDialog:extra-child`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.MessageDialog.extra-child.html), you may want
to remove the scrolled window and use its contents directly.

# Adw – 1: Migrating to Breakpoints

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html

#### Migrating to Breakpoints

# Migrating to Breakpoints [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html\#migrating-to-breakpoints "Permanent link")

Libadwaita 1.4 introduces [`AdwBreakpoint`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Breakpoint.html) and new adaptive widgets that can
integrate with it, while deprecating the old widgets.

# Start Using `AdwToolbarView` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html\#start-using-adwtoolbarview "Permanent link")

[`AdwToolbarView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToolbarView.html) is a widget that can be used instead of [`GtkBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Box.html) for
widgets like [`AdwHeaderBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html). It’s required to have the correct header bar
style, especially in sidebars.

Replace your `GtkBox` with `AdwToolbarView` and add your header bar and other
toolbars (e.g. [`GtkSearchBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.SearchBar.html) or [`AdwTabBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabBar.html)) as top bars using
[`adw_toolbar_view_add_top_bar()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.ToolbarView.add_top_bar.html) or `<child type="top">` in a UI file.

If you have any toolbars at the bottom of the window, e.g. [`GtkActionBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ActionBar.html)
or [`AdwViewSwitcherBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcherBar.html), add them using
[`adw_toolbar_view_add_bottom_bar()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.ToolbarView.add_bottom_bar.html) or `<child type="bottom">`.

Finally, use [`AdwToolbarView:content`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ToolbarView.content.html) to set the content widget. Unlike in
`GtkBox`, there’s no need to set [`GtkWidget:vexpand`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Widget.vexpand.html) to `TRUE`, so
that can be removed.

Example:

```
<object class="GtkBox">
  <property name="orientation">vertical</property>
  <child>
    <object class="AdwHeaderBar">
      <!-- ... -->
    </object>
  </child>
  <child>
    <object class="...">
      <property name="vexpand">True</property>
      <!-- ... -->
    </object>
  </child>
</object>
```

Copy

becomes this:

```
<object class="AdwToolbarView">
  <child type="top">
    <object class="AdwHeaderBar">
      <!-- ... -->
    </object>
  </child>
  <property name="content">
    <object class="...">
      <!-- ... -->
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

`AdwToolbarView` defaults to flat header bars, replacing the `.flat` style
class. To use a raised style, set the [`AdwToolbarView:top-bar-style`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ToolbarView.top-bar-style.html)
and/or [`AdwToolbarView:bottom-bar-style`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ToolbarView.bottom-bar-style.html) properties to
[`ADW_TOOLBAR_RAISED`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.ToolbarStyle.html#raised).

Subsequent sections will assume that you’re using `AdwToolbarView`.

# Start Using `AdwWindow` or `AdwApplicationWindow` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html\#start-using-adwwindow-or-adwapplicationwindow "Permanent link")

All of the new adaptive widgets require using breakpoints, which can only be
added into [`AdwWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Window.html) or [`AdwApplicationWindow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ApplicationWindow.html). Alternatively, they can
be added into [`AdwBreakpointBin`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.BreakpointBin.html) when only a specific part of the window
needs to be adaptive.

To migrate from `GtkWindow` to `AdwWindow`, or from `GtkApplicationWindow` to
`AdwApplicationWindow`, put your header bar and window content into an
`AdwToolbarView` and set that as the window’s content.

Example:

```
<object class="GtkWindow">
  <property name="titlebar">
    <!-- titlebar -->
  </property>
  <property name="child">
    <!-- content -->
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

becomes this:

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwToolbarView">
      <child type="top">
        <!-- titlebar -->
      </child>
      <property name="content">
        <!-- content -->
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

Using breakpoints also requires the window to have a minimum size. It can be set
using [`gtk_widget_set_size_request()`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/method.Widget.set_size_request.html), or the
[`GtkWidget:width-request`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Widget.width-request.html) and [`GtkWidget:height-request`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Widget.height-request.html) properties.

`AdwWindow` has a default size: 360×200, which should work well for most use
cases, but if it doesn’t, change it to something else.

The child widget must completely fit into your minimum size. If it doesn’t, then
as soon as you add a breakpoint and resize the window to that size, the contents
will overflow and a warning message will be printed.

When checking if the contents fit, consider translations and text scale factor
changes. Make sure to leave enough space for text labels, and enable ellipsizing
or wrapping if they might not fit.

For [`GtkLabel`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Label.html) this can be done via [`GtkLabel:ellipsize`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Label.ellipsize.html), or
via [`GtkLabel:wrap`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Label.wrap.html) together with [`GtkLabel:wrap-mode`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Label.wrap-mode.html).

For buttons, use [`GtkButton:can-shrink`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Button.can-shrink.html),
[`GtkMenuButton:can-shrink`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.MenuButton.can-shrink.html), [`AdwSplitButton:can-shrink`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.SplitButton.can-shrink.html), or
[`AdwButtonContent:can-shrink`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ButtonContent.can-shrink.html).

Subsequent sections will assume that you’re using `AdwWindow` or
`AdwApplicationWindow`.

# Start using `AdwHeaderBar` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html\#start-using-adwheaderbar "Permanent link")

[`AdwHeaderBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html) provides additional integration with some of the widgets
listed below, compared to [`GtkHeaderBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.HeaderBar.html), and can make them noticeably
easier to use.

```
<object class="GtkHeaderBar">
  <property name="show-title-buttons">False</property>
</object>
```

Copy

Replace your header bar with `AdwHeaderBar`, and
[`GtkHeaderBar:show-title-buttons`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.HeaderBar.show-title-buttons.html) with a combination of
[`AdwHeaderBar:show-start-title-buttons`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.show-start-title-buttons.html) and
[`AdwHeaderBar:show-end-title-buttons`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.show-end-title-buttons.html).

```
<object class="AdwHeaderBar">
  <property name="show-start-title-buttons">False</property>
  <property name="show-end-title-buttons">False</property>
</object>
```

Copy

# Replace `AdwLeaflet` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html\#replace-adwleaflet "Permanent link")

`AdwLeaflet` can be replaced by either [`AdwNavigationView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationView.html) or
[`AdwNavigationSplitView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationSplitView.html), depending on how it’s used.

## Navigation [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html\#navigation "Permanent link")

Leaflets that have their [`AdwLeaflet:can-unfold`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Leaflet.can-unfold.html) property set to `FALSE`
can be replaced using `AdwNavigationView`.

A typical use case with two pages looks as follows:

```
<object class="AdwLeaflet">
  <property name="can-unfold">False</property>
  <property name="can-navigate-back">True</property>
  <child>
    <object class="AdwLeafletPage">
      <property name="name">page-1</property>
      <property name="child">
        <object class="AdwToolbarView">
          <child type="top">
            <object class="GtkHeaderBar">
              <property name="title-widget">
                <object class="AdwWindowTitle">
                  <property name="title" translatable="yes">Page 1</property>
                </object>
              </property>
            </object>
          </child>
          <property name="content">
            <!-- ... -->
          </property>
        </object>
      </property>
    </object>
  </child>
  <child>
    <object class="AdwLeafletPage">
      <property name="name">page-2</property>
      <property name="child">
        <object class="AdwToolbarView">
          <child type="top">
            <object class="GtkHeaderBar">
              <child type="start">
                <object class="GtkButton">
                  <property name="icon-name">go-previous-symbolic</property>
                  <property name="tooltip-text" translatable="yes">Back</property>
                  <signal name="clicked" handler="back_clicked_cb" swapped="yes"/>
                </object>
              </child>
              <property name="title-widget">
                <object class="AdwWindowTitle">
                  <property name="title" translatable="yes">Page 2</property>
                </object>
              </property>
            </object>
          </child>
          <property name="content">
            <!-- ... -->
          </property>
        </object>
      </property>
    </object>
  </child>
</object>
```

Copy

Replace the leaflet with `AdwNavigationView` and `AdwLeafletPage` with
[`AdwNavigationPage`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationPage.html). `AdwNavigationView` requires all children to be
`AdwNavigationPage`, so if you didn’t explicitly specify `AdwLeafletPage`,
wrap your child widgets into `AdwNavigationPage` instead.

Use [`AdwNavigationPage:title`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationPage.title.html) instead of manually adding titles to your
header bars. Even if you need a subtitle, [`AdwNavigationPage:title`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationPage.title.html) should
always be set to something meaningful, as it will be used as a tooltip for the
back button and label in its context menu, as well as read out by the screen reader.

Replace [`AdwLeafletPage:name`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.LeafletPage.name.html) with [`AdwNavigationPage:tag`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationPage.tag.html) and
remove the back button as [`AdwHeaderBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html) already provides one. If back
buttons are unwanted, set [`AdwHeaderBar:show-back-button`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.show-back-button.html) on your header
bar to `FALSE`.

`AdwNavigationView` always has back gestures and shortcuts enabled. To disable
them (as well as the back button) on a specific page, set its
[`AdwNavigationPage:can-pop`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationPage.can-pop.html) property to `FALSE`.

If you’re using [`GtkHeaderBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.HeaderBar.html), replace it with `AdwHeaderBar` as well:

```
<object class="AdwNavigationView">
  <child>
    <object class="AdwNavigationPage">
      <property name="title" translatable="yes">Page 1</property>
      <property name="tag">page-1</property>
      <property name="child">
        <object class="AdwToolbarView">
          <child type="top">
            <object class="AdwHeaderBar"/>
          </child>
          <property name="content">
            <!-- ... -->
          </property>
        </object>
      </property>
    </object>
  </child>
  <child>
    <object class="AdwNavigationPage">
      <property name="title" translatable="yes">Page 2</property>
      <property name="tag">page-2</property>
      <property name="child">
        <object class="AdwToolbarView">
          <child type="top">
            <object class="AdwHeaderBar"/>
          </child>
          <property name="content">
            <!-- ... -->
          </property>
        </object>
      </property>
    </object>
  </child>
</object>
```

Copy

Replace [`adw_leaflet_navigate()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.Leaflet.navigate.html) calls with
[`adw_navigation_view_push()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.NavigationView.push.html) for [`ADW_NAVIGATION_DIRECTION_FORWARD`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.NavigationDirection.html#forward) and
[`adw_navigation_view_pop()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.NavigationView.pop.html) for [`ADW_NAVIGATION_DIRECTION_BACK`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.NavigationDirection.html#back). It’s also
possible to push a page using the `navigation.push` action and the page’s tag as
parameter, or pop the visible page using the `navigation.pop` action.

If you were using nested `AdwLeaflet`s or [`GtkStack`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Stack.html) with pages inside it
to arrange a non-linear navigation structure (for example, page 1 that can lead
to page 2 and page 3, both of which lead back to page 1), `AdwNavigationView`
can support that directly.

To replace [`AdwLeaflet:can-navigate-forward`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Leaflet.can-navigate-forward.html), connect to the
[`AdwNavigationView::get-next-page`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/signal.NavigationView.get-next-page.html) signal.

Leaflets that implement adaptive sidebar layouts can be replaced with
[`AdwNavigationSplitView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationSplitView.html).

A typical use case looks as follows:

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwLeaflet" id="leaflet">
      <property name="can-navigate-back">True</property>
      <child>
        <object class="AdwToolbarView">
          <child type="top">
            <object class="AdwHeaderBar">
              <property name="show-end-title-buttons"
                              bind-object="leaflet"
                              bind-property="folded"
                              bind-flags="sync-create"/>
              <property name="title-widget">
                <object class="AdwWindowTitle">
                  <property name="title" translatable="yes">Sidebar</property>
                </object>
              </property>
            </object>
          </child>
          <property name="content">
            <!-- sidebar -->
          </property>
        </object>
      </child>
      <child>
        <object class="AdwLeafletPage">
          <property name="navigatable">False</property>
          <property name="child">
            <object class="GtkSeparator"/>
          </property>
        </object>
      </child>
      <child>
        <object class="AdwToolbarView">
          <property name="hexpand">True</property>
          <child type="top">
            <object class="AdwHeaderBar">
              <property name="show-start-title-buttons"
                              bind-object="leaflet"
                              bind-property="folded"
                              bind-flags="sync-create"/>
              <child type="start">
                <object class="GtkButton">
                  <property name="visible"
                                  bind-object="leaflet"
                                  bind-property="folded"
                                  bind-flags="sync-create"/>
                  <property name="icon-name">go-previous-symbolic</property>
                </object>
              </child>
              <property name="title-widget">
                <object class="AdwWindowTitle">
                  <property name="title" translatable="yes">Content</property>
                </object>
              </property>
            </object>
          </child>
          <property name="content">
            <!-- content -->
          </property>
        </object>
      </child>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

Replace `AdwLeaflet` with `AdwNavigationSplitView` and `AdwLeafletPage` with
[`AdwNavigationPage`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationPage.html). `AdwNavigationSplitView` requires all children to be
`AdwNavigationPage`, so if you didn’t explicitly specify `AdwLeafletPage`,
wrap your child widgets into `AdwNavigationPage` instead.

Remove the separator child, `AdwNavigationSplitView` provides a separator as
part of its styling.

Stop binding window button visibility to the leaflet’s folded state, as
`AdwHeaderBar` handles that automatically when inside `AdwNavigationSplitView`.

Use [`AdwNavigationPage:title`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationPage.title.html) instead of manually adding titles to your
header bars. Even if you need a subtitle, [`AdwNavigationPage:title`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationPage.title.html) should
always be set to something meaningful, as it will be used as a tooltip for the
back button, as well as read out by the screen reader.

Replace [`AdwLeafletPage:name`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.LeafletPage.name.html) with [`AdwNavigationPage:tag`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationPage.tag.html) and
remove the back button from your content header bar, as [`AdwHeaderBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html)
already provides one. If back buttons are unwanted, set
[`AdwHeaderBar:show-back-button`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.show-back-button.html) on your header bar to `FALSE`.

It’s also possible to disable the back button, as well as related shortcuts and
actions on the content page by setting its [`AdwNavigationPage:can-pop`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationPage.can-pop.html)
property to `FALSE`.

Add a breakpoint with a `max-width` condition to your window. To accommodate
the Large Text setting, the width value should be using `sp` unit, e.g. `400sp`.
Add a setter to your breakpoint, setting the
[`AdwNavigationSplitView:collapsed`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationSplitView.collapsed.html) property to `TRUE`.

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <child>
    <object class="AdwBreakpoint">
      <condition>max-width: 400sp</condition>
      <setter object="split_view" property="collapsed">True</setter>
    </object>
  </child>
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwNavigationSplitView" id="split_view">
      <property name="sidebar">
        <object class="AdwNavigationPage">
          <property name="title" translatable="yes">Sidebar</property>
          <property name="child">
            <object class="AdwToolbarView">
              <child type="top">
                <object class="AdwHeaderBar"/>
              </child>
              <property name="content">
                <!-- sidebar -->
              </property>
            </object>
          </property>
        </object>
      </property>
      <property name="content">
        <object class="AdwNavigationPage">
          <property name="title" translatable="yes">Content</property>
          <property name="child">
            <object class="AdwToolbarView">
              <child type="top">
                <object class="AdwHeaderBar"/>
              </child>
              <property name="content">
                <!-- content -->
              </property>
            </object>
          </property>
        </object>
      </property>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

Replace [`AdwLeaflet:visible-child`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Leaflet.visible-child.html) and/or
[`AdwLeaflet:visible-child-name`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Leaflet.visible-child-name.html) uses with
[`AdwNavigationSplitView:show-content`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationSplitView.show-content.html). It’s also
possible to show content using using the `navigation.push` action with the
content page’s tag as a parameter, or show sidebar using the `navigation.pop`
action.

By default, `AdwNavigationSplitView` will dynamically resize the sidebar
depending on its own width. If that behavior is unwanted, set
[`AdwNavigationSplitView:min-sidebar-width`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationSplitView.min-sidebar-width.html) and
[`AdwNavigationSplitView:max-sidebar-width`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationSplitView.max-sidebar-width.html) to 0.

For triple-pane layouts, see [the adaptive layouts page](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-layouts.html#triple-pane-layouts).

## Other Uses [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html\#other-uses "Permanent link")

Other uses of `AdwLeaflet,` e.g. in vertical orientation, have no direct
replacement, but can be replicated using e.g. [`GtkBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Box.html), the
[`GtkWidget:visible`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Widget.visible.html) property and breakpoints.

# Replace `AdwFlap` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html\#replace-adwflap "Permanent link")

`AdwFlap` can be used for multiple different things, and is generally replaced
with [`AdwOverlaySplitView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.OverlaySplitView.html). That widget has similar API to `AdwFlap` and its
common uses can be directly replaced.

## Utility pane [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html\#utility-pane "Permanent link")

The main `AdwFlap` use case is
[utility panes](https://developer.gnome.org/hig/patterns/containers/utility-panes.html).

A common case looks as follows:

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwToolbarView">
      <property name="top-bar-style">raised</property>
      <child type="top">
        <object class="AdwHeaderBar">
          <object class="GtkToggleButton" id="toggle_pane_button">
            <property name="icon-name">sidebar-show-symbolic</property>
            <property name="active">True</property>
          </object>
        </object>
      </child>
      <property name="content">
        <object class="AdwFlap">
          <property name="reveal-flap"
                    bind-source="toggle_pane_button"
                    bind-property="active"
                    bind-flags="sync-create|bidirectional"/>
          <property name="flap">
            <!-- utility pane -->
          </property>
          <property name="separator">
            <object class="GtkSeparator"/>
          </property>
          <property name="content">
            <!-- main view -->
          </property>
        </object>

      </property>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

Replace `AdwFlap` with `AdwOverlaySplitView`, the `flap` property with
[`AdwOverlaySplitView:sidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.OverlaySplitView.sidebar.html) and the `reveal-flap` property with
[`AdwOverlaySplitView:show-sidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.OverlaySplitView.show-sidebar.html).

Remove the separator child, `AdwOverlaySplitView` provides a separator as part
of its styling.

Add an ID to your split view if you’re using UI files.

Add a breakpoint with a `max-width` condition to your window. To accommodate
the Large Text setting, the width value should be using `sp` unit, e.g. `400sp`.
Add a setter to your breakpoint, setting the
[`AdwOverlaySplitView:collapsed`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.OverlaySplitView.collapsed.html) property to `TRUE`.

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <child>
    <object class="AdwBreakpoint">
      <condition>max-width: 400sp</condition>
      <setter object="split_view" property="collapsed">True</setter>
    </object>
  </child>
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwToolbarView">
      <property name="top-bar-style">raised</property>
      <child type="top">
        <object class="AdwHeaderBar">
          <object class="GtkToggleButton" id="toggle_pane_button">
            <property name="icon-name">sidebar-show-symbolic</property>
            <property name="active">True</property>
          </object>
        </object>
      </child>
      <property name="content">
        <object class="AdwOverlaySplitView" id="split_view">
          <property name="show-sidebar"
                    bind-source="toggle_pane_button"
                    bind-property="active"
                    bind-flags="sync-create|bidirectional"/>
          <property name="sidebar">
            <!-- utility pane -->
          </property>
          <property name="content">
            <!-- main view -->
          </property>
        </object>

      </property>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

The [`AdwFlap:locked`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Flap.locked.html) property can be replaced with
[`AdwOverlaySplitView:pin-sidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.OverlaySplitView.pin-sidebar.html).

## Sidebar [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html\#sidebar_1 "Permanent link")

Sidebar-style `AdwFlap` use cases, with split header bars, are handled similarly
to utility panes. One additional difference is that, like in
`AdwNavigationSplitView`, `AdwHeaderBar` can manage window button visibility
automatically when using `AdwOverlaySplitView`, so there’s no need to bind their
visibility to the [`AdwFlap:folded`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.Flap.folded.html) property anymore.

While `AdwOverlaySplitView` doesn’t require using [`AdwNavigationPage`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationPage.html), it can
still be used to provide header bar titles instead of using [`AdwWindowTitle`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.WindowTitle.html).

## Bottom Sheet [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html\#bottom-sheet "Permanent link")

A vertical `AdwFlap` can be used as a bottom sheet-like widget. It can be
replaced with [`AdwBottomSheet`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.BottomSheet.html).

## Fullscreen Header Bar [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html\#fullscreen-header-bar "Permanent link")

A vertical `AdwFlap` can also be used to handle header bars in fullscreen,
specifically for either overlaying a header bar above content in fullscreen,
or showing it next to the content otherwise.

This can be replaced with [`AdwToolbarView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToolbarView.html) and the
[`AdwToolbarView:extend-content-to-top-edge`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ToolbarView.extend-content-to-top-edge.html) property.

## Other Uses [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html\#other-uses_1 "Permanent link")

Other use cases of `AdwFlap` have no direct replacement but can be replicated
using e.g. [`GtkBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Box.html), [`GtkRevealer`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Revealer.html), the
[`GtkWidget:visible`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Widget.visible.html) property, and breakpoints.

# Replace `AdwViewSwitcherTitle` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html\#replace-adwviewswitchertitle "Permanent link")

`AdwViewSwitcherTitle` can be replaced by using [`AdwViewSwitcher`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcher.html) together
with a breakpoint.

A typical `AdwViewSwitcherTitle` use looks as follows:

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <property name="content">
    <object class="AdwToolbarView">
      <child type="top">
        <object class="AdwHeaderBar">
          <property name="centering-policy">strict</property>
          <property name="title-widget">
            <object class="AdwViewSwitcherTitle" id="title">
              <property name="stack">stack</property>
              <property name="title" translatable="yes">Title</property>
            </object>
          </property>
        </object>
      </child>
      <property name="content">
        <object class="AdwViewStack" id="stack">
          <!-- ... -->
        </object>
      </property>
      <child type="bottom">
        <object class="AdwViewSwitcherBar">
          <property name="stack">stack</property>
          <property name="reveal"
                    bind-source="title"
                    bind-property="title-visible"
                    bind-flags="sync-create"/>
        </object>
      </child>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

Replace your `AdwViewSwitcherTitle` with a regular [`AdwViewSwitcher`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ViewSwitcher.html) and set
the [`ADW_VIEW_SWITCHER_POLICY_WIDE`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.ViewSwitcherPolicy.html#wide) policy on it.

Also remove the [`AdwViewSwitcherBar:reveal`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ViewSwitcherBar.reveal.html) property binding on your
switcher bar, and stop setting [`AdwHeaderBar:centering-policy`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.centering-policy.html) on your
header bar.

Add an ID to your header bar and switcher bar if you’re using UI files.

```
<object class="AdwHeaderBar" id="header_bar">
  <!-- ... -->
  <property name="title-widget">
    <object class="AdwViewSwitcher">
      <property name="policy">wide</property>
      <property name="stack">stack</property>
    </object>
  </property>
  <!-- ... -->
</object>
<!-- ... -->
<object class="AdwViewSwitcherBar" id="switcher_bar">
  <property name="stack">stack</property>
</object>
```

Copy

Add a breakpoint with a `max-width` condition to your window. To accommodate
the Large Text setting, the width value should be using `sp` unit.

Recommended width values depending on the number of pages:

- 2 pages: 400sp
- 3 pages: 450sp
- 4 pages: 550sp

You may need to tweak the value to match your application’s layout. It needs to
be large enough that the view switcher is not yet ellipsized at that width, but
small enough that the view switcher doesn’t move to the bottom yet at common
window sizes.

The rest of this section will assume 550sp as the threshold.

Add two setters to your breakpoint, unsetting the header bar’s titlebar widget,
and setting the switcher bar’s `reveal` property to `TRUE`.

Specify the header bar’s title using [`GtkWindow:title`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Window.title.html) or
[`AdwNavigationPage:title`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationPage.title.html).

```
<object class="AdwWindow">
  <property name="title" translatable="yes">Title</property>
  <child>
    <object class="AdwBreakpoint">
      <condition>max-width: 550sp</condition>
      <setter object="header_bar" property="title-widget"/>
      <setter object="switcher_bar" property="reveal">True</setter>
    </object>
  </child>
  <property name="child">
    <object class="AdwToolbarView">
      <child type="top">
        <object class="AdwHeaderBar" id="header_bar">
          <property name="title-widget">
            <object class="AdwViewSwitcher">
              <property name="policy">wide</property>
              <property name="stack">stack</property>
            </object>
          </property>
        </object>
      </child>
      <property name="content">
        <object class="AdwViewStack" id="stack">
          <!-- ... -->
        </object>
      </property>
      <child type="bottom">
        <object class="AdwViewSwitcherBar" id="switcher_bar">
          <property name="stack">stack</property>
        </object>
      </child>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

Copy

## Subtitle [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html\#subtitle "Permanent link")

If you were using [`AdwViewSwitcherTitle:subtitle`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.ViewSwitcherTitle.subtitle.html), use a [`GtkStack`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Stack.html)
containing an `AdwViewSwitcher` and [`AdwWindowTitle`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.WindowTitle.html), and switch the stack’s

```
<object class="AdwWindow">

      <condition>max-width: 550sp</condition>

      <setter object="switcher_bar" property="reveal">True</setter>
    </object>
  </child>

    <object class="AdwToolbarView">
      <child type="top">
        <object class="AdwHeaderBar">
          <property name="title-widget">
            <object class="GtkStack" id="title_stack">
              <child>
                <object class="AdwViewSwitcher">
                  <property name="policy">wide</property>
                  <property name="stack">stack</property>
                </object>
              </child>
              <child>
                <object class="AdwWindowTitle" id="window_title">
                  <property name="title" translatable="yes">Title</property>
                  <property name="subtitle" translatable="yes">Subtitle</property>
                </object>
              </child>
            </object>
          </property>
        </object>
      </child>
      <property name="content">
        <object class="AdwViewStack" id="stack">
          <!-- ... -->
        </object>
      </property>
      <child type="bottom">
        <object class="AdwViewSwitcherBar" id="switcher_bar">
          <property name="stack">stack</property>
        </object>
      </child>
    </object>
  </property>
</object>
```

# Migrate `AdwPreferencesWindow` Subpages [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html\#migrate-adwpreferenceswindow-subpages "Permanent link")

`AdwPreferencesWindow` can now use `AdwNavigationView` for its subpages instead
of `AdwLeaflet`. As such, [`adw_preferences_window_present_subpage()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.PreferencesWindow.present_subpage.html) and
[`adw_preferences_window_close_subpage()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.PreferencesWindow.close_subpage.html) have been deprecated in favor of
[`adw_preferences_window_push_subpage()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.PreferencesWindow.push_subpage.html) and
[`adw_preferences_window_pop_subpage()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.PreferencesWindow.pop_subpage.html).

Wrap your subpages into [`AdwNavigationPage`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.NavigationPage.html), stop setting the header bar
titles manually and use [`AdwNavigationPage:title`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationPage.title.html) instead, remove your
back buttons if you had any. If back buttons are unwanted, set
[`AdwHeaderBar:show-back-button`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.HeaderBar.show-back-button.html) on your header bar to `FALSE`.

`AdwPreferencesWindow` always has back gestures and shortcuts enabled for the
new subpage API. To disable them (as well as the back button) on a specific
page, set its [`AdwNavigationPage:can-pop`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.NavigationPage.can-pop.html) property to `FALSE`.

Unlike [`adw_preferences_window_present_subpage()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.PreferencesWindow.present_subpage.html), repeatedly calling
[`adw_preferences_window_push_subpage()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/method.PreferencesWindow.push_subpage.html) with different pages won’t replace the
current page, so if you had an [`AdwLeaflet`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Leaflet.html) inside your subpage, you can use
`adw_preferences_window_push_subpage()` directly instead.

# Adw.SpringParams

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/struct.SpringParams.html

\[−\]

#### Description  [\[src\]](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libadwaita/-/blob/main/src/adw-spring-params.c\#L16 "go to source location")

```
struct AdwSpringParams {
  /* No available fields */
}
```

Physical parameters of a spring for [`AdwSpringAnimation`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SpringAnimation.html).

Any spring can be described by three parameters: mass, stiffness and damping.

An undamped spring will produce an oscillatory motion which will go on forever.

The frequency and amplitude of the oscillations will be determined by the
stiffness (how “strong” the spring is) and its mass (how much “inertia” it has).

If damping is larger than 0, the amplitude of that oscillating motion will
exponientally decrease over time. If that damping is strong enough that the
spring can’t complete a full oscillation, it’s called an overdamped spring.

If we the spring can oscillate, it’s called an underdamped spring.

The value between these two behaviors is called critical damping; a
critically damped spring will comes to rest in the minimum possible time
without producing oscillations.

The damping can be replaced by damping ratio, which produces the following springs:

- 0: an undamped spring.
- Between 0 and 1: an underdamped spring.
- 1: a critically damped spring.
- Larger than 1: an overdamped spring.

As such.

\[−\]
