# Adw – 1: Style Classes

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html

#### Style Classes

# Style Classes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#style-classes "Permanent link")

The Adwaita stylesheet provides a number of style classes. They can be applied
to widgets to change their appearance.

# Buttons [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#buttons "Permanent link")

The following style classes can be applied to [`GtkButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Button.html) to change its appearance.

## Suggested Action [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#suggested-action "Permanent link")

![buttons-suggested-action](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/buttons-suggested-action.png)

![button-row-suggested-action](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/button-row-suggested-action.png)

The `.suggested-action` style class makes the button use accent colors. It can
be used to denote important buttons, for example, the affirmative button in an
action dialog.

It can be used in combination with [`.circular`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#circular) or [`.pill`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#pill).

Can also be used with [`GtkMenuButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.MenuButton.html), [`AdwSplitButton`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SplitButton.html) or
[`AdwButtonRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ButtonRow.html).

## Destructive Action [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#destructive-action "Permanent link")

![buttons-destructive-action](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/buttons-destructive-action.png)

![button-row-destructive-action](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/button-row-destructive-action.png)

The `.destructive-action` style class makes the button use destructive colors.
It can be used to draw attention to the potentially damaging consequences of
using a button. This style acts as a warning to the user.

It can be used in combination with [`.flat`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#flat), [`.circular`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#circular),
or [`.pill`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#pill).

Can also be used with [`GtkMenuButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.MenuButton.html), [`AdwSplitButton`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SplitButton.html) or
[`AdwButtonRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ButtonRow.html).

## Flat [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#flat "Permanent link")

![buttons-flat](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/buttons-flat.png)

The `.flat` style class makes the button use flat appearance, looking like a
label or an icon until hovered.

Button inside [toolbars and similar widgets](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#toolbars) appear flat by default.

It can be used in combination with [`.circular`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#circular) or [`.pill`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#pill).

Can also be used with [`GtkMenuButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.MenuButton.html), [`AdwSplitButton`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SplitButton.html) or
[`GtkDropDown`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.DropDown.html).

Can be set via [`GtkButton:has-frame`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Button.has-frame.html) and
[`GtkMenuButton:has-frame`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.MenuButton.has-frame.html).

## Raised [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#raised "Permanent link")

![buttons-raised](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/buttons-raised.png)

The `.raised` style class makes the button use the regular appearance instead of
the flat one.

This style class is only useful inside [toolbars and similar widgets](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#toolbars).

It can be used in combination with [`.circular`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#circular) or [`.pill`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#pill).

Can also be used with [`GtkMenuButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.MenuButton.html), [`AdwSplitButton`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SplitButton.html) or
[`GtkDropDown`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.DropDown.html).

## Circular [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#circular "Permanent link")

![buttons-circular](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/buttons-circular.png)

The `.circular` style class makes the button round. It can be used with buttons
containing icons or short labels (1-2 characters).

It can be used in combination with [`.suggested-action`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#suggested-action),
[`.destructive-action`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#destructive-action), [`.flat`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#flat),
[`.raised`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#raised), [`.opaque`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#opaque) or [`.osd`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#overlay-buttons).

Can also be used with [`GtkMenuButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.MenuButton.html).

## Pill [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#pill "Permanent link")

![buttons-pill](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/buttons-pill.png)

The `.pill` style class makes the button appear as a pill. It’s often used for
important standalone buttons, for example, inside a [`AdwStatusPage`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.StatusPage.html).

It can be used in combination with [`.suggested-action`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#suggested-action),
[`.destructive-action`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#destructive-action), [`.flat`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#flat),
[`.raised`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#raised), [`.opaque`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#opaque) or [`.osd`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#overlay-buttons).

# Toggle Groups [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#toggle-groups "Permanent link")

The following style classes can be applied to [`AdwToggleGroup`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToggleGroup.html) or
[`AdwInlineViewSwitcher`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.InlineViewSwitcher.html) to change its appearance.

## Flat [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#flat_1 "Permanent link")

![toggle-group-flat](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/toggle-group-flat.png)

The `.flat` style class makes the group look like a series of flat buttons.

It can be used in combination with [`.round`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#round).

## Round [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#round "Permanent link")

![toggle-group-round](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/toggle-group-round.png)

The `.round` style class makes the group, as well as toggles inside it rounded.

It can be used in combination with [`.flat`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#flat_1).

# Linked Controls [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#linked-controls "Permanent link")

![linked-controls](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/linked-controls.png)

The `.linked` style class can be applied to a [`GtkBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Box.html) to make its
children appear as a single group. The box must have no spacing.

Linked boxes can be both horizontal and vertical.

The following widgets can be linked:

- [`GtkButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Button.html)
- [`GtkMenuButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.MenuButton.html)
- [`GtkDropDown`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.DropDown.html)
- [`GtkColorDialogButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ColorDialogButton.html)
- [`GtkFontDialogButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.FontDialogButton.html)
- [`AdwTabButton`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabButton.html)
- [`GtkEntry`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Entry.html)
- [`GtkPasswordEntry`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.PasswordEntry.html)
- [`GtkSearchEntry`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.SearchEntry.html)
- [`GtkSpinButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.SpinButton.html)

Linked styles will not work correctly for buttons with the following style classes:

- [`.flat`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#flat)
- [`.suggested-action`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#suggested-action)
- [`.opaque`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#opaque)

If a linked box is contained within a [toolbar or a similar widget](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#toolbars),
buttons inside it won’t get the flat appearance.

# Toolbars [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#toolbars "Permanent link")

![toolbar](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/toolbar.png)

The `.toolbar` style class can be applied to a horizontal [`GtkBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Box.html). The
same appearance is also used by [`AdwHeaderBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html), [`GtkHeaderBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.HeaderBar.html),
[`GtkActionBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ActionBar.html) and [`GtkSearchBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.SearchBar.html) automatically.

It changes the appearance of buttons inside it to make them flat when possible,
according to the following rules:

The following buttons get flat appearance:

![toolbar-flat](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/toolbar-flat.png)

- Icon-only buttons;
- Buttons with an icon and a label (using [`AdwButtonContent`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ButtonContent.html));
- Menu buttons containing an arrow;
- [`AdwSplitButton`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SplitButton.html);
- [`GtkDropDown`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.DropDown.html);
- Any other button with the [`.flat`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#flat) style class.

The following buttons keep default appearance:

![toolbar-raised](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/toolbar-raised.png)

- Text-only buttons;
- Buttons with other content;
- Buttons within widgets with the [`.linked`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#linked-controls) style class;
- Buttons with the [`.suggested-action`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#suggested-action) or
[`.opaque`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#opaque) style classes;
- Buttons with the [`.destructive-action`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#destructive-action)
style class;
- Buttons with the [`.raised`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#raised) style class;
- [`GtkDropDown`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.DropDown.html) with the [`.raised`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#raised) style class.

It also ensures 6px margins and spacing between widgets. The
[`.spacer`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#spacers) style class can be useful to separate groups of widgets.

Important

The [`GtkButton:has-frame`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Button.has-frame.html) property will **not** be set to `FALSE`
when a button gets the flat appearance automatically. It also cannot be set
to `TRUE` to make a button raised, the style class should be used directly instead.

# Spacers [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#spacers "Permanent link")

![toolbar-spacer](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/toolbar-spacer.png)

The `.spacer` style class can be applied to a [`GtkSeparator`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Separator.html) to make it
appear invisible and act as whitespace. This can be useful with [toolbars and\\
similar widgets](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#toolbars) to separate groups of widgets from each other.

# Dimmed [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#dimmed "Permanent link")

![dimmed](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/dimmed.png)

The `.dimmed` style class make the widget it’s applied to partially transparent.

The opacity changes between regular and high contrast styles and is represented
by the [`--dim-opacity`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#opacity) variable. Use that variable
if the style class cannot be used directly.

Since: 1.7

# Typography [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#typography "Permanent link")

These style classes can be applied to any widgets, but are mostly used for
[`GtkLabel`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Label.html) or other widgets that contain them.

## Titles [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#titles "Permanent link")

![typography-titles](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/typography-titles.png)

The `.title-1`, `.title-2`, `.title-3`, `.title-4` classes provide four levels
of title styles, indicating hierarchy. The specific use heavily depends on
context. Generally, the larger styles are intended to be used in bigger views
with plenty of whitespace around them.

## Heading [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#heading "Permanent link")

![typography-heading](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/typography-heading.png)

The `.heading` style class is the standard style for UI headings using the
default text size, such as window titles or boxed list labels.

## Document [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#document "Permanent link")

![typography-document](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/typography-document.png)

The `.document` style class makes the widget use the
[document font](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#document-font). This increases the font size
and line height to help make large amounts of text more readable. It should be
used for the app’s main content, such as messages in a chat app. For other long
text, use `.body` instead.

Since: 1.8

## Body [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#body "Permanent link")

![typography-body](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/typography-body.png)

The `.body` style class increases line height to make text more readable. It
should be used for text within the UI, such as descriptions or dialog body, to
make it more legible. For the main content, use `.document` instead.

Avoid using `.body` for non-wrapping text.

## Captions [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#captions "Permanent link")

![typography-captions](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/typography-captions.png)

The `.caption-heading` and `.caption` style classes make text smaller. They
are intended to be used to differentiate sub-text which accompanies text in
the regular body style.

## Monospace [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#monospace "Permanent link")

![typography-monospace](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/typography-monospace.png)

The `.monospace` style class makes the widget use the
[monospace font](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#monospace-font). This can be useful when
displaying code, logs or shell commands.

For [`AdwEntryRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.EntryRow.html), it only makes the editable part monospace, but not title
or any extra widgets. To make everything in the row monospace, apply
`.monospace` to the [`GtkListBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListBox.html) around the row.

## Numeric [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#numeric "Permanent link")

![typography-numeric](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/typography-numeric.png)

The `.numeric` style class makes the widget use tabular figures. This is
equivalent to using [`PangoAttrFontFeatures`](https://docs.gtk.org/Pango/struct.AttrFontFeatures.html) with `"tnum=1"` features.
This style is useful in situations where multiple labels are vertically aligned,
or when displaying time, an operation progress or another number that can
quickly change.

# Colors [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#colors "Permanent link")

![style-colors](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-colors.png)

The following style classes change widget colors:

| Class | Color |
| --- | --- |
| `.accent` | [accent color](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#accent-colors) |
| `.success` | [success color](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#success-colors) |
| `.warning` | [warning color](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#warning-colors) |
| `.error` | [error color](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#error-colors) |

They can be applied to any widget.

The `.error`, `.warning`, `.success` style classes also change the widget’s
accent color to the respective color. They can also be applied to
[`GtkEntry`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Entry.html). In that case, they can be used to indicate input validation state.

# Boxed Lists & Cards [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#boxed-lists-cards "Permanent link")

![boxed-lists](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/boxed-lists.png)

The `.boxed-list` style class can be applied to a [`GtkListBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListBox.html) to make it
a [boxed list](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/boxed-lists.html). The list box should have
[`GtkListBox:selection-mode`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.ListBox.selection-mode.html) set to [`GTK_SELECTION_NONE`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.SelectionMode.html#none).

![boxed-lists-separate](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/boxed-lists-separate.png)

The `.boxed-list-separate` style class is similar to `.boxed-list`, but presents
each row as a separate card instead of the whole list being a single card with
separators. The list box should have [`GtkListBox:selection-mode`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.ListBox.selection-mode.html) set
to [`GTK_SELECTION_NONE`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/enum.SelectionMode.html#none).

![cards](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/cards.png)

The `.card` style class can be applied to any other widget to give it a similar appearance.

If a widget with the `.card` style class also has the `.activatable` style
class, it will also have hover and active states similar to an activatable row
inside a boxed list.

If the `.card` style class is applied to a [`GtkButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Button.html), it will get these
states automatically, without needing the `.activatable` class.

# Sidebars [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#sidebars "Permanent link")

![navigation-sidebar](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/navigation-sidebar.png)

The `.navigation-sidebar` style class can be applied to a [`GtkListBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListBox.html)
or [`GtkListView`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListView.html), as well as [`GtkFlowBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.FlowBox.html) and
[`GtkGridView`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.GridView.html), to make it look like a sidebar: it makes the items rounded
and padded, makes selected items use neutral color instead of accent, and
removes the default list background.

# App Icons [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#app-icons "Permanent link")

![app-icons](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/app-icons.png)

GNOME application icons require a shadow to be legible on a light background.
The `.icon-dropshadow` and `.lowres-icon` style classes provide it when used
with [`GtkImage`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Image.html) or any other widget that contains an image.

`.lowres-icon` should be used for 32×32 or smaller icons, and `.icon-dropshadow`
should be used otherwise.

# Selection Mode Check Buttons [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#selection-mode-check-buttons "Permanent link")

![selection-mode-checks](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/selection-mode-checks.png)

The `.selection-mode` style class can be added to a [`GtkCheckButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.CheckButton.html) to
give it a larger and round appearance. These check buttons are intended to be
used for selecting items from a list or a grid.

# OSD [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#osd "Permanent link")

![osd](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/osd.png)

The `.osd` style class has a number of loosely related purposes depending on
what widget it’s applied to.

Usually, it makes the widget background dark and partially transparent, and
makes its accent color white.

However, it has different effects in a few specific cases.

## Overlay Buttons [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#overlay-buttons "Permanent link")

![osd-buttons](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/osd-buttons.png)

When used with [`GtkButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Button.html), `.osd` can be used to create large standalone
buttons that overlap content, for example, the previous/next page arrows in an
image viewer. They appear dark and slightly larger than regular buttons.

It can be used in combination with [`.circular`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#circular) or [`.pill`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#pill).

## Floating Toolbars [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#floating-toolbars "Permanent link")

![osd-toolbar](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/osd-toolbar.png)

When used along with the [`.toolbar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#toolbars) style class, `.osd` gives the
box additional padding and round corners. This can be used to create floating
toolbars, such as video player controls.

## Progress Bars [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#progress-bars "Permanent link")

![osd-progress-bar](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/osd-progress-bar.png)

When used with [`GtkProgressBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ProgressBar.html), `.osd` makes the progress bar thinner
and removes its visible trough.

OSD progress bars are intended to be used as [`GtkOverlay`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Overlay.html) children,
attached to the top of the window.

# Background [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#background "Permanent link")

![style-background](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-background.png)

The `.background` style class can be used with any widget to give it the default
[window](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#window-colors) background and foreground colors.

This can be useful when a widget needs an opaque background.

It’s equivalent to using the following CSS:

```
.background {
  background-color: var(--window-bg-color);
  color: var(--window-fg-color);
}
```

Copy

# View [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#view "Permanent link")

![style-view](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-view.png)

The `.view` style class can be used with any widget to give it the default
[view](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#window-colors) background and foreground colors.

It’s equivalent to using the following CSS:

```
.view {
  background-color: var(--view-bg-color);
  color: var(--view-fg-color);
}
```

Copy

# Frame [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#frame "Permanent link")

![style-frame](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-frame.png)

The `.frame` style class can be used with any widget to give it the default border.

It’s equivalent to using the following CSS:

```
.frame {
  border: 1px solid var(--border-color);
}
```

Copy

# Compact Status Page [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#compact-status-page "Permanent link")

![status-page-compact](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/status-page-compact.png)

The `.compact` style class can be used with a [`AdwStatusPage`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.StatusPage.html) to make it take
less space. This is usually used with sidebars or popovers.

# Menu Popovers [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#menu-popovers "Permanent link")

![popover-menu-list](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/popover-menu-list.png)

The `.menu` style class can be used with a [`GtkPopover`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Popover.html) to give it a
menu-like appearance if it has a [`GtkListBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListBox.html) or a [`GtkListView`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListView.html)
inside it.

# Development Window [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#development-window "Permanent link")

![devel-window](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/devel-window.png)

The `.devel` style class can be used with [`GtkWindow`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Window.html). This will give
any [`AdwHeaderBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html) or [`GtkHeaderBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.HeaderBar.html) inside that window a striped appearance.

This style class is typically used to indicate unstable or nightly applications.

# Inline [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#inline "Permanent link")

![search-bar-inline](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/search-bar-inline.png)

![tab-bar-inline](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/tab-bar-inline.png)

The `.inline` style class can be used with [`GtkSearchBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.SearchBar.html), [`AdwTabBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.TabBar.html)
or [`GtkTextView`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.TextView.html).

By default `GtkSearchBar` and `AdwTabBar` look like a part of an `AdwHeaderBar`
and are intended to be used directly attached to one or used as
[`AdwToolbarView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToolbarView.html) toolbars. With the `.inline` style class they have neutral
backgrounds and can be used in different contexts instead.

When used with `GtkTextView`, it allows it to e.g. be put into a card while
following its styles.

Note

The `.inline` style class cannot be used with `GtkSourceView`.

# Undershoot Indicators [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#undershoot-indicators "Permanent link")

![undershoot](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/undershoot.png)

The `.undershoot-top`, `.undershoot-bottom`, `.undershoot-start` and
`.undershoot-end` style classes can be used with [`GtkScrolledWindow`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ScrolledWindow.html) to
add an undershoot indicator on the given edge, presented as a shadow.

`.undershoot-start` and `.undershoot-end` automatically follow text direction,
same as [`GtkWidget:margin-start`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Widget.margin-start.html) and [`GtkWidget:margin-end`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/property.Widget.margin-end.html).

Most applications should use [`AdwToolbarView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToolbarView.html) instead, as it manages
undershoots automatically based on presence and visibility of top and bottom bars.

Since: 1.4

# Property Rows [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#property-rows "Permanent link")

![property-row](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property-row.png)

The `.property` style class can be used with [`AdwActionRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ActionRow.html) and
[`AdwExpanderRow`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ExpanderRow.html). It deemphasizes the row title and emphasizes subtitle
instead, which is useful for displaying read-only properties, as follows:

```
<object class="AdwActionRow">
  <property name="title" translatable="yes">Property Name</property>
  <property name="subtitle">Value</property>
  <property name="subtitle-selectable">True</property>
  <style>
    <class name="property"/>
  </style>
</object>
```

Copy

Since: 1.4

The `.monospace` style class with `.property` only makes the subtitle monospace,
but not the title or any extra widgets. To make everything in the row monospace,
apply `.monospace` to the [`GtkListBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListBox.html) around the row.

Since: 1.6

# Deprecated Style Classes [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#deprecated-style-classes "Permanent link")

The following style classes are deprecated and remain there for compatibility.
They shouldn’t be used in new code.

## `.content` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#content "Permanent link")

![boxed-lists](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/boxed-lists.png)

The `.content` style class can be applied to a [`GtkListBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListBox.html) to give it a
boxed list appearance. The [`.boxed-list`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#boxed-lists-cards) style class is
completely equivalent to it and should be used instead.

![deprecated-sidebar](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/deprecated-sidebar.png)

The `.sidebar` style class adds a border at the end of the widget (`border-right`
for left-to-right text direction, `border-left` for right-to-left) and removes
background from any [`GtkListBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListBox.html) or [`GtkListView`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.ListView.html) inside it.

It can be replaced by using the [`.navigation-sidebar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#sidebars) style class
on the list widget, combined with a [`GtkSeparator`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Separator.html) to achieve the border.

## `.app-notification` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#app-notification "Permanent link")

![deprecated-app-notification](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/deprecated-app-notification.png)

The `.app-notification` style class is used with widgets like [`GtkBox`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Box.html).
It adds [`.osd`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#osd) appearance to the widget and makes its bottom corners
round. When used together with a [`GtkOverlay`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Overlay.html) and a [`GtkRevealer`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Revealer.html),
it allows creating in-app notifications.

[`AdwToastOverlay`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToastOverlay.html) can be used to replace it.

## `.large-title` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#large-title "Permanent link")

![typography-large-title](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/typography-large-title.png)

The `.large-title` style class makes text large and thin. It’s the largest
style, infrequently used for display headings in greeters or assistants. It
should only be used in conjunction with large amounts of whitespace.

The [`.title-1`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#titles) style class should be used instead.

Deprecated since: 1.2

## Flat Header Bar [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#flat-header-bar "Permanent link")

![flat-header-bar](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/flat-header-bar.png)

The `.flat` style class can be used with an [`AdwHeaderBar`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.HeaderBar.html) or
[`GtkHeaderBar`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.HeaderBar.html) to give it a flat appearance.

Use [`AdwToolbarView`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.ToolbarView.html) instead.

Deprecated since: 1.4

## `.opaque` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#opaque "Permanent link")

![buttons-opaque](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/buttons-opaque.png)

The `.opaque` style class gives the button an opaque background. It’s intended
to be used together with custom styles that override `background-color` and
`color`, to create buttons with an appearance similar to
[`.suggested-action`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#suggested-action), but with custom colors.

For example, `.suggested-action` is equivalent to using the `.opaque` style
using the `.opaque` style
class with the following CSS:

```
#custom-suggested-action-button {
  background-color: var(--accent-bg-color);
  color: var(--accent-fg-color);
}
```

Copy

It can be used in combination with [`.circular`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#circular) or [`.pill`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#pill).

Can also be used with [`GtkMenuButton`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.MenuButton.html) or [`AdwSplitButton`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.SplitButton.html).

Use [`.suggested-action`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#suggested-action) instead, and override the accent
color, for example:

```
#custom-destructive-action-button {
  --accent-bg-color: var(--destructive-bg-color);
  --accent-fg-color: var(--destructive-fg-color);
  --accent-color: var(--destructive-color);
}
```

Copy

Deprecated since: 1.6

## `.dim-label` [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html\#dim-label "Permanent link")

![dim-label](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/dimmed.png)

The `.dim-label` style class makes the widget it’s applied to partially transparent.

The opacity changes between regular and high contrast styles and is represented
by the [`--dim-opacity`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#opacity) variable. Use that variable
if the style class cannot be used directly.

The [`.dimmed`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#dimmed) style class is completely equivalent to it and should
be used instead.

Deprecated since: 1.7

# Adw – 1: Styles & Appearance

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/styles-and-appearance.html

#### Styles & Appearance

# Styles & Appearance [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/styles-and-appearance.html\#styles-appearance "Permanent link")

## Dark Style [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/styles-and-appearance.html\#dark-style "Permanent link")

Libadwaita applications can use a light or a dark appearance. This can be used
to request a darker UI, or to support a system-wide dark style preference if one exists.

By default, applications use light appearance unless the system prefers dark
appearance, matching the [`ADW_COLOR_SCHEME_PREFER_LIGHT`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.ColorScheme.html#prefer-light) color scheme. The
[`AdwStyleManager:color-scheme`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.StyleManager.color-scheme.html) property allows to change this behavior
when set to:

- [`ADW_COLOR_SCHEME_PREFER_DARK`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.ColorScheme.html#prefer-dark): Use dark appearance unless the system prefers
light appearance.
- [`ADW_COLOR_SCHEME_FORCE_DARK`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.ColorScheme.html#force-dark): Always use dark appearance.
- [`ADW_COLOR_SCHEME_FORCE_LIGHT`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.ColorScheme.html#force-light): Always use light appearance.

| App \ System | Prefer Light | No Preference | Prefer Dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FORCE_LIGHT` | Light | Light | Light |
| `PREFER_LIGHT` | Light | Light | Dark |
| `PREFER_DARK` | Light | Dark | Dark |
| `FORCE_DARK` | Dark | Dark | Dark |

Common use cases:

1. An application wants to use dark UI. Use the [`ADW_COLOR_SCHEME_PREFER_DARK`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.ColorScheme.html#prefer-dark)
    color scheme.

2. An application has a style switcher with the system, light and
dark states. Use the following color scheme values:
   - System: [`ADW_COLOR_SCHEME_PREFER_LIGHT`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.ColorScheme.html#prefer-light)
   - Light: [`ADW_COLOR_SCHEME_FORCE_LIGHT`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.ColorScheme.html#force-light)
   - Dark: [`ADW_COLOR_SCHEME_FORCE_DARK`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/enum.ColorScheme.html#force-dark)

If the system does not provide a style preference, the
[`AdwStyleManager:system-supports-color-schemes`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.StyleManager.system-supports-color-schemes.html) property can be used to
provide a fallback. For example, applications with a system/light/dark switcher
may want to hide or disable the system value.

All standard GTK and Libadwaita widgets automatically support both styles.
Applications that use custom drawing or styles may need to ensure the UI
remains legible in both appearances:

- When possible, use [CSS variables](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html) instead of hardcoded
colors. For custom drawing, use [`gtk_style_context_get_color()`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/method.StyleContext.get_color.html) to get the
current text color for your widget, or [`gtk_style_context_lookup_color()`](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/method.StyleContext.lookup_color.html)
to look up other colors.

- If that’s not possible, use the [`AdwStyleManager:dark`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.StyleManager.dark.html) property to check
the current appearance and vary the drawing accordingly.

- The `prefers-color-scheme: dark`CSS media query can be used to add custom
styles specific to dark appearance.

- Alternatively, [`AdwApplication`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Application.html) allows loading additional styles for dark
appearance via the `style-dark.css` resource.


## Accent Color [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/styles-and-appearance.html\#accent-color "Permanent link")

Libadwaita applications follow the system accent color by default. Applications
with custom drawing or styles may need to ensure that they use the actual accent
color instead of hardcoding blue:

- Use [accent color variables](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#accent-colors) and the
[`.accent`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#colors) style class in CSS.

- Use [`AdwStyleManager:accent-color-rgba`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.StyleManager.accent-color-rgba.html) to get the background accent
color programmatically.

- Use [`AdwStyleManager:accent-color`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.StyleManager.accent-color.html) and
[`adw_accent_color_to_standalone_rgba()`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/type_func.AccentColor.to_standalone_rgba.html) to get the standalone accent color programmatically.


Applications can override the accent color using CSS, as follows:

```
:root {
  --accent-bg-color: var(--accent-green); /* Always use the green color */
}
```

Copy

Accent can also be overridden for an individual widget. In this case
`--accent-color` must be manually overridden as well:

```
my-widget {
  --accent-bg-color: var(--accent-purple); /* Always use the purple color */
  --accent-color: oklab(from var(--accent-bg-color) var(--standalone-color-oklab));
}
```

Copy

All of the default accent colors use white text as the foreground color. If the
custom accent color is too bright, use a dark foreground color instead:

```
:root {
  --accent-bg-color: var(--yellow-3);
  --accent-fg-color: rgb(0 0 0 / 80%);
}
```

Copy

Note

When accent color is overridden, [`AdwStyleManager`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.StyleManager.html) API will still return
the system color.

## High Contrast [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/styles-and-appearance.html\#high-contrast "Permanent link")

The system can provide a high contrast preference. Libadwaita applications
automatically support it; applications cannot disable it.

High contrast appearance can be combined with the [dark style](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/styles-and-appearance.html#dark-style) and
is independent from it.

All standard GTK and Libadwaita widgets automatically support the high contrast
appearance. Applications that use custom drawing or styles may need to support
it manually.

- Use style classes such as [`.dimmed`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html#dimmed) instead
of changing widget opacity manually.

- Use the [helper variables](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html#helpers) when possible, instead
of hardcoding colors and opacities.

- The [`AdwStyleManager:high-contrast`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/property.StyleManager.high-contrast.html) property can be used to check the
current appearance.

- The `prefers-contrast: more`CSS media query can be used to add custom styles
specific to high contrast.

- Alternatively, [`AdwApplication`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Application.html) allows loading additional styles for high
contrast appearance via the `style-hc.css` and `style-hc-dark.css` resources.


## Custom Styles [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/styles-and-appearance.html\#custom-styles "Permanent link")

[`AdwApplication`](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/class.Application.html) provides a simple way to load additional styles from a
resource named `style.css`, relative to the application’s base path (see
[`g_application_set_resource_base_path()`](https://docs.gtk.org/gio/method.Application.set_resource_base_path.html)).

To add styles conditionally only for certain color schemes or high contrast, use
the following media queries:

- `prefers-color-scheme: dark` for styles used only for dark appearance.
- `prefers-contrast: more` for styles used only when the system high contrast
preference is enabled.

# Controls [Permanent link](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/widget-gallery.html\#controls "Permanent link")
